summary: World-action models adapt pretrained video generators, and vision-language-action models build on pretrained vision-language backbones; both tie policy architecture and inference cost to large transformers designed for generation rather than control. It remains unclear how much these generation-oriented choices affect control. In this work, we introduce Latent Action JEPA (La-JEPA), a compact world-action model whose policy transformer is trained from scratch in the feature space of a pretrained V-JEPA 2.1 encoder. Following Fast-WAM, La-JEPA learns to predict future features jointly with actions during training and generates only actions at inference. Among policies without embodied pretraining, La-JEPA achieves state-of-the-art performance in clean and randomized RoboTwin 2.0 scenes and on LIBERO-Plus with correct instructions, while using far fewer parameters than the strongest competing policies. It runs substantially faster than Fast-WAM at comparable performance and outperforms the closest JEPA-based methods, LeapBot-WA and JEPA-WAM, on LIBERO-Plus and RoboTwin 2.0 without their pretrained policy backbones. On four real-robot tasks, its average success is comparable to pi0.5 and above non-embodied-pretrained baselines. Through a design study of the choices behind La-JEPA, we show that JEPA features outperform video VAE latents, most clearly out of distribution, and that training-time future prediction choices significantly impact the policy even when future prediction is skipped at inference. We correct the LIBERO-Plus instructions, as the officially released evaluator corrupts them for most variants, and re-evaluate several strong open baselines. Without a generative pretrained policy backbone, La-JEPA is better and faster than far larger policies, suggesting that robot foundation models may benefit from architectures designed for control rather than inherited from generation.
title: La-JEPA: Compact Robot Policies with Latent World Modeling

summary: In large-scale payment networks, entities (card, merchant, etc.) and their interactions play a key role in transaction anomaly detection. However, transaction patterns between different entities usually change more frequently than the production model refresh schedule. Meanwhile, entity embedding tables suffer from high-cardinality and sparse interaction issues. summary: Tensor network kernel machines (TNKMs) combine nonlinear features with low-rank tensor representations to model complex relationships efficiently. However, selecting an appropriate tensor rank remains challenging, as conventional rank-search methods require training multiple candidate models, increasing computational costs. In this work, we focus on a canonical polyadic (CP) tensor network parameterization and propose GB-CPKM, a gradient boosting framework that builds a higher-capacity predictor by sequentially adding fixed-rank learners. This approach provides a new perspective on rank selection by incrementally increasing model capacity, with ensemble size selected based on validation performance rather than through explicit rank search. Experiments on real-world regression benchmarks show that GB-CPKM trains up to 6x faster and uses up to 2x less peak memory than a conventional rank-selection method based on cross-validation, while achieving comparable predictive performance. These results highlight the potential of gradient boosting to improve the computational efficiency and scalability of tensor-network learning.
title: Gradient Boosting for Efficient Rank Discovery in Tensor Network Kernel Machines

summary: Real-time voice agents need a speech recognizer that never waits for future audio and whose memory per call does not grow with the length of the call. We present E-Gaborformer, a strictly causal encoder that combines Gated DeltaNet-2 recurrent layers with sliding-window attention in a 3:1 ratio, and builds every temporal convolution from a fixed dictionary of causal Gabor atoms. Its streaming state is constant, about 19 MB per call at production scale including the prediction network, where a causal-attention encoder of the same size accumulates over 1 GB after ten minutes. In a controlled causal study on LibriSpeech, E-Gaborformer leaves the initial plateau earlier, reaches a given accuracy up to 18% sooner, and matches or beats an E-Branchformer trained with the identical front end and recipe. At production scale, a 0.6B-parameter Hebrew and English streaming transducer built on E-Gaborformer has 28 to 31% lower word error rate (WER) than NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 ASR Streaming, a model of the same size, on English voice-agent traffic, and up to 20% lower Hebrew WER than our previous production system. The same weights serve strictly causal and 480 ms-lookahead decoding with no loss in accuracy, and a two-class formulation of the RNN-T lattice trains the transducer 2.6x faster with exact loss and gradients.
title: Gabor Gabor: E-Gaborformer, a Strictly Causal Speech Recognizer with Gabor-Dictionary Convolutions and Delta-Rule Memory

summary: Efficient deployment of large language models (LLMs) on mobile devices requires balancing performance with compute and memory constraints. Post-training compression is an effective approach to managing this trade-off, while requiring much less computation than in-training counterparts. We propose DictLLM, a dictionary-based compression scheme in which weight matrices within grouped layers are decomposed into a shared dictionary and layer-specific sparse coefficients, directly obtained from a pre-trained model without further training. Specifically, we cast DictLLM as a four-step post-training optimization. First, we obtain shared dictionaries via singular value decomposition (SVD) of input-scaled weight matrices, amortizing rank across grouped layers; second, we sparsify the layer-specific coefficients to the target compression ratio using a dictionary-aware Hessian; and third, we refine the dictionaries given the resulting sparse coefficients. Finally, we aggressively quantize both components using factor-specific Hessian information: input covariance for the dictionaries and the dictionary-aware Hessian for the coefficients. The resulting representation reduces memory footprint by storing a single shared dictionary per layer group, along with sparse layer-specific coefficients. On language modeling and zero-shot reasoning benchmarks, DictLLM consistently outperforms existing post-training low-rank compression methods and pushes the Pareto frontier between model size and performance. DictLLM compresses the original LLaMA-7B model by 5.1x with only a 2.9-point increase in WikiText-2 perplexity, achieving a 3.6x higher compression ratio than the state-of-the-art low-rank method.
title: DictLLM: Post-training Compression of Large Language Model with Dictionary Kernels

summary: To interpret a direction in a language model's residual stream, we can look for text that strongly activates it. But when such text is found by scanning a corpus, it is limited to what that corpus contains. We develop Maximally-Activating Example Metamodels (MAEMs), language models which map residual stream directions from a subject model to text exemplars that strongly activate those directions. Our objective is to maximise the cosine similarity of a supplied residual stream direction with the activations of the text generated by the MAEM. This label-free RL objective helps to scale MAEMs on diverse sources of residual stream directions. Empirically, we find the resultant metamodel produces informative exemplars: a Qwen3.6-27B MAEM inverts held-out activations better than corpus search or a natural-language autoencoder (NLA), beats corpus search (at 10M tokens) on a majority of held-out languages/domains, and activates 89% of held-out SAE features. It also identifies concepts behind steering vectors about as well as NLAs, recovers the payloads of LoRA backdoors more often than corpus search, and can even verbalise some model workspace inner monologue. Unlike explanations produced by other metamodels (e.g. NLAs), MAEM exemplars can be verified with a forward pass on the subject model, making the MAEM objective a grounded alternative for scaling the training of metamodels.
title: Towards interpreting any residual stream direction by scaling activation inversion

summary: The goal of this paper is to investigate the following question: what geometric restrictions does the existence of a transitive family of constant mean curvature hyperspheres impose on a Riemannian metric on $\mathbb S^n$? The notion of a transitive family can be made precise through the theory of Zoll families developed by Ambrozio, Marques, and Neves. Within this framework, we partially extend their local rigidity theorem for even conformal factors on $\mathbb S^3$ to every dimension $n\ge4$, assuming each hypersphere in the minimal Zoll family has the area of a round equator. Moreover, we give a partial answer to the following higher-dimensional version of a question posed by Robert Bryant: must a metric on $\mathbb S^n$, conformal to the round metric and admitting a Zoll family of hyperspheres with a common nonzero constant mean curvature, have constant sectional curvature? Finally, we also investigate inverse problems in the spirit of Hangan, asking which metrics make a fixed family of geodesic spheres have a common prescribed mean curvature.
title: Spheres with transitive families of CMC hypersurfaces

summary: Reconstructing turbulent flow fields from sparse and irregular measurements remains challenging because the underlying inverse problem is severely underdetermined. Here we present MANTRA, a manifold-based tensor framework that represents each velocity component in a continuous tensor-product space while constraining its coefficient tensor to a low-rank Tucker manifold. This structure provides a compact, data-adaptive representation without requiring gridded observations or governing equations. Riemannian optimization and adaptive selection of rank and basis complexity enable the model to exploit coordinate-wise spatiotemporal correlations. In simulations of forced isotropic turbulence and flow over a cylinder, MANTRA recovers multiscale structures at sampling densities orders of magnitude below the underlying grids and remains accurate under Gaussian noise up to 20% of the peak velocity. It also recovers leading coordinate-wise correlation structures from sparse observations. Applied to experimental particle-tracking velocimetry of an oscillating impinging jet, MANTRA reveals time-evolving structures that are not apparent from the scattered measurements alone.
title: Low-Rank Tensor Manifolds for Turbulent Field Reconstruction from Sparse Data

summary: We prove a logarithmic central limit theorem for a tagged particle in infinite-dimensional Dyson Brownian motion at inverse temperature $β=2$, starting from the sine$_2$ point process. The fluctuation is of order $\sqrt{\log t}$, which is subdiffusive and substantially slower than the polynomial fluctuations of classical short-range interacting particle systems, reflecting the rigidity induced by long-range logarithmic repulsion. We further identify the scaling limit as the singular Gaussian field corresponding to the zero-Hurst parameter, which provides a realisation of the singular Gaussian field as a scaling limit of a tagged particle raised by Dürr, Goldstein and Lebowitz (Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 38 (1985)).
title: The singular Gaussian scaling limit for a tagged particle in the infinite-dimensional Dyson model at $β=2$

summary: AI agents store text as embedding vectors and compress them at scale. A compression is accepted when each item's nearest neighbors survive, but agents also consolidate, delete, and compare memories, tasks that depend on which items lie far apart. We evaluate both ends with two label-free fidelities from our prior work: the local fidelity $L$ at 10 neighbors and the global fidelity $G$ at 30 to 50 percent of the memory. At 96 bytes per passage, rescored binary codes reach an $L$ of 0.97 yet move 10.1 percent of passages to another theme; PCA with 8-bit codes, at an $L$ of 0.77, moves 1.7 percent. Rescoring leaves the stored codes, and thus $G$, unchanged. We prove that across the $G$ band, $1-ν_k$ is at most 2 to 2.18 times the square root of the near-far rank-violation rate, and that this rate follows the distance noise of the compression (correlation 0.979). Our locality-aware quantization (LAQ) turns the bound into a hinge objective on the codebooks of an OPQ index, keeping its bytes, rotation, and search. To our knowledge, LAQ is the first quantizer whose objective comes from a proven bound on the far end. Reconstruction alone raises $G$ in 0 of 52 held-out runs; the far hinge raises it in all 52. LAQ raises $G$ in all 52 ($p=8.5\times 10^{-4}$ over 13 memory-encoder groups), including the external FinDER memory, has the highest $G$ of seven equal-size quantizers in all 12 Multi-Doc-2025 runs, scales to a million passages, and keeps evidence recall.
title: Enhancing Local and Global Structure in Compressed AI Agent Memory

summary: Two-phase designs provide a cost-effective framework for biomarker studies and have been widely used to reduce the burden of collecting expensive biomarker measurements. Most methodological research has focused on efficient Phase II sampling and estimation of biomarker--outcome associations. A natural subsequent step, however, is to incorporate identified biomarkers into risk prediction models, where measures of predictive performance become important inferential targets. Even for binary outcomes, methodological developments for two-phase designs that jointly address association parameters and predictive performance remain limited. Building on classical case-control and matched case-control designs developed primarily for association inference with binary outcomes, we propose a risk-matched case-control (RMCC) design that uses a scalar disease-risk score constructed from Phase I variables to define matching strata and guide Phase II sampling. To address the limitations of existing likelihood-based approaches, which typically require correct specification of the nuisance distribution of biomarkers, we develop a unified design-based inference framework based on inverse probability weighting for both association parameters and predictive performance measures, including positive predictive value and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve. We further introduce target-specific weight scaling and calibration procedures and derive variance estimators that account for sampling variability in both phases. Simulation studies demonstrate the efficiency and robustness of the proposed design and inference procedures, and an application to a Taiwanese oral cancer cohort illustrates their potential utility.
title: Risk-matched case-control sampling and semiparametric weight calibration for efficient biomarker assessment with binary outcomes

summary: We study the coherent transfer of circulation between two weakly coupled lattice rings of ultracold bosons, in which a persistent current initially prepared in one ring oscillates back and forth between the rings without net transfer of particles. Combining Bose--Hubbard simulations with their Gross--Pitaevskii and quantum phase model limits, we show that similar current oscillations arise from two distinct microscopic mechanisms. At weak interactions, particles in each occupied momentum mode tunnel independently between the rings, leading to a transfer time inversely proportional to the inter-ring tunnelling, extensive particle-number fluctuations and entanglement distributed over many Schmidt components; this mode-exchange dynamics is suppressed by self-trapping as the interactions increase. At stronger interactions and large filling, in the phase-dominated regime, circulation is instead transferred through a second-order collective process between many-body persistent-current states, with a transfer time scaling as the inverse square of the inter-ring tunnelling in the weak-link limit. Number fluctuations then remain of order one instead of growing with the particle number, and within each number sector the system evolves into coherent superpositions of two many-body configurations, distinguished by which ring carries the circulation. The entanglement accessible under number-conserving operations therefore reaches up to approximately one bit. We propose a quench protocol to prepare the initial state and estimate transfer times within reach of current ring-lattice experiments, identifying coupled rings as a platform to study coherent quantum phase slips and to manipulate persistent-current states.
title: Coherent phase slips in coupled rings: from weak to strong interactions

summary: Semantic communication (SemCom) using a relay node is considered, where the relay assists in conveying task-relevant information from a source to a destination, with meaning defined by classification labels. A joint end-to-end design of the source encoder, relay transformation, and destination decoders is developed to optimize both semantic inference accuracy and perceptual reconstruction quality for image data. Relay-assisted schemes are shown to outperform direct transmission, with gains that become more pronounced in low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) regimes across different relaying strategies. Alongside these performance benefits, however, a key security vulnerability introduced by the relay is identified, and a Byzantine attack is formulated in which the relay injects structured, learned perturbations into its transmitted signal. The attack operates on intermediate communication representations subject to channel effects, with perturbations generated through a learned mapping applied at test time. It is shown to significantly degrade semantic inference accuracy at the destination. These results reveal a clear trade-off between SemCom gains and security risks in relay-assisted systems, motivating the need for secure relay designs that account for insider threats.
title: AI-Native Task-Oriented Semantic Communications over a Relay: Benefits and Vulnerabilities

summary: This work identifies a fundamental, controller-independent limitation in reusable launch vehicle powered descent: a sudden $180^\circ$ phase transition in the open-loop transfer functions from the control inputs to the lateral drift and drift rate. The transition occurs inside the flight envelope, reverses the effective control direction, and can destabilize the closed loop system under uncertainty. An analytical condition governing this transition is derived, its physical mechanism is established, and its dependence on vehicle mass, aerodynamic properties, and geometry is characterized. An Incremental Nonlinear Dynamic Inversion (INDI)-based control architecture is then developed to inherently address this limitation and is tuned via $\mathcal{H}_\infty$ Closed Loop Shaping to provide local robustness and performance guarantees. The internal dynamics introduced by the INDI inversion are analytically derived and proven to be stable throughout the flight envelope. The proposed controller is compared against a robust gain-scheduled baseline controller through linear stability analysis and an extensive nonlinear Monte Carlo campaign. Both controllers achieve 100% success across the considered Monte Carlo campaign, though the INDI-based controller provides improved tracking performance, superior nominal and dispersed stability margins, requires fewer controller design points, and reduces controller tuning complexity.
title: Overcoming Fundamental Control Limitations in Powered Descent Flight through Robust Incremental Nonlinear Dynamic Inversion

summary: Bacterial cellulose biofilms are complex networks of strong interwoven nanofibers that control transport and protect bacterial colonies in the film. Design of diverse applications of bacterial cellulose films also relies on understanding and controlling transport through the fiber mesh, and transport simulations of the films are most accurate when guided by experimental characterization of the structures and the resultant diffusion inside. Diffusion through such films is a function of their key microstructural length scales, determining how molecules, as well as particles and microorganisms, permeate them. We use microscopy to study the unique bacterial cellulose film structure and quantify the mobility dynamics of various sizes of tracer particles and macromolecules. Mobility is hindered within the films, as confinement and local movement strongly depend on void size relative to diffusing tracers. The biofilms have a naturally periodic structure of alternating dense and porous layers of nanofiber mesh, and we tune the magnitude of the spacing via fermentation conditions. Micron-sized particles can diffuse through the porous layers, but can not penetrate the dense layers. Tracer mobility in the porous layers is isotropic, indicating a largely random pore structure there. Molecular diffusion through the whole film is only slightly reduced by the structural tortuosity. Knowledge of transport variations within bacterial cellulose networks can be used to guide design of symbiotic cultures in these structures and enhance their use in applications biomedical implants, wound dressings, lab-grown meat, and sensors.
title: Molecular and colloidal transport in bacterial cellulose hydrogels

summary: Bacterial cellulose is an important class of biomaterials which can be grown in well-controlled laboratory and industrial conditions. The cellulose structure is affected by several biological, chemical and environmental factors, including hydrodynamic flows in bacterial suspensions. In this work, we explore the possibility of using well controlled turbulent flow to control the bacterial cellulose production. Turbulent flows leading to random motion of fluid elements may affect the structure of the extracellular polymeric matrix produced by bacteria. Here we show that two-dimensional turbulence at the air-liquid interface generates chaotic rotation at a well-defined scale and random persistent stretching of the fluid elements. The results offer new approaches to engineering of the bacterial cellulose structure by controlling turbulence parameters.
title: Turbulence-assisted formation of bacterial cellulose

summary: Hydrogels provide a solution-mimicking environment for the interaction with living systems that make them desirable for various biomedical and technological applications. Because relevant biological processes in living tissues occur at the biomolecular scale, hydrogel nanopatterning can be leveraged to attain novel material properties and functionalities. However, the fabrication of high aspect ratio (HAR) nanostructures in hydrogels capable of self-standing in aqueous environments, with fine control of the size and shape distribution, remains challenging. Here, we report the synthesis of nanostructures with a HAR in bacterial cellulose (BC) hydrogel via directed plasma nanosynthesis using argon ions. The nanostructures in BC are reproducible, stable to sterilization, and liquid immersion. Using in-situ surface characterization and semi-empirical modeling, we discovered that pattern formation was linked to the formation of graphite-like clusters composed of a mixture of C-C and C=C bonds. Moreover, our model predicts that reactive species at the onset of the argon irradiation accelerate the bond breaking of weak bonds, contributing to the formation of an amorphous carbon layer and nanopattern growth.
title: Ion-induced nanopatterning of a bacterial cellulose hydrogel

summary: The interparticle interactions in a magnetic nanocomposite play a dominant role in controlling the phase transitions superparamagnetic to superspinglass to superferromagnetic. These interactions can be tuned by controlling the size and number density of nanoparticles. Aerogel composites, 0.3 Ni-BC and 0.7 Ni-BC, consisting of Ni nanoparticles distributed in bacterial cellulose have been used as model systems to study the effect of interparticle interactions with increasing fraction of Ni in the composite. Contrary to conventional approach, the size of Ni nanoparticles is not controlled and was allowed to form naturally in the bacterial cellulose template. The structural characterization using x-ray diffraction and electron microscopies indicates the presence of only Ni and cellulose with no other phases. The uncontrolled growth of Ni in cellulose matrix results in the formation of nanoparticles with 3 different size distributions - 10 nm particles mainly distributed along the length of fibrils, 50 nm particles present in the intermediate spaces between the fibrils and 100 nm particles present in voids formed by the reticulate structure. At room temperature the composites exhibit a weakly ferromagnetic behavior with a coercivity of 40 Oe which increases to 160 Oe at 10 K. The transition from weakly ferromagnetic state at room temperature to a superferromagnetic state at low temperatures is mediated via a superspinglass state at intermediate temperatures. A temperature dependent microstructural model has been developed combining the structural and magnetic results obtained from the two composite aerogels.
title: Interparticle interactions mediated superspinglass to superferromagnetic transition in Ni-bacterial cellulose aerogel nanocomposites

summary: Background: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) are persistent, hydrophobic and in several cases carcinogenic pollutants of soils and sediments. Bacterial degradation of high-molecular-weight PAHs is slow because of their low bioavailability, which has directed attention to ligninolytic fungi that attack pollutants extracellularly. Scope: This narrative review, based exclusively on published secondary data (1983–2024), examines the diversity of ligninolytic fungi, their enzyme systems, the biochemical mechanisms of PAH transformation, the factors that control degradation in soil, and the evidence from pilot- and field-scale applications. Key findings: Lignin peroxidase, manganese peroxidase (including lipid-peroxidation chemistry), versatile peroxidase and laccase–mediator systems oxidise PAHs to quinones and ring-fission products, while cytochrome P450 monooxygenases and unspecific peroxygenases form dihydrodiols and phenols. Fungi mineralise only part of the oxidised carbon, but their polar products are readily mineralised by soil bacteria. Field trials – from US demonstrations with Phanerochaete sordida to tonne-scale Finnish piles inoculated on pine bark and Danish trials with spent oyster-mushroom substrate – confirm that inoculation and colonisation are feasible, but improvements over indigenous microbial activity have been inconsistent and strongly site-dependent, limited by bioavailability, competition and logistics. Conclusion: Ligninolytic fungi are most promising for soils dominated by high-molecular-weight PAHs and as partners in integrated fungal–bacterial treatment. Soil-competent strains, low-cost lignocellulosic carriers, attention to bioavailability and standardised metabolite and toxicity monitoring are required for reliable field deployment.

title: Ligninolytic Fungi in Bioremediation: Mechanism of Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbon (Pah) Degradation and Field Applications

summary: Grant-free uplink access in low-Earth-orbit (LEO) non-terrestrial networks (NTNs) poses a coordination challenge when multiple UEs share a satellite channel without real-time centralized scheduling under long propagation delays and time-varying channels. Conventional random access does not exploit peer context, leading to collisions and inefficient channel use as contention increases. To address this problem, we propose IRIS, a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for decentralized grant-free direct-to-satellite (D2S) uplink access, with A2A-IRIS as its sidelink-assisted Agent-to-Agent (A2A) realization. Each UE executes a shared binary transmission policy using local traffic/channel information augmented by compact peer states exchanged over UE-to-UE sidelink, while Vanilla-IRIS serves as a local-only ablation. Evaluations in rural and suburban LEO D2S deployments use TLE-based trajectories propagated using the Simplified General Perturbations 4 (SGP4), with a Walker-Delta constellation as fallback. A2A-IRIS achieves 2.1579 and 5.4478 Mbps, corresponding to 99.9% and 96.1% of the respective scenario-specific upper bounds. Relative to Vanilla-IRIS, throughput improves by 40.8% and 325.0%, with collision rates of 0.0000 and 0.0433, while one- and two-epoch delayed centralized schedulers are outperformed by approximately 51--130%. A2A-IRIS also improves fairness, service coverage, and transmission efficiency with moderate Deep Q-Network (DQN) inference overhead. Active-UE load scalability results further show sustained performance over the evaluated load range. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of sidelink-assisted A2A coordination for decentralized LEO D2S uplink access under propagation delay and delayed channel feedback.
title: IRIS: Intelligent Random Access with Integrated Shared Learning for Decentralized LEO Direct-to-Satellite Uplinks

title: IRIS: Intelligent Random Access with Integrated Shared Learning for Decentralized LEO Direct-to-Satellite Uplinks

summary: Multi-agent LLM systems explore in parallel by spawning sub-agents with isolated context windows, whereas single-agent systems append every search and verification step into one growing trajectory. However, existing multi-agent frameworks duplicate prefix KV caches across branches, exchange findings by re-prefilling text summaries, and flatten or drop cross-branch dependencies during reinforcement learning (RL). We introduce Octopus, a single-model multi-agent RL framework in which all threads share one backbone and coordinate over a GPU-resident directed acyclic graph (DAG) of KV states through five primitives (fork, read_thread, wait_threads, rewind, commit). Octopus combines three co-designed mechanisms: (1) Zero-Copy Radix Forking, which spawns branches as $\mathcal{O}(1)$ cursor views over shared physical KV pages; (2) Attention-Only KV Mounting, which mounts a sibling thread's terminal KV blocks directly into full-attention layers while bypassing linear-recurrent states (Gated DeltaNet / Mamba-2), cutting off-task hijacking by $21\times$ ($57.9\% \to 2.7\%$) while retaining $92.2\%$ of full-text mutual information at zero extra KV allocation; and (3) a Packed DAG-GRPO Trainer, which packs all episode branches into one block-sparse attention pass and assigns counterfactual branch credit via leave-one-branch-out marginal rewards. Trained end-to-end with GRPO on Qwen3.5-4B over a sparse BM25 corpus, Octopus reaches $49.6\%$ accuracy on BrowseComp-Plus ($+17.5$ points over single-agent GRPO at 143K context and $+12.5$ points over text-summary multi-agent RL) and $51.2\%$ on OpenResearcher, outperforming dense-retrieval agents up to $250\times$ larger while increasing training throughput $3.3\times$ and cutting peak KV memory $2.8\times$.

summary: Wellbore stability analysis is an essential part of well planning where mechanical characteristics of rocks and the state of in-situ stresses are determined to evaluate the likelihood of borehole failure during drilling. In this study, natural and drilling induced fractures were characterized using image logs for a fractured reservoir located in Southern Iran. Mechanical Earth Modeling (MEM) and wellbore stability analysis were also carried out by the combination of wireline log data and in-situ measurements for a vertical well drilled in this field. The obtained results indicated the presence of several major/minor fractures in the studied interval but majority of them were found to be closed fractures. According to the MEM, formations would suffer from breakout (shear failure) in several intervals which might be linked to their low strengths, huge stress anisotropy and inappropriate selection of the mud weight. Give then fact that the break-out failure obtained from the Mogi-Coulomb criterion had a match with the borehole failure captured by the caliper log, the geomechanical parameters estimated through the methodology proposed should have sufficient accuracy and can be used for the stability analysis of other wells drilled in the same field.
title: Natural fracture characterization and wellbore stability analysis of a highly fractured southwestern Iranian oilfield

summary: Thermal Quantum Annealing (tQuA) is a quantum architecture in which a system coupled non-adiabatically to a thermodynamic reservoir evolves toward the ground state of a target Hamiltonian . This paper provides a rigorous and honest foundation for tQuA and its extension to Quantum Intelligent Matrix Methods (QIMM). We distinguish carefully among Theorems (proved in cited literature), Propositions (proof sketches with explicitly identified gaps), and Conjectures (claims with open steps). This work delivers three principal contributions: Convergence Proof Chain: We present a five-pillar proof chain establishing that tQuA converges to the global minimum from any initial state, without adiabatic scheduling, without eigenstate knowledge, and with a strictly positive escape rate from every local minimum at any . Honest Scaling Benchmarks: We present scaling benchmarks for the Liouvillian spectral gap   on gopherhole Hamiltonians, reporting a key finding: fixed-schedule tQuA achieves a perfectly flat gap ( , independent of   up to ) when the number of local minima   is fixed and small, but experiences steep polynomial decay ( ) when   grows proportionally to . Adaptive Policy Framework: Third, we outline a rich adaptive annealing policy framework using observed function evaluations and prior probability distributions   over problem classes, framing it as a primary research direction for future empirical tuning.   The framework applies broadly to nonconvex optimization in artificial intelligence, signal processing, and imaging, with specific application to "seeing the sky" technologies described in the companion paper on intensity-correlation interferometry (Hyland & Werbos 2024).

summary: This record contains the data and Stata code used in the article "Bonding without bridging: Social capital, business organisation and the late Industrial Revolution in the Ottoman Empire, c. 1740–1880". data/table1_maddison2020.csv – population, GDP per capita and GDP for eight economies, c. 1740–1840 (Maddison Project Database 2020). data/table2_vdem_v16.csv – armed conflict, rule of law, corruption and freedom of association, 1789–1840 (V-Dem v16). data/table3_britain_ottoman_c1740.csv – values and sources for the comparison of Great Britain and the Ottoman Empire, c. 1740. data/panel_5yr_1789_1913.csv – five-year panel of 34 countries, 1789–1913, used for the cross-country estimates (Table 4). data/panel_cs_series.csv – civil society index series used for Figure 3. code/ottoman_panel_step1.do to step4.do – Stata 19.5 do-files that build the panel from the V-Dem Country-Year Dataset v16 and reproduce the diagnostics (Pesaran CD, CIPS, Westerlund), the Mundlak and Driscoll–Kraay estimates, the first-difference and CCE models, and Figure 3. The original V-Dem file (V-Dem-CY-Full+Others-v16.dta) is not redistributed and should be downloaded from https://v-dem.net. See README.txt for variable definitions and the order in which to run the files.

summary: In standard multi-head attention, every head uses the same query, key, and value (QKV) projection matrices for every token. We study a simple variant in which, in every layer, a subset of the heads are token-specific: their QKV projections depend on the identity of the input token, while the remaining heads keep ordinary shared projections. Token-specific projections are parameterized as a shared matrix plus a per-token low-rank correction stored in a hashed lookup table, so the extra computation is small, although the parameter count grows. In GPT-style language models trained on FineWeb, with 2 of 4 heads per layer token-specific, every run had lower validation loss than every standard-attention run, at both of the scales we tested. At the larger of two scales (6 layers, width 512, 300M training tokens, 3 seeds per method), validation loss fell from 4.154 ± 0.005 to 4.107 ± 0.008, a 4.6% reduction in perplexity. A control that adds the same number of lookup-table parameters to the same heads as per-token vectors, rather than per-token matrix corrections, reached only 4.148 ± 0.002, indicating that the gain is not explained by the additional parameters alone. At the smaller scale, a sweep over the number of token-specific heads suggests that mixing token-specific and shared heads works at least as well as making all heads token-specific. The main cost is throughput: our unoptimized implementation trains about 30% slower than the baseline. These are small-scale results, and we discuss their limitations in detail.
title: Token-Specific Attention Heads: Mixing Per-Token and Shared Query, Key, and Value Projections in Transformer Language Models

Token-specific projections are parameterized as a shared matrix plus a per-token low-rank correction stored in a hashed lookup table, so the extra computation is small, although the parameter count grows. In GPT-style language models trained on FineWeb, with 2 of 4 heads per layer token-specific, every run had lower validation loss than every standard-attention run, at both of the scales we tested. At the larger of two scales (6 layers, width 512, 300M training tokens, 3 seeds per method), validation loss fell from 4.154 ± 0.005 to 4.107 ± 0.008, a 4.6% reduction in perplexity. A control that adds the same number of lookup-table parameters to the same heads as per-token vectors, rather than per-token matrix corrections, reached only 4.148 ± 0.002, indicating that the gain is not explained by the additional parameters alone. At the smaller scale, a sweep over the number of token-specific heads suggests that mixing token-specific and shared heads works at least as well as making all heads token-specific. The main cost is throughput: our unoptimized implementation trains about 30% slower than the baseline. These are small-scale results, and we discuss their limitations in detail.

summary: Supplementary data for an experiment that replaced the larva segmentation model of the Tenebrio molitor behavioral-phenotyping pipeline while every downstream step (Petri geometry, primary-larva selection, continuity gate, interpolation, smoothing, features, quality control) was held fixed. Five segmenters were compared: the YOLO11s-seg used for the v1.0.0 dataset, YOLOv8s-seg, YOLO26s-seg and Mask R-CNN R50-FPN v2 trained on full tray images, and a YOLO11s-seg trained on Petri crops. The crop-trained model was then applied to all 34 videos and the Results analysis repeated. On Petri crops, the input the pipeline processes, mask mAP@0.5 was 0.10 for the full-tray YOLO11s and 0.99 for the crop-trained YOLO11s and Mask R-CNN; on 79 held-out labelled video frames larva recall was 0.69, 0.99 and 0.96. The two ground-truth-accurate models agreed with each other (CCC 0.91–0.99 on distance, speed, edge fraction, entropy and area). Heat contrasts kept their direction on the 34 videos. Contents: configuration, protocol and results documents, held-out accuracy, ground-truth localization, the 12-video comparison (agreement, equivalence, per-configuration features and QC), the 34-video re-run with the crop-trained model, treatment contrasts and provenance. Model weights are not included. The values are objective behavioral proxies and do not measure welfare or any subjective state.

summary: Abstract The Laser Cognition (LC) is a proposed multilevel theoretical framework for investigating how selective attention, conscious access, curiosity-guided inquiry, associative recruitment, and representational integration may contribute to the emergence and evaluation of novel ideas. Its central explanatory metaphor is laser illumination: a complex cognitive field contains multiple thoughts, memories, representations, and potential relationships, while a selected cognitive target receives processing priority. The framework uses this metaphor to organize a proposed mechanism linking cognitive-field activation, attentional targeting, awareness-mediated processing, focus regulation, associative recruitment, integrative recombination, candidate generation, and metacognitive evaluation. LC retains the distinction between the full theory, its default mechanism, and its canonical primary case. The primary case is the Laser-Spotlight Cognitive Genesis Case (LSCGC); the proposed default mechanism is the Laser Cognition Default Mechanism (LC-DM); and its principal operational cycle is the Laser-Guided Cognitive Integration Cycle (LGCIC). The framework is formalized using a weighted cognitive graph, a dual-route attentional-targeting model, a normalized attentional-allocation function, a focus-stability measure, an associative-recruitment equation, a cognitive-integration index, a probabilistic candidate-emergence model, and a feedback-control representation. The mathematical expressions constitute proposed model specifications, not established equations of human neural operation. Awareness, attention, curiosity, affective engagement, cognitive flexibility, and metacognitive monitoring are treated as related but conceptually distinct constructs. The architecture includes eighteen layers, a multidomain research structure, eight initial research hypotheses, explicit falsifiability requirements, a cross-system functional generalization framework, a fourteen-step research protocol, and a twenty-part manuscript structure. Human cognition is the primary explanatory domain. Applications to artificial intelligence, large language models, artificial general intelligence, and possible artificial superintelligence are framed as hypotheses about functional or computational correspondence rather than established claims of shared consciousness or identical mechanisms. LC is presented as a theory-development and validation framework. Its explanatory value, novelty, causal assumptions, parameter identifiability, empirical adequacy, and cross-domain applicability remain subject to systematic literature review, mathematical audit, empirical testing, model comparison, and replication.

summary: Language-generating AI systems are no longer only objects of linguistic interaction: their outputs increasingly re-enter the communicative and institutional practices from which their training material was drawn. Drawing on social theory, social epistemology, and the philosophy of language, this article develops a sociotechnical account of that re-entry. We introduce recursive semantic normalization: the process through which machine-generated formulations, once recurrently taken up, evaluated, reused, and institutionally retained, participate in the reproduction and transformation of semantic regularities. Under the heading of technohybridism, we argue that the relevant unit of analysis is the hybrid semantic system, a recursively coupled configuration of human practices, computational generation, and institutional uptake. First, we distinguish the concept from neighbouring accounts, including model collapse, looping effects, machine habitus, machine culture, and the epistemology of AI testimony. Second, we develop an analytical model that separates generation, selection, uptake, and persistence and distinguishes machine-attributable change from change that would have occurred anyway. Third, we analyse uptake as routinized, institutionally diffused, and socially stratified practice and state conditions under which machine-derived regularities become norms. Fourth, we identify social-epistemic consequences: the laundering of provenance that weakens epistemic vigilance, the erosion of the cognitive diversity on which collective inquiry depends, and the narrowing of shared hermeneutical resources. An evidential ladder for empirical research follows. The account attributes no normative authority to machine outputs; what changes is the field within which human and institutional uptake operates.
title: Technohybridism: Recursive Semantic Normalization in AI-Mediated Societies

summary: Keyword retrieval returns expressions of personal anxiety together with many other uses of anxiety-related language. We present a benchmark of 1,000 Arabic Twitter/X posts retrieved with the keyword qalaq ("anxiety/worry") and annotated for six discourse functions. Two native Arabic-speaking annotators labeled every post independently, reaching 51.1% raw agreement (Cohen's $κ= 0.378$). We then reviewed all 489 disagreements and all 511 agreements under the same guidelines. The review changed 120 of the agreed labels (23.5%), which shows that agreements need auditing as well as disagreements. The final labels form a consensus reference; on a random sample of 200 posts, an additional annotator agreed with it on 60.5% of posts ($κ= 0.517$). Against this reference, Fanar-C-2-27B reaches 79.8% accuracy and macro-F1 0.784 ($κ= 0.749$). Its errors concentrate in the residual category (41.1% of errors; precision 0.905, recall 0.447), whose definition is internally inconsistent in the executed prompt, so the low recall cannot be attributed to the model alone. Sociopolitical Anxiety (27.1%) outnumbers Personal Emotional Expression (22.0%); these are assignment proportions in the sample, not estimates of prevalence or retrieval precision. We release the guidelines, a residual-subtype scheme, a fixed data split, label provenance, and evaluation code.
title: Beyond the Keyword: A Human-Annotated Benchmark for Arabic Anxiety-Related Discourse

summary: A no-build, local-first cataloguer for archives that no longer exist: destroyed, damaged, looted, dispersed, and unlocated works recorded with evidence hashes, consent states down to the entry, a register of narrators whose identities never publish, dated sightings, status histories, loss events, typed relations, surviving copies (IIIF), a memorial register, a timeline, an atlas of consented places, CSV import, serverless merge, fixity checks, passphrase encryption of the working file, and self-contained finding-aid and memorial-book exports. Arabic and right-to-left ready.
title: MIRL Lacuna: a catalogue of an absent archive

summary: High-performance geospatial analysis library, CLI and dynamic tile server in Rust: 127 algorithms (56 also available in the browser via WebAssembly), streaming I/O for arbitrarily large DEMs, native CRS reprojection, windowed GeoTIFF and Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF reads (including ZSTD, band-interleaved, bottom-up and BigTIFF files such as the AlphaEarth Foundations embedding tiles), a native ECW decoder, an end-to-end satellite composite pipeline, foundation-model embeddings as first-class rasters (similarity maps, PCA false colour), embedded verifiable provenance in every output with a bit-exact determinism contract, and SurtGIS Server (`surtgis serve`), an analysis-first XYZ tile server with materialisation jobs where terrain operators, spectral formulas and embedding operators are tile-URL parameters. Covers terrain analysis, hydrology and remote sensing from a single dependency-free binary. This record archives the source of release v1.8.0.
title: SurtGIS: a high-performance raster geospatial analysis library, CLI and dynamic tile server in Rust

summary: The Suggested Upper Merged Ontology (SUMO) supplies general categories, relations and axioms for knowledge representation. Its source language, Standard Upper Ontology Knowledge Interchange Format (SUO-KIF), and its reasoning environment, Sigma Knowledge Engineering Environment (KEE), have different roles. Rikishi is a source-bound workbench for inspecting those commitments, submitting selected reasoning problems, and retaining their inputs and evidence. This paper asks how that infrastructure can make a scientific modeling connection inspectable. Prior Active Inference–SUMO alignment provides a direct precedent (Douglass et al., 2024; doi:10.5281/zenodo.11463326). One shared finite witness connects selected ontology expressions to probability models, numerical evaluation, pinned FEP_Formal Lean statements and synthetic observation histories. The ontology lane investigates declared model, representation, calculation and result roles. The mathematical lane supplies finite normalization, conditioning and information identities under stated hypotheses. The computational lane checks numerical outputs and generates trajectories from an explicit persistent-state model. Stable identifiers and common inputs join these lanes without treating their claims as interchangeable. Worked source formulas, direction-sensitive queries, numerical references and formal controls make the connections testable. Exact conditioning is separated from simulated frequencies, and variational inference from action selection and empirical model assessment. The resulting interface supports reproducible inspection of particular examples; it does not establish full-SUMO consistency, a general SUMO-to-Lean interpretation, verification of all Python execution, or biological validity of the Free Energy Principle (FEP).
title: Rikishi: Reproducible operation and analysis of the Suggested Upper Merged Ontology

summary: Rikishi is a source-bound SUMO ontology workbench with controlled automated-theorem-prover campaigns, finite probability calculations, restricted Lean obligations, read-only human and agent interfaces, and a reproducible manuscript pipeline. A separate finite one-step action planner evaluates explicit action-dependent transitions, observation channels and outcome preferences, retaining pragmatic and information-seeking terms. Shared finite witnesses connect model, representation, calculation, and result roles while retaining the separate scope of each observation and proof. Results concern explicitly retained sources, submitted logical kernels, declared finite models, and named formal hypotheses; they do not establish ontology-wide consistency, general SUMO-to-Lean semantic preservation, proof-object authentication, or empirical biological validity. This MIT-licensed software archive is distinct from the separately reviewed manuscript PDF and its record. The original manuscript and figures are licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0); third-party material is excluded from that original-work grant. Third-party sources, tools, and bundled materials retain their own licenses and attribution.
title: Rikishi: Reproducible operation and analysis of the Suggested Upper Merged Ontology

summary: Maintainers sometimes cite a low token-similarity score as evidence that an LLM-assisted rewrite of a copyleft project is independent of the original. We test what such a score can support under \emph{source-conditioned} rewriting: a coding agent keeps the original in its working copy, rewrites the repository, and iterates until a fixed behavioural harness passes, with no human edit to the code. On 69 rewrites of six copyleft Python projects we find that: \ding{182}~Agent-only rewriting is inexpensive and often yields low scores. Every controlled rewrite passes the harness after repair, usually within half an hour for the initial rewrite. Under a ground-up rearchitecture prompt, most rewrites fall below 25\% JPlag similarity and still pass the harness. \ding{183}~A single low score is an unreliable witness. Identical project--agent--prompt configurations produce wide spreads in similarity; run-to-run variation dominates project and agent effects, and in more than a third of configurations the three repeats straddle the threshold. Rewrites retain more of the original's imports and fingerprint facts than unrelated projects do, yet hand-written independent implementations of the same task often retain as much, and neither signal separates the two groups better than chance. Thus a low score on one rewrite is weak evidence of independence: another run of the same agent may score high. Claims based on similarity should report repeated generations, and candidate provenance signals should be checked against same task independent implementations, not only against unrelated projects.
title: A Low Similarity Score Does Not Show Independence after Source-Conditioned Repository Rewriting

It includes the verified arithmetic, elliptic-curve, height, complex-analytic, period-lattice, auxiliary-function, interpolation, and subgroup developments, together with calculation scripts, documentation, verification logs, and provenance records. Compared with the previously described 1,682-theorem snapshot, this adds 637 supporting theorems and 1,429 project declarations. The audits check declaration types, safe logical values, and transitive axioms in Lean’s kernel, including private and generated proof declarations. They record no unfinished proof values, no project axioms, and no additional transitive axioms beyond propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. Incorrectly typed negative controls are rejected. Mathlib dependencies use the pinned compiled cache. Counts include elementary and supporting results, not independent discoveries. The unconditional bounded classification is proved. Any additional solution would therefore require C to have more than 10^119 decimal digits. The rational circle-valued logarithm is injective, and the actual period and three basis logarithms are linearly independent over the integers and rationals. Exact lattice certificates implement the coefficient reduction 1.5 × 10^60 → 44 → 10 → 9 when the initial coefficient maximum satisfies the stated bound. summary: Аннотация . Статья посвящена работе с цифровыми архивами при изучении первых дней Великой Отечественной войны. Рассмотрены возможности порталов «Память народа», ОБД «Мемориал», «Подвиг народа» и коллекций Президентской библиотеки. Показано, почему готовый пересказ, в том числе созданный нейросетью, нельзя ставить на место архивного документа. Предложен простой порядок проверки: найти первичный образ, уточнить происхождение документа, сопоставить его с другими свидетельствами и только после этого формулировать вывод. Такой подход помогает сохранить личное измерение военной истории и снижает риск повторения неточных или вырванных из контекста утверждений. Abstract. The article discusses the use of digital archives in studying the first days of the Great Patriotic War. It examines the resources Memory of the People, Memorial, Feat of the People, and the Presidential Library collections. The paper explains why a ready-made narrative, including an AI-generated one, cannot replace an archival document. A simple verification procedure is proposed: locate the original image, identify the document provenance, compare it with other evidence, and only then formulate a conclusion. This approach preserves the personal dimension of military history and reduces the risk of repeating inaccurate or decontextualized claims.

summary: As "AI Scientists" emerge to drive research via the Model Context Protocol (MCP), systems relying on ephemeral scripts will fail. The sheer scale of stateful, interconnected evidence requires a machine-walkable warranty grounded in a purpose-built database architecture. Eigenius is an open-source, typed knowledge-graph DBMS built on a single premise: answering the audit question ("what do you know, and what is your warranty?") requires a unified kernel. By tightly coupling the type system, storage engine, and integration protocol, Eigenius turns data provenance into a structural invariant rather than a property reconstructed across subsystem boundaries. The kernel rests on three pillars whose metatheory is mechanized in Lean 4: a dependent type theory (EigenTT) separating confluent conversion from ontology subsumption and keeping proof irrelevance axiomatic so distinct warrants remain inspectable; proof-calculus institutions acting as strongly typed integration boundaries; and a content-addressed immutable storage layer. Epistemic status (declared/observed/derived/verified) forms a bounded lattice over a justification logic enforced at commit. Cross-system comorphisms carry explicit axiom policies (Adopt, Discharge, Relativize), transport witnesses at commit, and materialize outputs into the graph, while EigenQL provides a Grothendieck query view across all hosted logics and shared on-chain IRs collapse multi-system translations to identity. Pairing empirical justification logic with an in-process Lean 4 term checker, an end-to-end recomputation of a published Nature study from pinned data discharges all 52 derived conclusions and surfaces four machine-checked discrepancies in the original study.
title: Eigenius: A Typed Knowledge-Graph DBMS with Epistemic Stratification and Institution-Mediated Reasoning

summary: Supplementary data for an experiment that replaced the larva segmentation model of the Tenebrio molitor behavioral-phenotyping pipeline while every downstream step (Petri geometry, primary-larva selection, continuity gate, interpolation, smoothing, features, quality control) was held fixed. Five segmenters were compared: the YOLO11s-seg used for the v1.0.0 dataset, YOLOv8s-seg, YOLO26s-seg and Mask R-CNN R50-FPN v2 trained on full tray images, and a YOLO11s-seg trained on Petri crops. The crop-trained model was then applied to all 34 videos and the Results analysis repeated. On Petri crops, the input the pipeline processes, mask mAP@0.5 was 0.10 for the full-tray YOLO11s and 0.99 for the crop-trained YOLO11s and Mask R-CNN; on 79 held-out labelled video frames larva recall was 0.69, 0.99 and 0.96. The two ground-truth-accurate models agreed with each other (CCC 0.91–0.99 on distance, speed, edge fraction, entropy and area). Heat contrasts kept their direction on the 34 videos. Contents: configuration, protocol and results documents, held-out accuracy, ground-truth localization, the 12-video comparison (agreement, equivalence, per-configuration features and QC), the 34-video re-run with the crop-trained model, treatment contrasts and provenance. Model weights are not included. The values are objective behavioral proxies and do not measure welfare or any subjective state.
title: Tenebrio molitor behavioral phenotyping dataset: segmenter comparison supplementary data

summary: Supplementary data package for the systematic review "Wireless Body Sensor Networks in Sports: A Systematic Review of Technologies, Applications, and Challenges" (80 included studies described in 82 reports, 2016–2026; PRISMA 2020). The package contains the complete data-extraction table (80 studies × 64 deposited fields across seven research questions), the screening register of all 394 records with relevance scores, exclusion reasons and quality appraisals, the literal search strings per database with execution dates and hit counts, the per-study quality judgments, the provenance of the nine prior reviews compared in the article, the SpringerLink post-filter with its per-record decision matrix, including the disposition of every record re-screened in the August 2026 audit, and the completed PRISMA 2020 checklist, which maps each item to the section, table or figure of the article that reports it. A multi-tab workbook compiles every supplementary table together with a codebook of the extraction fields. Every field is in English: column headers, coded values and free text in every table. Extraction and appraisal were carried out in Spanish, and the Spanish originals remain in the authors' working spreadsheet. The extraction template has 65 fields and 64 are deposited: the omitted one holds the reviewer's working annotations rather than data about the studies, and the codebook records both its existence and its absence. This version adds the completed PRISMA 2020 checklist (Table S8), which the article now provides as supplementary material. It also regenerates the per-study quality table from the screening register, in which the five studies admitted in the August 2026 audit had been exported with zero on every criterion; translates the 78 cells that remained in Spanish, including the notes of the search table; corrects two rows of the SpringerLink decision matrix and one extraction error checked against the full text; and defines the cloud-platform field in the codebook.
title: Supplementary materials — Wireless Body Sensor Networks in Sports: A Systematic Review (2016–2026)

summary: This archive contains the code, derived data, and results of the study " Reported or observed? Satellite-mapped flood exposure reveals a reporting gap that machine-learned impact models inherit."  The study compares the number of people reported as affected by floods in EM-DAT with the population living inside the inundation mapped by MODIS in the Global Flood Database, for 1,266 country-level flood records from 2000 to 2018. It measures how the ratio of reported to observed impact depends on the reporting country at equal hazard, including floods that cross borders; tests whether ridge and gradient-boosting impact models trained on reported labels inherit this dependence; evaluates transfer across continents with importance weighting, the area of applicability and (weighted, Mondrian) conformal prediction; and shows how a small fraction of satellite labels removes most of the inherited bias. Results are expressed in the relative economic value of impact-based warnings. Contents. scripts/: the complete Python pipeline, including Google Earth Engine extraction of observed labels, ex-ante exposure (GHSL, GloFAS, MERIT Hydro) and ERA5-Land forcing on administrative footprints (steps 10-15), statistical and machine-learning analyses (steps 20-25), and figure scripts (steps 30-32). jobs/: the SLURM batch script used on the national supercomputer of Côte d'Ivoire and an equivalent local runner. data/: derived tables at the level of the EM-DAT record (observed exposure and flooded area, quality fractions, exposure and landscape predictors, hydroclimatic forcing, country covariates, EM-DAT-GFD links), GFD event metadata, study regions and a Natural Earth base map. results/: all result tables of the paper (2,000 cluster-bootstrap draws). README.md explains how to reproduce every result and figure. EM-DAT data are not redistributed, in accordance with the CRED terms of use. The derived tables carry only the EM-DAT identifier, country code and year. Users can download the public EM-DAT export of 11 May 2026 from https://www.emdat.be and rebuild the analysis table with two scripts; with that export the rebuilt table is identical to the one used in the paper. summary: Data and analysis code for a mixed-method, between-subjects user study comparing SQL-LLM, a natural-language database interface backed by GPT-4o, with Snowflake, a conventional SQL editor. Twenty SQL-literate participants each completed 12 querying tasks drawn from the BIRD Text-to-SQL benchmark across three relational schemas (Books, Mondial Geo, Legislator), with screen recordings, think-aloud protocols, and timing logs. The package contains the raw study inputs (cleaned timing/SQL spreadsheet, hand-coded behavioral proxies, 11 think-aloud transcripts, per-participant notebooks and reports), derived and graded artifacts (execution-based correctness grades, three LLM-judge grades, BIRD gold answers, model/timing CSVs, LLM inter-coder reliability files), and the full analysis pipeline (figure notebook, execution grader, gold-answer fetcher, difficulty-validation and effect-size scripts). See README.md for the layout and steps. The BIRD gold SQLite databases are not included but are regenerated from the public BIRD train split via the provided script. Code is released under the MIT License; data files under CC BY 4.0.
title: Replication Package: Natural Language Interfaces for Databases — What Changes for Users? (SQL-LLM vs. Snowflake User Study)

summary: Audio textures exhibit complex temporal dynamics that are not well represented by single-scale models. We propose a multi-scale latent trajectory approach for audio texture synthesis using latent representations extracted from a pretrained neural audio codec. By decomposing latent trajectories into slow structural and fast stochastic components, we enable direct modeling and interpretation of the longterm temporal structure and fine-grained detail of audio textures. Our experiments on environmental audio textures suggest that the proposed method significantly improves audio quality over a single-scale baseline and achieves performance competitive with a latent diffusion model. Using perceptually motivated summary statistics, we demonstrate that generated continuations preserve texture identity. Through the proposed methods, we enable continuous texture generation from a given context and expose a latent structure that may support control over long-term dynamics.
title: MULTI-SCALE LATENT TRAJECTORY MODELLING FOR AUDIO TEXTURE SYNTHESIS

summary: Analysis code, result tables and manuscript sources for a leakage-controlled benchmark of missense variant effect predictors (AlphaMissense, REVEL, CADD, ESM1b) in genes listed in the 2024 IUIS classification of inborn errors of immunity. Per-variant tables containing REVEL scores are not included because of REVEL licence terms. Files are restricted during peer review.

summary: Аннотация. В статье представлен комплексный лингвистический и историко-дипломатический анализ письма вице-губернатора крепости Анапа Сеид-Махмуда Мусселима от 29 марта 1817 года, которое адресовано русскому адмиралу Алексею Самуиловичу Грейгу. Этот документ рассматривается как важнейшее локальное историческое открытие, который на данный момент формирует вокруг себя уникальный контекст пограничной российско-османской коммуникации и одновременно вписывается в макроконтекст реализации условий Бухарестского мирного договора 1812 г. В ходе исследования подробно изучена композиционная структура документа, выявлены системные графические, орфографические и грамматические девиации во французском тексте. Исследование позволяет реконструировать уровень османских адъютантов и специфику функционирования французского языка как инструмента дипломатии.   Abstract. The article presents a complex linguistic and historical-diplomatic analysis of the letter of the vice-governor of the fortress Anapa Seyid-Mahmud Mousselim dated 29 March 1817, which was addressed to the Russian admiral Alexey Samuilovitch Greig. This document is regarded as the most important local historical discovery, which at the moment forms around it a unique context of the Russian border -Ottoman communication and at the same time fits into the macro context of the implementation of the terms of the Treaty of Bucharest (1812). In the course of the study, the compositional structure of the document was thoroughly examined, systematic graphical, orthographic, and grammatical deviations in the French text were identified. The study allows for a reconstruction of the level of Ottoman adjutants and the specificity of the functioning of the French language as an instrument of diplomacy.
title: ЛИНГВИСТИЧЕСКИЕ ИНТЕРФЕРЕНЦИИ И ПРАГМАТИКА ДИПЛОМАТИЧЕСКОГО ДИСКУРСА В РОССИЙСКО-ОСМАНСКОЙ КОРРЕСПОНДЕНЦИИ НАЧАЛА XIX ВЕКА (НА МАТЕРИАЛЕ ПИСЬМА ИЗ АНАПЫ А.С. ГРЕЙГУ)

summary: This software update consolidates the cumulative Lean formalization and supporting computational records for the fixed Singmaster-type equation choose(A,4) = choose(C,6), with A ≥ 4 and C ≥ 6. It includes the verified arithmetic, elliptic-curve, height, complex-analytic, period-lattice, auxiliary-function, interpolation, and subgroup developments, together with calculation scripts, documentation, verification logs, and provenance records. summary: Аннотация . Статья посвящена работе с цифровыми архивами при изучении первых дней Великой Отечественной войны. Рассмотрены возможности порталов «Память народа», ОБД «Мемориал», «Подвиг народа» и коллекций Президентской библиотеки. Показано, почему готовый пересказ, в том числе созданный нейросетью, нельзя ставить на место архивного документа. Предложен простой порядок проверки: найти первичный образ, уточнить происхождение документа, сопоставить его с другими свидетельствами и только после этого формулировать вывод. Такой подход помогает сохранить личное измерение военной истории и снижает риск повторения неточных или вырванных из контекста утверждений. Abstract. The article discusses the use of digital archives in studying the first days of the Great Patriotic War. It examines the resources Memory of the People, Memorial, Feat of the People, and the Presidential Library collections. The paper explains why a ready-made narrative, including an AI-generated one, cannot replace an archival document. A simple verification procedure is proposed: locate the original image, identify the document provenance, compare it with other evidence, and only then formulate a conclusion. This approach preserves the personal dimension of military history and reduces the risk of repeating inaccurate or decontextualized claims.
title: ПЕРВЫЕ ДНИ ВЕЛИКОЙ ОТЕЧЕСТВЕННОЙ ВОЙНЫ В ЦИФРОВЫХ АРХИВАХ: КАК НЕ ПОТЕРЯТЬ ДОКУМЕНТ ЗА ГОТОВЫМ ПЕРЕСКАЗОМ

summary: Interpretability, AI auditing and assessments of machine consciousness increasingly rest on mechanism-level quantities: functionals of a system's causal transition law that describe how it computes, not what it outputs. Experiments see that law only through finite, partial and noisy interventions. We ask when such a quantity is identifiable from an experiment's access, continuous in the mechanism and certifiable from finite data, and answer exactly for a deliberately demanding case - the integrated information $\varphi$ of integrated information theory - in stochastic networks of four and five units with known ground truth. Behavior can be silent: a recurrent and a feed-forward network with identical input-output laws at their response delay carry 0.28 and 0 bits, yet internal recordings separate them within 4-53 trials. Partial access can be just as blind: in our examples, units left out of a one-step recording impose precision floors of 0.30-1.02 bits that no sample size lowers, and in all-but-self parity networks, recordings of any length see several hidden units only through the product of their fidelities - a symmetry that one intervention broke in exact checks. The measure has sharp edges: because $\varphi$ selects a partition, and the cause and effect it specifies, by one criterion and reports another, infinitesimal changes of mechanism that cross an edge change it by 25-100% at 99% of the edges we found in random networks, and about 1% of surrogate models that fit interventional data almost perfectly misreport it by more than 20%. One-sided claims survive: the same data certify a lower bound on both sides of an edge, and we prove $\varphi>1.004$ bits throughout a 64-dimensional region of mechanisms and certify it from about $10^7$ controlled transitions with false-certificate probability at most $α$. Measurability is thus a design question with computable answers.
title: Same Behavior, Different Mechanism: What Finite Experiments Can Certify About Integrated Information

summary: Discovering continuous symmetries directly from differential-equation data can reveal geometric structure for model reduction and scientific machine learning without symbolic determining equations or a closed-form representation of the governing system. We formulate intrinsic Lie point-symmetry discovery as an operator-theoretic problem on sampled jet-space data. Admissible generators are identified from a sampled determining operator and separated from redundant, solution-dependent, and geometrically trivial directions. The framework combines prolongation, sequential subspace restrictions, and a fixed nonlinear dictionary linear in trainable coefficients. A rank-stabilization preflight test diagnoses systems whose represented intrinsic symmetry algebra does not stabilize under dictionary refinement. On a controlled differential-equation benchmark with an analytically known 11-dimensional represented intrinsic symmetry algebra, the method recovers the complete represented generator set, reproduces its Lie-bracket structure to numerical precision, and approximates a known generator beyond the training domain. Here we show that explicit intrinsic continuous-symmetry generators can be recovered from data obtained from exact or approximate differential systems.
title: Data-driven discovery of intrinsic Lie point symmetries of differential equation systems

summary: As "AI Scientists" emerge to drive research via the Model Context Protocol (MCP), systems relying on ephemeral scripts will fail. The sheer scale of stateful, interconnected evidence requires a machine-walkable warranty grounded in a purpose-built database architecture. Eigenius is an open-source, typed knowledge-graph DBMS built on a single premise: answering the audit question ("what do you know, and what is your warranty?") requires a unified kernel. By tightly coupling the type system, storage engine, and integration protocol, Eigenius turns data provenance into a structural invariant rather than a property reconstructed across subsystem boundaries. The kernel rests on three pillars whose metatheory is mechanized in Lean 4: a dependent type theory (EigenTT) separating confluent conversion from ontology subsumption and keeping proof irrelevance axiomatic so distinct warrants remain inspectable; proof-calculus institutions acting as strongly typed integration boundaries; and a content-addressed immutable storage layer. Epistemic status (declared/observed/derived/verified) forms a bounded lattice over a justification logic enforced at commit. Cross-system comorphisms carry explicit axiom policies (Adopt, Discharge, Relativize), transport witnesses at commit, and materialize outputs into the graph, while EigenQL provides a Grothendieck query view across all hosted logics and shared on-chain IRs collapse multi-system translations to identity. Pairing empirical justification logic with an in-process Lean 4 term checker, an end-to-end recomputation of a published Nature study from pinned data discharges all 52 derived conclusions and surfaces four machine-checked discrepancies in the original study.
title: Eigenius: A Typed Knowledge-Graph DBMS with Epistemic Stratification and Institution-Mediated Reasoning

summary: The goal of this paper is to investigate the following question: what geometric restrictions does the existence of a transitive family of constant mean curvature hyperspheres impose on a Riemannian metric on $\mathbb S^n$? The notion of a transitive family can be made precise through the theory of Zoll families developed by Ambrozio, Marques, and Neves. Within this framework, we partially extend their local rigidity theorem for even conformal factors on $\mathbb S^3$ to every dimension $n\ge4$, assuming each hypersphere in the minimal Zoll family has the area of a round equator. Moreover, we give a partial answer to the following higher-dimensional version of a question posed by Robert Bryant: must a metric on $\mathbb S^n$, conformal to the round metric and admitting a Zoll family of hyperspheres with a common nonzero constant mean curvature, have constant sectional curvature? Finally, we also investigate inverse problems in the spirit of Hangan, asking which metrics make a fixed family of geodesic spheres have a common prescribed mean curvature.
title: Spheres with transitive families of CMC hypersurfaces

summary: Reconstructing turbulent flow fields from sparse and irregular measurements remains challenging because the underlying inverse problem is severely underdetermined. Here we present MANTRA, a manifold-based tensor framework that represents each velocity component in a continuous tensor-product space while constraining its coefficient tensor to a low-rank Tucker manifold. This structure provides a compact, data-adaptive representation without requiring gridded observations or governing equations. Riemannian optimization and adaptive selection of rank and basis complexity enable the model to exploit coordinate-wise spatiotemporal correlations. In simulations of forced isotropic turbulence and flow over a cylinder, MANTRA recovers multiscale structures at sampling densities orders of magnitude below the underlying grids and remains accurate under Gaussian noise up to 20% of the peak velocity. It also recovers leading coordinate-wise correlation structures from sparse observations. Applied to experimental particle-tracking velocimetry of an oscillating impinging jet, MANTRA reveals time-evolving structures that are not apparent from the scattered measurements alone.
title: Low-Rank Tensor Manifolds for Turbulent Field Reconstruction from Sparse Data

summary: This work identifies a fundamental, controller-independent limitation in reusable launch vehicle powered descent: a sudden $180^\circ$ phase transition in the open-loop transfer functions from the control inputs to the lateral drift and drift rate. The transition occurs inside the flight envelope, reverses the effective control direction, and can destabilize the closed loop system under uncertainty. An analytical condition governing this transition is derived, its physical mechanism is established, and its dependence on vehicle mass, aerodynamic properties, and geometry is characterized. An Incremental Nonlinear Dynamic Inversion (INDI)-based control architecture is then developed to inherently address this limitation and is tuned via $\mathcal{H}_\infty$ Closed Loop Shaping to provide local robustness and performance guarantees. The internal dynamics introduced by the INDI inversion are analytically derived and proven to be stable throughout the flight envelope. The proposed controller is compared against a robust gain-scheduled baseline controller through linear stability analysis and an extensive nonlinear Monte Carlo campaign. Both controllers achieve 100% success across the considered Monte Carlo campaign, though the INDI-based controller provides improved tracking performance, superior nominal and dispersed stability margins, requires fewer controller design points, and reduces controller tuning complexity.
title: Overcoming Fundamental Control Limitations in Powered Descent Flight through Robust Incremental Nonlinear Dynamic Inversion

summary: Supplementary data for an experiment that replaced the larva segmentation model of the Tenebrio molitor behavioral-phenotyping pipeline while every downstream step (Petri geometry, primary-larva selection, continuity gate, interpolation, smoothing, features, quality control) was held fixed. Five segmenters were compared: the YOLO11s-seg used for the v1.0.0 dataset, YOLOv8s-seg, YOLO26s-seg and Mask R-CNN R50-FPN v2 trained on full tray images, and a YOLO11s-seg trained on Petri crops. The crop-trained model was then applied to all 34 videos and the Results analysis repeated. On Petri crops, the input the pipeline processes, mask mAP@0.5 was 0.10 for the full-tray YOLO11s and 0.99 for the crop-trained YOLO11s and Mask R-CNN; on 79 held-out labelled video frames larva recall was 0.69, 0.99 and 0.96. The two ground-truth-accurate models agreed with each other (CCC 0.91–0.99 on distance, speed, edge fraction, entropy and area). Heat contrasts kept their direction on the 34 videos.
