summary: Abstract The Laser Cognition (LC) is a proposed multilevel theoretical framework for investigating how selective attention, conscious access, curiosity-guided inquiry, associative recruitment, and representational integration may contribute to the emergence and evaluation of novel ideas. Its central explanatory metaphor is laser illumination: a complex cognitive field contains multiple thoughts, memories, representations, and potential relationships, while a selected cognitive target receives processing priority. The framework uses this metaphor to organize a proposed mechanism linking cognitive-field activation, attentional targeting, awareness-mediated processing, focus regulation, associative recruitment, integrative recombination, candidate generation, and metacognitive evaluation. LC retains the distinction between the full theory, its default mechanism, and its canonical primary case. The primary case is the Laser-Spotlight Cognitive Genesis Case (LSCGC); the proposed default mechanism is the Laser Cognition Default Mechanism (LC-DM); and its principal operational cycle is the Laser-Guided Cognitive Integration Cycle (LGCIC). The framework is formalized using a weighted cognitive graph, a dual-route attentional-targeting model, a normalized attentional-allocation function, a focus-stability measure, an associative-recruitment equation, a cognitive-integration index, a probabilistic candidate-emergence model, and a feedback-control representation. The mathematical expressions constitute proposed model specifications, not established equations of human neural operation. Awareness, attention, curiosity, affective engagement, cognitive flexibility, and metacognitive monitoring are treated as related but conceptually distinct constructs. The architecture includes eighteen layers, a multidomain research structure, eight initial research hypotheses, explicit falsifiability requirements, a cross-system functional generalization framework, a fourteen-step research protocol, and a twenty-part manuscript structure. Human cognition is the primary explanatory domain. Applications to artificial intelligence, large language models, artificial general intelligence, and possible artificial superintelligence are framed as hypotheses about functional or computational correspondence rather than established claims of shared consciousness or identical mechanisms. LC is presented as a theory-development and validation framework. Its explanatory value, novelty, causal assumptions, parameter identifiability, empirical adequacy, and cross-domain applicability remain subject to systematic literature review, mathematical audit, empirical testing, model comparison, and replication.

title: THE LASER COGNITION (LC): A Multilevel Neurocognitive, Mathematical, and Cybernetic Framework of Awareness-Guided Attentional Illumination, Neural-Pattern Integration, and Novel Idea Emergence

summary: Supplementary data package for the systematic review "Wireless Body Sensor Networks in Sports: A Systematic Review of Technologies, Applications, and Challenges" (80 included studies described in 82 reports, 2016–2026; PRISMA 2020). The package contains the complete data-extraction table (80 studies × 64 deposited fields across seven research questions), the screening register of all 394 records with relevance scores, exclusion reasons and quality appraisals, the literal search strings per database with execution dates and hit counts, the per-study quality judgments, the provenance of the nine prior reviews compared in the article, the SpringerLink post-filter with its per-record decision matrix, including the disposition of every record re-screened in the August 2026 audit, and the completed PRISMA 2020 checklist, which maps each item to the section, table or figure of the article that reports it. A multi-tab workbook compiles every supplementary table together with a codebook of the extraction fields. Every field is in English: column headers, coded values and free text in every table. Extraction and appraisal were carried out in Spanish, and the Spanish originals remain in the authors' working spreadsheet. The extraction template has 65 fields and 64 are deposited: the omitted one holds the reviewer's working annotations rather than data about the studies, and the codebook records both its existence and its absence. This version adds the completed PRISMA 2020 checklist (Table S8), which the article now provides as supplementary material. It also regenerates the per-study quality table from the screening register, in which the five studies admitted in the August 2026 audit had been exported with zero on every criterion; translates the 78 cells that remained in Spanish, including the notes of the search table; corrects two rows of the SpringerLink decision matrix and one extraction error checked against the full text; and defines the cloud-platform field in the codebook.

summary: Interpretations have been widely used in the study of provenance of queries on semiring-annotated databases. Here, we consider two different interpretation-based semantics for first-order formulas in negation normal form, namely, the canonical-interpretation semantics and the compatible-interpretation semantics. We show that the resulting query languages cannot express the monus operation on semiring-annotated relations, when the annotations come from the bag semiring or the tropical semiring or the fuzzy semiring. Consequently, the semantics of SQL cannot be captured using the interpretation-based semantics considered here.
title: Monus vs. Interpretations in Semiring Semantics

summary: It was shown by Braverman-Finkelberg-Nakajima that the regular perverse sheaf on the affine Grassmannian of type A is isomorphic to the ring object associated to a Gelfand-Tsetlin quiver. We use this result to identify, for any finite dimensional representation $\mathbf{N}$ of a product of general linear groups, the relative Langlands dual $(T^*\mathbf{N})^\vee$ of $T^*\mathbf{N}$ with the Coulomb branch of a suitable representation. By a result of Bellamy, this implies that $(T^*\mathbf{N})^\vee$ has symplectic singularities.
title: Symplectic singularities in Relative Langlands duality for products of general linear groups

By a result of Bellamy, this implies that $(T^*\mathbf{N})^\vee$ has symplectic singularities.
title: Symplectic singularities in Relative Langlands duality for products of general linear groups

summary: Deposit accompanying S. A. Oprisan and A. Oprisan, "What a Prompt Can and Cannot Enforce: A Seventeen-Version Case Study of a Socratic Physics Tutor on Microsoft 365 Copilot Agent Builder", American Journal of Physics (Reports), manuscript AJP26-AR-00984. It contains the final (v17) system prompt of the PhysCoach agent (7,999 Unicode codepoints, byte for byte as deployed), four earlier drafts recovered from the design-phase record, and the complete record of the 240-trial evaluation campaign: the frozen protocol and its amendments, the void log, the authors' rulings, the canonical student responses and frozen probe table, the authoritative author-reviewed trial log and the original log, the 55 failure records with sub-modes, the run plan, one verbatim transcript per trial, and the script that draws the paper's compliance and failure-mode figures. Copilot conversation identifiers and the name of an unrelated personal document are withheld. See README.md inside the archive for contents and how to read the record. The scripts that logged and paced the trials, the send log, the throttle records, and a labeled reconstruction of the browser script that sent the student turns are in the related record 10.5281/zenodo.24012086.

summary: Supplementary dataset for three pre-registered buyer-side experiments verifying x402 v2 payments on Base mainnet, executed as scripted protocol runs and committed regardless of outcome; every reported number traces to a committed analysis.json and raw artifacts under experiments/ . Experiment 1: echo-verify A fresh USD 0.01 mainnet happy-path settlement, verified end-to-end via payer-anchored Transfer events on two independent RPCs (paid run 1.11 s; discovery median 0.0388 s over 15 GETs; tx 0xa3143d32319392227c017ce86dceb2a8e377b7e4f32c21f2693a6925e91f201c ). Headline finding: exactly 0.01 USDC settled to payTo per Transfer events on both RPCs. Experiment 2: mock-seller Hostile-seller failure-mode detection, including a same-nonce EIP-3009 replay on an Anvil fork pinned at block 54035433. Headline finding: 4 of 4 hostile-seller failure modes were correctly detected; the replay reverted at EVM state level with FiatTokenV2: authorization is used or canceled . Experiment 3: preflight-external Decode-only compatibility probing of third-party x402 endpoints, with a hard no-payment guard: zero payment-bearing headers sent, guard trips on 0 paid requests. Headline finding: 2 of 3 third-party endpoints returned protocol-compatible v2 402 challenges; agent402.tools diverged with a 404. Contents experiments/ — pre-registered protocols, runners, run records, verbatim raw API artifacts and on-chain receipts results/ , RESULTS.md , METHODOLOGY.md , DATA_DICTIONARY.md — per-experiment reports, record schema figures/ , recipe/ — frozen figure recipes and rendered figures Disclosure: the operator is affiliated with aptu.dev; Experiment 1 verifies the operator's own endpoint. Findings are about verification of the x402 protocol, not any product.

summary: Analysis and figure-generation code for the manuscript "[title]". The code demonstrates, on a public dataset of student teaching evaluations, why comparing a section's mean rating to a department average is statistically invalid, and shows how the power to detect a real difference collapses at small sample sizes. Scripts: turkiye_simulation_NREP5000.py (Monte Carlo power/breakpoint analysis), turkiye_leaveoneout_analysis.py (structure and leave-one-out benchmark comparisons), turkiye_make_all_figures.py (figures). See README for versions and seeds. Data: Türkiye Student Evaluation dataset (Gündüz & Fokoue), UCI ML Repository ID 262, DOI 10.24432/C5S02S, CC BY 4.0. Not redistributed here; retrieved from UCI at run time. Reproducibility: all draws seeded; results stable to <1 percentage point at NREP = 5000; fast Mann–Whitney routine validated against scipy to machine precision. Requirements: Python 3 with numpy, pandas, scipy, matplotlib, ucimlrepo. License: [MIT/BSD-3-Clause]. Please cite both this code and the dataset (DOI 10.24432/C5S02S). Code is released under the MIT License; figures and documentation are released under CC BY 4.0.
title: Statistics of Course Evaluation Scores

summary: Аннотация . Статья посвящена работе с цифровыми архивами при изучении первых дней Великой Отечественной войны. Рассмотрены возможности порталов «Память народа», ОБД «Мемориал», «Подвиг народа» и коллекций Президентской библиотеки. Показано, почему готовый пересказ, в том числе созданный нейросетью, нельзя ставить на место архивного документа. Предложен простой порядок проверки: найти первичный образ, уточнить происхождение документа, сопоставить его с другими свидетельствами и только после этого формулировать вывод. Такой подход помогает сохранить личное измерение военной истории и снижает риск повторения неточных или вырванных из контекста утверждений. Abstract. The article discusses the use of digital archives in studying the first days of the Great Patriotic War. It examines the resources Memory of the People, Memorial, Feat of the People, and the Presidential Library collections. The paper explains why a ready-made narrative, including an AI-generated one, cannot replace an archival document. A simple verification procedure is proposed: locate the original image, identify the document provenance, compare it with other evidence, and only then formulate a conclusion. This approach preserves the personal dimension of military history and reduces the risk of repeating inaccurate or decontextualized claims.
title: ПЕРВЫЕ ДНИ ВЕЛИКОЙ ОТЕЧЕСТВЕННОЙ ВОЙНЫ В ЦИФРОВЫХ АРХИВАХ: КАК НЕ ПОТЕРЯТЬ ДОКУМЕНТ ЗА ГОТОВЫМ ПЕРЕСКАЗОМ

summary: Knowledge distillation transfers predictions, representations, or other supervisory information between learning models and is increasingly investigated in quantum machine learning. Its applications extend beyond compression to cross-architecture transfer, circuit approximation, distributed learning, and classical deployment of models trained using quantum-derived supervision. This survey reviews these approaches using two complementary classification axes: teacher-student configuration and the role of quantum resources in the distillation process. Quantum-inspired methods are discussed separately from methods that simulate quantum computations classically or execute them on quantum hardware. We explain how measurement probabilities, expectation values, classical readouts, state overlaps, and circuit-level objectives support different transfer mechanisms. We then critically assess the presented results against baseline design, execution conditions, uncertainty, and resource costs. The evidence shows that distillation can improve selected quantum students, but benefits are task- and architecture-dependent, and several studies find negligible gains or even performance degradation. Evaluations on physical quantum hardware remain limited, with some testing individual quantum components rather than complete learning pipelines. Heterogeneous protocols and incomplete resource reporting prevent general conclusions about practical quantum advantage. We identify priorities for controlled benchmarking, noise-aware learning, reproducible evaluation, and efficient transfer between quantum and classical models.
title: Quantum Knowledge Distillation: State-of-the-art, Applications and Open Problems

summary: Discovering continuous symmetries directly from differential-equation data can reveal geometric structure for model reduction and scientific machine learning without symbolic determining equations or a closed-form representation of the governing system. We formulate intrinsic Lie point-symmetry discovery as an operator-theoretic problem on sampled jet-space data. Admissible generators are identified from a sampled determining operator and separated from redundant, solution-dependent, and geometrically trivial directions. The framework combines prolongation, sequential subspace restrictions, and a fixed nonlinear dictionary linear in trainable coefficients. A rank-stabilization preflight test diagnoses systems whose represented intrinsic symmetry algebra does not stabilize under dictionary refinement. On a controlled differential-equation benchmark with an analytically known 11-dimensional represented intrinsic symmetry algebra, the method recovers the complete represented generator set, reproduces its Lie-bracket structure to numerical precision, and approximates a known generator beyond the training domain. Here we show that explicit intrinsic continuous-symmetry generators can be recovered from data obtained from exact or approximate differential systems.
title: Data-driven discovery of intrinsic Lie point symmetries of differential equation systems

summary: Analog compute-in-memory (CIM) enables energy-efficient AI inference by performing in-situ matrix multiplication. The growing demand for deploying larger models motivates chiplet integration to expand CIM capacity. However, simulation abstractions based on local operator costs and aggregate communication metrics obscure the impact of weight-mapping topology when CIM system scales up. We develop a phase analysis that quantifies how strongly mapping topology affects system performance across hardware configurations and how mapping optimization translates into latency gains. To evaluate and exploit this design space, we present Isobar, a simulation platform integrating CIM decompositions, heterogeneous execution, and resource modeling. Validated against silicon measurements and cycle-accurate simulation, Isobar provides reliable cost estimates that enable effective mapping search across model and hardware configurations. For Gemma-7B prefill, Isobar-guided mapping reduces communication time by 23.3% and end-to-end latency by 18.6% relative to the strongest baseline. Isobar's system-level modeling show that analog CIM retains energy-efficiency potential relative to GPU when scaled to thousands of dies, and identify topology-aware mapping as a key design dimension for efficient execution.
title: Scaling Up Analog CIM: A Simulation Framework for Topology-Aware Mapping

summary: Latent communication enables agents to collaborate efficiently by directly exchanging intermediate model representations rather than raw sensor data or text messages. Existing approaches, however, are primarily designed for LLM agents and do not consider the bandwidth constraints and heterogeneous task deadlines faced by cyber-physical agents. In this work, we propose SCALE, a real-time latent communication method tailored for cyber-physical agents. Motivated by the spatio-temporal continuity of the physical world, SCALE matches tokens across consecutive latent messages using similarity scores to identify reusable information and avoid redundant transmission. It then profiles the semantic gain and communication cost of transmitting different amounts of latent information. Based on these profiles, SCALE employs a real-time scheduler that jointly determines which pending messages to transmit and how many latent tokens to send, subject to available bandwidth and task deadlines. We evaluate SCALE across three cyber-physical benchmarks and a physical spider robot case study under diverse network conditions and heterogeneous task deadlines. Our results show that SCALE significantly improves both task performance and on-time delivery in bandwidth-constrained networks. Our code is available at: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/SCALE-4E80/.
title: SCALE: Real-Time Latent Communication for Cyber-Physical Agents

summary: LLM-based medical assistants that follow a patient across visits need a memory that keeps the patient's clinical state correct as it changes. We examine the errors of five memory systems on longitudinal medical dialogue and find three recurring causes: the retrieved evidence gives an outdated state, includes another person's health facts, or lacks a safety fact the answer depends on. We present MedGraph, a graph memory built for these three cases. Construction extracts dated facts from each session, attributes each fact to the person it describes, and links medication, diagnosis, and measurement records into chains that keep earlier states. Retrieval ranks the patient's chains as units, reads each chain at the time the question asks about, and adds the original dialogue text; a patient profile lists every recorded safety fact with every question. On MedMemoryBench, MedGraph has the highest overall accuracy with both a GPT and a Qwen backbone, 10.5 and 10.4 points above the strongest of five baselines, with efficient memory construction and answering in the GPT setting.
title: MedGraph: Maintaining Patient State with Graph Memory for Long-Term Medical Dialogue

summary: Landing-phase safety-event prediction requires the detection of rare abnormal approaches within strongly imbalanced multivariate flight data. Capturing coupled temporal behavior while distinguishing event-specific signatures across airport operating contexts remains a central modeling challenge. This study proposes an interpretable hybrid feature-fusion framework for multiclass landing-phase safety-event prediction. A long short-term memory (LSTM) autoencoder trained on nominal flight windows characterizes deviations from routine approach behavior. Its continuous reconstruction-error descriptor is fused with parameter-specific statistical flight-history features and supplied to a class-weighted XGBoost classifier to distinguish Normal, Speed High, Path High, and Flaps Late windows. The framework is evaluated using 53,750 NASA DASHlink approach windows from three arrival airports. Pooled and airport-specific learning strategies are compared alongside component-level benchmarks, repeated pipeline retraining, and feature-attribution analysis. The results demonstrate strong class-balanced detection, with mean macro recall above 0.90 across all airports under repeated partitioning and retraining. Component comparisons establish the importance of class weighting and show that continuous feature fusion outperforms reconstruction-error-only and hard-gate alternatives. Airport-level comparisons reveal benefits from local specialization at the two airports with larger datasets and from pooled training at the airport with the smallest dataset. Feature attributions associate predictions with operationally relevant vertical-path, configuration, speed, and approach-context variables. The framework provides an interpretable approach to rare-event detection and practical guidance for adapting flight-data monitoring models to airport-level data availability.
title: Hybrid Machine Learning for Imbalanced Landing-Phase Safety Event Prediction from Flight Data

summary: Linear attention compresses context into a fixed-size key-value state for linear-time training and constant-memory inference. Gated delta-rule models decay this state and erase its prediction for an incoming key before writing a new value; Gated DeltaNet-2 (GDN-2) generalizes this with channel-wise decay and decoupled, full-rank erase and write gates. However, we show that state updates are far less sensitive to erasure than to writes: key activation and unit normalization concentrate key energy onto a sparse subset of channels, whereas value writes scale all channels, so the erase gate can be parameterized at lower rank. Furthermore, slow-decaying state rows accumulate much larger norms than fast rows, dominating unweighted readout and forcing stronger write-time erasure to suppress interference. Guided by this analysis, we introduce Muir, which fuses all gates into a sensitivity-allocated low-rank projection, re-weights state rows with a matched-filter readout gate, and reinvests the saved parameters in a wider feed-forward network. Because standard chunkwise algorithms become numerically unstable at the large chunk sizes needed to saturate wide matrix units, we design a parallel update for stable, efficient training. Across 166M-1.34B parameters, Muir lowers perplexity by 1.8-2.0% over GDN-2 and 2.5-3.6% over Transformer, raises commonsense accuracy by up to 1.9 points, and improves extractive recall over GDN-2. At 1.34B, Muir outperforms both baselines on multi-hop and multi-needle recall, extrapolates 2,560x from its 4K training length to 10M-token streams without perplexity drift, and maintains near-100% passkey retrieval to 1M tokens with static readout. Muir achieves these gains while matching GDN-2 throughput, reaching its 100B-token validation loss 1.2x faster, and training 2.7x faster than Transformer at 32K.
title: Muir: Linear Attention with Sensitivity-Allocated Gating and Matched-Filter Readout

summary: Online Convex Optimization with memory and time-varying constraints (COCO-M) is a recently-introduced framework that captures the dynamics of stateful online learning and non-stochastic control with budget constraints. Despite its expressive power, COCO-M remains largely understudied. In this work, we tackle this problem in its full scale, providing an optimistic algorithm that incorporates untrusted predictions to tame universal dynamic regret and cumulative constraint violation. Our analysis leverages a potent reduction from memory to delay and treats state-dependent gradients as delayed feedback. We establish the first bounds that adapt to both environment non-stationarity (path length $P_T$) and prediction accuracy, while lifting previous restrictive assumptions such as functional separability. En route to these results, we derive findings of independent interest for the memory-to-delay reduction, and for delayed OCO with time-varying constraints. The proposed framework ensures sublinear worst-case guarantees that improve with prediction accuracy, reaching $\mathcal O(1)$ regret under perfect predictions, with cumulative constraint violation (CCV) $\mathcal O(\sqrt{T})$ for unknown $P_T$ and $\mathcal O(\log T)$ for known or online observable $P_T$ , while recovering the optimal COCO rates when memory disappears.
title: Dynamic Optimistic Constrained OCO with Memory via Delay Equivalence

summary: LLM pruning must preserve quality while meeting hardware- and workload-specific constraints on latency, throughput, and memory. Existing pruning workflows often target parameter counts, requiring practitioners to manually select model sizes that meet latency, throughput, and GPU memory limits. However, parameter count alone does not predict these metrics, which depend on the model architecture, workload, hardware, and serving engine. We introduce AutoCompress, a hardware-guided compression framework that directly incorporates such constraints into differentiable architecture search. AutoCompress jointly optimizes global and per-layer structure to produce heterogeneous architectures, guided by serving-engine cost models validated against end-to-end latency, throughput, and memory measurements. We evaluate AutoCompress on long-context local coding, batched datacenter serving, and latency-sensitive in-game interaction. Compared to the state-of-the-art Minitron pruning framework, AutoCompress improves average accuracy across eight benchmarks by 6.57, 2.35, and 0.57 percentage points on RTX 5070, RTX 5080, and H100, respectively. AutoCompress also compresses Nemotron 3.5 Super from 120B to 74B parameters for single-B200 BF16 serving at 128K context, retaining 95% of its mean benchmark score.
title: AutoCompress: Automated Hardware-Guided Model Compression

summary: World-action models adapt pretrained video generators, and vision-language-action models build on pretrained vision-language backbones; both tie policy architecture and inference cost to large transformers designed for generation rather than control. It remains unclear how much these generation-oriented choices affect control. In this work, we introduce Latent Action JEPA (La-JEPA), a compact world-action model whose policy transformer is trained from scratch in the feature space of a pretrained V-JEPA 2.1 encoder. Following Fast-WAM, La-JEPA learns to predict future features jointly with actions during training and generates only actions at inference. Among policies without embodied pretraining, La-JEPA achieves state-of-the-art performance in clean and randomized RoboTwin 2.0 scenes and on LIBERO-Plus with correct instructions, while using far fewer parameters than the strongest competing policies. It runs substantially faster than Fast-WAM at comparable performance and outperforms the closest JEPA-based methods, LeapBot-WA and JEPA-WAM, on LIBERO-Plus and RoboTwin 2.0 without their pretrained policy backbones. On four real-robot tasks, its average success is comparable to pi0.5 and above non-embodied-pretrained baselines. Through a design study of the choices behind La-JEPA, we show that JEPA features outperform video VAE latents, most clearly out of distribution, and that training-time future prediction choices significantly impact the policy even when future prediction is skipped at inference. We correct the LIBERO-Plus instructions, as the officially released evaluator corrupts them for most variants, and re-evaluate several strong open baselines. Without a generative pretrained policy backbone, La-JEPA is better and faster than far larger policies, suggesting that robot foundation models may benefit from architectures designed for control rather than inherited from generation.
title: La-JEPA: Compact Robot Policies with Latent World Modeling

summary: In large-scale payment networks, entities (card, merchant, etc.) and their interactions play a key role in transaction anomaly detection. However, transaction patterns between different entities usually change more frequently than the production model refresh schedule. Meanwhile, entity embedding tables suffer from high-cardinality and sparse interaction issues. To resolve the above challenges, we present PersonaAgent, an agentic transaction anomaly detection framework which represents the latest entity behavior signals as personas and saves them in a refreshable memory. Offline, a weekly scheduled batch job is used to extract the latest behavior signals and update them in the memory. At inference time, a lightweight adapter retrieves the corresponding entity behavior signals of each transaction from memory and uses them to augment the base anomaly classifier's scoring. Through comprehensive benchmarking with different anomaly detection models at Visa, PersonaAgent is able to score transactions efficiently (a 1,000-transaction CPU batch in 1-2 ms), lifting the PR-AUC by 0.65-6.58% and the production business metric by 8.93-14.24% relatively in deployment.
title: PersonaAgent: Retrieval-Augmented Transaction Anomaly Scoring with Refreshable Multi-Entity Persona Memory

summary: Tensor network kernel machines (TNKMs) combine nonlinear features with low-rank tensor representations to model complex relationships efficiently. However, selecting an appropriate tensor rank remains challenging, as conventional rank-search methods require training multiple candidate models, increasing computational costs. In this work, we focus on a canonical polyadic (CP) tensor network parameterization and propose GB-CPKM, a gradient boosting framework that builds a higher-capacity predictor by sequentially adding fixed-rank learners. This approach provides a new perspective on rank selection by incrementally increasing model capacity, with ensemble size selected based on validation performance rather than through explicit rank search. Experiments on real-world regression benchmarks show that GB-CPKM trains up to 6x faster and uses up to 2x less peak memory than a conventional rank-selection method based on cross-validation, while achieving comparable predictive performance. These results highlight the potential of gradient boosting to improve the computational efficiency and scalability of tensor-network learning.
title: Gradient Boosting for Efficient Rank Discovery in Tensor Network Kernel Machines

summary: Real-time voice agents need a speech recognizer that never waits for future audio and whose memory per call does not grow with the length of the call. We present E-Gaborformer, a strictly causal encoder that combines Gated DeltaNet-2 recurrent layers with sliding-window attention in a 3:1 ratio, and builds every temporal convolution from a fixed dictionary of causal Gabor atoms. Its streaming state is constant, about 19 MB per call at production scale including the prediction network, where a causal-attention encoder of the same size accumulates over 1 GB after ten minutes. In a controlled causal study on LibriSpeech, E-Gaborformer leaves the initial plateau earlier, reaches a given accuracy up to 18% sooner, and matches or beats an E-Branchformer trained with the identical front end and recipe. At production scale, a 0.6B-parameter Hebrew and English streaming transducer built on E-Gaborformer has 28 to 31% lower word error rate (WER) than NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 ASR Streaming, a model of the same size, on English voice-agent traffic, and up to 20% lower Hebrew WER than our previous production system. The same weights serve strictly causal and 480 ms-lookahead decoding with no loss in accuracy, and a two-class formulation of the RNN-T lattice trains the transducer 2.6x faster with exact loss and gradients.
title: Gabor Gabor: E-Gaborformer, a Strictly Causal Speech Recognizer with Gabor-Dictionary Convolutions and Delta-Rule Memory

summary: Efficient deployment of large language models (LLMs) on mobile devices requires balancing performance with compute and memory constraints. Post-training compression is an effective approach to managing this trade-off, while requiring much less computation than in-training counterparts. We propose DictLLM, a dictionary-based compression scheme in which weight matrices within grouped layers are decomposed into a shared dictionary and layer-specific sparse coefficients, directly obtained from a pre-trained model without further training. Specifically, we cast DictLLM as a four-step post-training optimization. First, we obtain shared dictionaries via singular value decomposition (SVD) of input-scaled weight matrices, amortizing rank across grouped layers; second, we sparsify the layer-specific coefficients to the target compression ratio using a dictionary-aware Hessian; and third, we refine the dictionaries given the resulting sparse coefficients. Finally, we aggressively quantize both components using factor-specific Hessian information: input covariance for the dictionaries and the dictionary-aware Hessian for the coefficients. The resulting representation reduces memory footprint by storing a single shared dictionary per layer group, along with sparse layer-specific coefficients. On language modeling and zero-shot reasoning benchmarks, DictLLM consistently outperforms existing post-training low-rank compression methods and pushes the Pareto frontier between model size and performance. DictLLM compresses the original LLaMA-7B model by 5.1x with only a 2.9-point increase in WikiText-2 perplexity, achieving a 3.6x higher compression ratio than the state-of-the-art low-rank method.
title: DictLLM: Post-training Compression of Large Language Model with Dictionary Kernels

summary: Reconstructing turbulent flow fields from sparse and irregular measurements remains challenging because the underlying inverse problem is severely underdetermined. Here we present MANTRA, a manifold-based tensor framework that represents each velocity component in a continuous tensor-product space while constraining its coefficient tensor to a low-rank Tucker manifold. This structure provides a compact, data-adaptive representation without requiring gridded observations or governing equations. Riemannian optimization and adaptive selection of rank and basis complexity enable the model to exploit coordinate-wise spatiotemporal correlations. In simulations of forced isotropic turbulence and flow over a cylinder, MANTRA recovers multiscale structures at sampling densities orders of magnitude below the underlying grids and remains accurate under Gaussian noise up to 20% of the peak velocity. It also recovers leading coordinate-wise correlation structures from sparse observations. Applied to experimental particle-tracking velocimetry of an oscillating impinging jet, MANTRA reveals time-evolving structures that are not apparent from the scattered measurements alone.
title: Low-Rank Tensor Manifolds for Turbulent Field Reconstruction from Sparse Data

summary: AI agents store text as embedding vectors and compress them at scale. A compression is accepted when each item's nearest neighbors survive, but agents also consolidate, delete, and compare memories, tasks that depend on which items lie far apart. We evaluate both ends with two label-free fidelities from our prior work: the local fidelity $L$ at 10 neighbors and the global fidelity $G$ at 30 to 50 percent of the memory. At 96 bytes per passage, rescored binary codes reach an $L$ of 0.97 yet move 10.1 percent of passages to another theme; PCA with 8-bit codes, at an $L$ of 0.77, moves 1.7 percent. Rescoring leaves the stored codes, and thus $G$, unchanged. We prove that across the $G$ band, $1-ν_k$ is at most 2 to 2.18 times the square root of the near-far rank-violation rate, and that this rate follows the distance noise of the compression (correlation 0.979). Our locality-aware quantization (LAQ) turns the bound into a hinge objective on the codebooks of an OPQ index, keeping its bytes, rotation, and search. To our knowledge, LAQ is the first quantizer whose objective comes from a proven bound on the far end. Reconstruction alone raises $G$ in 0 of 52 held-out runs; the far hinge raises it in all 52. LAQ raises $G$ in all 52 ($p=8.5\times 10^{-4}$ over 13 memory-encoder groups), including the external FinDER memory, has the highest $G$ of seven equal-size quantizers in all 12 Multi-Doc-2025 runs, scales to a million passages, and keeps evidence recall.
title: Enhancing Local and Global Structure in Compressed AI Agent Memory

summary: Semantic communication (SemCom) using a relay node is considered, where the relay assists in conveying task-relevant information from a source to a destination, with meaning defined by classification labels. A joint end-to-end design of the source encoder, relay transformation, and destination decoders is developed to optimize both semantic inference accuracy and perceptual reconstruction quality for image data. Relay-assisted schemes are shown to outperform direct transmission, with gains that become more pronounced in low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) regimes across different relaying strategies. Alongside these performance benefits, however, a key security vulnerability introduced by the relay is identified, and a Byzantine attack is formulated in which the relay injects structured, learned perturbations into its transmitted signal. The attack operates on intermediate communication representations subject to channel effects, with perturbations generated through a learned mapping applied at test time. It is shown to significantly degrade semantic inference accuracy at the destination. These results reveal a clear trade-off between SemCom gains and security risks in relay-assisted systems, motivating the need for secure relay designs that account for insider threats.
title: AI-Native Task-Oriented Semantic Communications over a Relay: Benefits and Vulnerabilities

summary: Multi-agent LLM systems explore in parallel by spawning sub-agents with isolated context windows, whereas single-agent systems append every search and verification step into one growing trajectory. However, existing multi-agent frameworks duplicate prefix KV caches across branches, exchange findings by re-prefilling text summaries, and flatten or drop cross-branch dependencies during reinforcement learning (RL). We introduce Octopus, a single-model multi-agent RL framework in which all threads share one backbone and coordinate over a GPU-resident directed acyclic graph (DAG) of KV states through five primitives (fork, read_thread, wait_threads, rewind, commit). Octopus combines three co-designed mechanisms: (1) Zero-Copy Radix Forking, which spawns branches as $\mathcal{O}(1)$ cursor views over shared physical KV pages; (2) Attention-Only KV Mounting, which mounts a sibling thread's terminal KV blocks directly into full-attention layers while bypassing linear-recurrent states (Gated DeltaNet / Mamba-2), cutting off-task hijacking by $21\times$ ($57.9\% \to 2.7\%$) while retaining $92.2\%$ of full-text mutual information at zero extra KV allocation; and (3) a Packed DAG-GRPO Trainer, which packs all episode branches into one block-sparse attention pass and assigns counterfactual branch credit via leave-one-branch-out marginal rewards. Trained end-to-end with GRPO on Qwen3.5-4B over a sparse BM25 corpus, Octopus reaches $49.6\%$ accuracy on BrowseComp-Plus ($+17.5$ points over single-agent GRPO at 143K context and $+12.5$ points over text-summary multi-agent RL) and $51.2\%$ on OpenResearcher, outperforming dense-retrieval agents up to $250\times$ larger while increasing training throughput $3.3\times$ and cutting peak KV memory $2.8\times$.
title: Octopus: One Brain, Many Branches for Latent-KV Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

summary: Abstract The Laser Cognition (LC) is a proposed multilevel theoretical framework for investigating how selective attention, conscious access, curiosity-guided inquiry, associative recruitment, and representational integration may contribute to the emergence and evaluation of novel ideas. Its central explanatory metaphor is laser illumination: a complex cognitive field contains multiple thoughts, memories, representations, and potential relationships, while a selected cognitive target receives processing priority. The framework uses this metaphor to organize a proposed mechanism linking cognitive-field activation, attentional targeting, awareness-mediated processing, focus regulation, associative recruitment, integrative recombination, candidate generation, and metacognitive evaluation. LC retains the distinction between the full theory, its default mechanism, and its canonical primary case. The primary case is the Laser-Spotlight Cognitive Genesis Case (LSCGC); the proposed default mechanism is the Laser Cognition Default Mechanism (LC-DM); and its principal operational cycle is the Laser-Guided Cognitive Integration Cycle (LGCIC). The framework is formalized using a weighted cognitive graph, a dual-route attentional-targeting model, a normalized attentional-allocation function, a focus-stability measure, an associative-recruitment equation, a cognitive-integration index, a probabilistic candidate-emergence model, and a feedback-control representation. The mathematical expressions constitute proposed model specifications, not established equations of human neural operation. Awareness, attention, curiosity, affective engagement, cognitive flexibility, and metacognitive monitoring are treated as related but conceptually distinct constructs. The architecture includes eighteen layers, a multidomain research structure, eight initial research hypotheses, explicit falsifiability requirements, a cross-system functional generalization framework, a fourteen-step research protocol, and a twenty-part manuscript structure. Human cognition is the primary explanatory domain. Applications to artificial intelligence, large language models, artificial general intelligence, and possible artificial superintelligence are framed as hypotheses about functional or computational correspondence rather than established claims of shared consciousness or identical mechanisms. LC is presented as a theory-development and validation framework. Its explanatory value, novelty, causal assumptions, parameter identifiability, empirical adequacy, and cross-domain applicability remain subject to systematic literature review, mathematical audit, empirical testing, model comparison, and replication.
tags: Laser Cognition; selective attention; awareness; cognitive illumination; cognitive integration; associative recruitment; neural-pattern integration; creativity; scientific intuition; metacognition; cybernetics; mathematical modeling; artificial intelligence.
title: THE LASER COGNITION (LC): A Multilevel Neurocognitive, Mathematical, and Cybernetic Framework of Awareness-Guided Attentional Illumination, Neural-Pattern Integration, and Novel Idea Emergence

summary: Audio textures exhibit complex temporal dynamics that are not well represented by single-scale models. We propose a multi-scale latent trajectory approach for audio texture synthesis using latent representations extracted from a pretrained neural audio codec. By decomposing latent trajectories into slow structural and fast stochastic components, we enable direct modeling and interpretation of the longterm temporal structure and fine-grained detail of audio textures. Our experiments on environmental audio textures suggest that the proposed method significantly improves audio quality over a single-scale baseline and achieves performance competitive with a latent diffusion model. Using perceptually motivated summary statistics, we demonstrate that generated continuations preserve texture identity. Through the proposed methods, we enable continuous texture generation from a given context and expose a latent structure that may support control over long-term dynamics.
title: MULTI-SCALE LATENT TRAJECTORY MODELLING FOR AUDIO TEXTURE SYNTHESIS

summary: It was shown by Braverman-Finkelberg-Nakajima that the regular perverse sheaf on the affine Grassmannian of type A is isomorphic to the ring object associated to a Gelfand-Tsetlin quiver. We use this result to identify, for any finite dimensional representation $\mathbf{N}$ of a product of general linear groups, the relative Langlands dual $(T^*\mathbf{N})^\vee$ of $T^*\mathbf{N}$ with the Coulomb branch of a suitable representation. By a result of Bellamy, this implies that $(T^*\mathbf{N})^\vee$ has symplectic singularities.
title: Symplectic singularities in Relative Langlands duality for products of general linear groups

summary: Designing healthcare strategies requires anticipating their clinical and operational consequences before implementation, a task that often relies on health system simulation. Such a simulation necessitates modeling how patient states evolve and generate care demands. However, conventional approaches typically tailor compact state transitions to a single policy question and omit history-dependent dynamics, thus requiring the redefinition of states and transitions when there is a new question that entails different clinical information. We propose to learn a patient world model from longitudinal EHRs using a neural network to provide a shared clinical representation of patient trajectories that can serve simulation questions across scenarios. Taking ICU operations as an example, we train the model on MIMIC-IV, freeze it, and couple its time-queryable predictions to shared ICU calendars, resources, and queues via scenario-specific mappings, so that one model renders admission demand, care tasks, and discharge proposals across simulations evaluating ICU bed capacity, care dispatch, and post-ICU transfer capacity. Experiments show that our model matches Markov and semi-Markov comparators in aggregate occupancy and directional responses to capacity and dispatch policies. It also reproduces policy gains from replayed observed trajectories. For patients entering the same support state from different prior trajectories, the learned representation captures a 24-h recovery difference (-6.4 predicted versus -6.7 observed percentage points), a contrast missed by compact state models, which propagates into distinct simulated care demand, queue burden, and bed use. These results indicate that a learned world model of patient dynamics has the potential to replace question-specific state models, allowing new care policies to be evaluated by reconfiguring the scenario without model rebuilding.
title: Learning a patient world model for health system simulation in intensive care

Taking ICU operations as an example, we train the model on MIMIC-IV, freeze it, and couple its time-queryable predictions to shared ICU calendars, resources, and queues via scenario-specific mappings, so that one model renders admission demand, care tasks, and discharge proposals across simulations evaluating ICU bed capacity, care dispatch, and post-ICU transfer capacity. Experiments show that our model matches Markov and semi-Markov comparators in aggregate occupancy and directional responses to capacity and dispatch policies. It also reproduces policy gains from replayed observed trajectories. For patients entering the same support state from different prior trajectories, the learned representation captures a 24-h recovery difference (-6.4 predicted versus -6.7 observed percentage points), a contrast missed by compact state models, which propagates into distinct simulated care demand, queue burden, and bed use. These results indicate that a learned world model of patient dynamics has the potential to replace question-specific state models, allowing new care policies to be evaluated by reconfiguring the scenario without model rebuilding.
title: Learning a patient world model for health system simulation in intensive care

summary: Quantization reduces the memory and bandwidth demands of large language model (LLM) inference but can degrade accuracy; offloading higher-precision data can instead stall generation. We introduce StrataFlux, a framework that challenges this tradeoff by recovering accuracy lost to low-bit weight and key-value (KV) cache quantization while retaining quantization's memory and speed advantages. StrataFlux co-designs refinement representation, selection, and delivery to make host RAM and solid-state drives useful sources of additional precision. Its selective precision streaming reduces transfer volume, overlaps delivery with computation, and reuses fetched precision across decoding steps so generation need not wait for every transfer. We evaluate 2-4-bit weights and 2-3-bit KV-cache on dedicated GPUs and unified-memory platforms. For 2-bit Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct weights, StrataFlux reduces WikiText-2 perplexity from 9.46 to 8.40 while maintaining 95.4% of the quantized base's throughput on RTX 5090. With 2-bit weights and KV, StrataFlux raises Qwen3-8B's AIME 2024/2025 accuracy from 11.0% to 47.1% at unchanged GPU memory use. At 128K context, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct with 3-bit weights and 2-bit KV achieves comparable perplexity and speed to vLLM's 4-bit AWQ weights and 8-bit KV on RTX 5090, using approximately half the GPU memory. These results show that GPU-resident precision need not set the accuracy ceiling, nor offloading-tier latency dictate decoding speed.
title: StrataFlux: Memory-Hierarchy-Native Low-Bit LLM Inference

summary: Self-attention carries a quadratic cost in token count, which limits how far Vision Transformers can scale with input resolution. We introduce SSoG, a separable sum-of-Gaussians spatial operator that replaces dense self-attention with a learned mixture of axis-factorized Gaussian kernels, reducing the per-layer cost from $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ to subquadratic in $N$. Unlike dot-product self-attention, whose Lipschitz constant is unbounded outside a compact input domain, SSoG with fixed kernels is globally Lipschitz continuous, which, via the Picard--Lindelöf theorem, guarantees that the continuous-depth variant has a unique solution on the whole integration interval, a global guarantee that dense-attention counterparts lack in general. On CIFAR-100 at $224\times224$, in a matched discrete-Transformer setting and in the continuous setting, SSoG improves Top-1 accuracy by 2.2--4.1 points across three model widths while using 8.8--16.6\% fewer parameters, with depth and training recipe held fixed. In a looped-Transformer setting, SSoG improves Top-1 accuracy by 5.4--8.1 points. We further probe inference-time scaling by evaluating on inputs up to $1024\times1024$ at matched batch size: in the continuous-depth (Neural ODE) architecture, SSoG reaches up to 154\% higher throughput and over 60\% lower peak memory than dense attention, with the gap widening as resolution grows, consistent with the difference in asymptotic cost. In the discrete and looped settings, SSoG also achieves over 30\% higher throughput than dense attention at this resolution. Together, these results establish SSoG as a practical, parameter-efficient, and theoretically grounded alternative to dense attention across discrete, weight-shared, and continuous-depth Transformer variants.
title: Beyond Quadratic Attention: Separable Gaussian Operators for ODE Vision Transformers

summary: Imagine an AI that makes so many paperclips it consumes resources needed for human life. Its measure of success has displaced the purpose that made it valuable. This failure shares an optimization structure with Goodhart's law, which arose from human monetary policy. The connection turns the question toward civilization itself. Markets became powerful by responding to dispersed knowledge and changing reality. Yet financial success can increasingly depend on accumulating claims over future production rather than expanding human possibilities. We examine that hypothesis through financial claims, asset revaluation, and housing access. The Declaration of Independence supplies a different account of purpose: life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness. Enterprises can preserve market discovery while organizing first to avoid harm, then to create human benefit, and finally to earn returns that sustain their work. Perhaps solving the paperclip problem for machines begins with solving it for ourselves.
title: The Human Paperclip Maximizer: Goodhart's Law, Financial Optimization, and the Preconditions for AI Alignment

summary: AI appears to be accelerating because its benchmark scores are accelerating. Yet the systems being measured are trained and selected through closed procedures, while useful intelligence is ultimately judged against an open-ended world. Object detection provides an unusually direct empirical test of this mismatch. The high-end conventional COCO record reviewed here reached approximately 66 average precision in 2023 and has changed little through 2026 despite sustained research, large models, new architectures, new supervision, synthetic data, prompting, and architecture search. This is not a comparison between obsolete vision technology and modern language AI: object detection now uses the same fundamental machinery—transformers, learned representations, gradient optimization, sequence prediction, and in some systems the same multimodal parameters. Pix2Seq explicitly formulates detection as language modeling; Florence-2 and PaliGemma perform both perceptual and linguistic tasks.   We develop a mathematical model of the closed/open mismatch. Let an open causal state space have effective dimension d while the information admitted by a closed optimizer lies on a codimension-one boundary. At resolution ε, the number of distinguishable open states scales as (R/ε)^d while the boundary scales as (R/ε)^(d−1). The corresponding metric-entropy ratio approaches (d−1)/d. Under a state-identification model, Fano's inequality converts this information ratio into the same asymptotic upper bound on exact identification. For a three-dimensional causal volume and its two-dimensional boundary, the result is 2/3.   The theorem is mathematical: it establishes what follows from the stated information geometry. Its application to AI is scientific: observation determines whether contemporary closed-ended systems serving open-ended objectives exhibit that geometry. The empirical record is strikingly consistent with the resulting two-thirds hypothesis. Closed language benchmarks can exceed two-thirds easily because the objective itself is closed. More reality-coupled end-to-end tasks remain much harder. Recursive self-improvement does not escape the information boundary merely by searching it more aggressively. Under the stated information constraint, additional optimization alone cannot remove the modeled limitation.
title: The Illusion of Accelerating Intelligence: Closed Optimization, Open-Ended Reality, and the Two-Thirds Limit

summary: 微型機器人採樣失敗預測極限 | Flagship 023/300 MICROROBOTIC SAMPLING FAILURE PREDICTION AT THE LIMIT STARLI Research Design Working Edition v1.3 | Author: 33 | Research Family: Flagship 13 Fission, Volume I. This nonclinical prospective research monograph examines microrobotic sampling failure prediction at the limit within traceable microrobotic handling, reference-controlled sensing, and bounded laboratory autonomy. Its core scientific question is: Can microrobotic sampling failure prediction produce a measurable, independently reconstructable gain while preserving sample or reference identity and remaining inside a preregistered physical authority envelope? The book proposes a falsifiable comparison: Under equal sample, time, energy, photon, and analysis budgets, a preregistered microrobotic sampling failure prediction architecture will improve viability without worsening handling latency or recovery fraction relative to manual micropipette isolation under blinded counting. The principal comparator is manual micropipette isolation under blinded counting. The live competing explanation is the robot selects easier targets rather than preserving samples; the hard stop is carryover exceeds the preregistered ceiling. The architecture includes 30 mathematically distinct research model plates, 82 chapters, 410 one-page investigations, 200 separate Research Gates and 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos across exactly 777 English PDF pages. Each gate underwent a documented second-pass comparison of its original design and two competing proposed variants. This is an editorial hypothesis-generation protocol, not independent scientific verification. This volume is research design only: it reports no new bench results, demonstrated clinical efficacy, validated quantum advantage or approval for human intervention. Physical consistency, causal novelty, literature completeness and performance all remain subject to independent review and experimental falsification. Its core scientific question is: Can microrobotic sampling failure prediction produce a measurable, independently reconstructable gain while preserving sample or reference identity and remaining inside a preregistered physical authority envelope? The book proposes a falsifiable comparison: Under equal sample, time, energy, photon, and analysis budgets, a preregistered microrobotic sampling failure prediction architecture will improve viability without worsening handling latency or recovery fraction relative to manual micropipette isolation under blinded counting. The principal comparator is manual micropipette isolation under blinded counting. The live competing explanation is the robot selects easier targets rather than preserving samples; the hard stop is carryover exceeds the preregistered ceiling. The architecture includes 30 mathematically distinct research model plates, 82 chapters, 410 one-page investigations, 200 separate Research Gates and 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos across exactly 777 English PDF pages. Each gate underwent a documented second-pass comparison of its original design and two competing proposed variants. This is an editorial hypothesis-generation protocol, not independent scientific verification. This volume is research design only: it reports no new bench results, demonstrated clinical efficacy, validated quantum advantage or approval for human intervention. Physical consistency, causal novelty, literature completeness and performance all remain subject to independent review and experimental falsification. summary: Integrating contemporary infill architectural projects into historical urban environments presents a delicate challenge between spatial evolution and cultural heritage preservation. Traditional visual impact assessments rely heavily on qualitative, subjective expert evaluations, often leading to procedural delays, public disputes, and compromised urban aesthetics. This paper develops a quantitative, multi-criteria methodology—termed the Visual-Spatial Adaptability Index (VSAI)—to evaluate and optimize the insertion of new architectural objects within historic urban contexts. Combining 3D volumetric viewshed analysis, 2D morphological silhouette integrity, facade solid-to-void rhythm analysis, and computational material texture matching, the VSAI framework establishes an objective metric for context-sensitive design. Empirical validation conducted across 50 infill intervention scenarios in historic urban centers demonstrates that VSAI-guided design optimization yields a 34.2% increase in expert approval consensus and a 42.1% reduction in historical view corridor occlusion compared to conventional baseline proposals. The methodology provides urban planning boards, heritage authorities, and architectural practitioners with a repeatable, transparent computational tool for sustainable heritage conservation.

summary: Benchmark data for The UNICORNE Protein Conformation Database Enables Large-Scale Benchmarking of Dynamic Structure Prediction (NeurIPS 2026, Evaluations & Datasets Track). UNICORNE-BENCH-1, the first release of the UNICORNE benchmark, is a set of multi-conformation proteins, each a single UniProt entry with at least two experimentally resolved conformations (839 evaluated; 829 after fold-quality review). This record contains the benchmark definition, the superposed ground-truth structures, the OOD60 and DOMAINMOTION calibration sets, GT×GT TM-score matrices, and per-ensemble and per-conformation scores for eight predictors (BioEMU, ESMFlow, ESMDiff, AlphaFlow, CFrandom, AFsample2, AFsample3, SPEACH_AF). Together with the code repository it reproduces every figure and table in the paper's results section. The archive's layout matches the code repository; extract it at the repository root. UNICORNE-BENCH-1.README.md lists the contents. Predicted structures and raw TM-align output are not included. Version 1.1 recomputes the maximum-displacement matrices ( max_disp_xx.npy ) after superposing with the TM-align rotation, which version 1 omitted, and updates the paper title. All other files are unchanged.
title: UNICORNE-BENCH-1: benchmark data for sequence-to-ensemble protein structure predictors

summary: We study an extremal problem involving three disks inside the unit disk. Two disks are initially placed so that they are tangent to each other and internally tangent to the unit circle. A third disk of maximum possible radius is then inserted, subject to tangency with both original disks. We prove that the minimum possible sum of the areas of the three disks is 11π/18, attained when their radii are 1/2, 1/2, and 1/3. Surprisingly, the minimizing configuration does not consist of three equal disks, despite the symmetry of the problem. Three different proofs are presented, based on Descartes' circle theorem, geometric inversion, and a parametrization using tangency points.
tags: Circle packing; Descartes' circle theorem; inversion; extremal geometry; geometric optimization
title: Three Circles in a Unit Disk: Three Solutions to an Extremal Problem

We prove that the minimum possible sum of the areas of the three disks is 11π/18, attained when their radii are 1/2, 1/2, and 1/3. Surprisingly, the minimizing configuration does not consist of three equal disks, despite the symmetry of the problem. Three different proofs are presented, based on Descartes' circle theorem, geometric inversion, and a parametrization using tangency points.

summary: This dataset supports the manuscript “Assessing the Interpretability of QM/MM Interaction Energies: A Representation-Aware Diagnostic Framework,” submitted to the Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling (ci-2026-038804). The numerical data describe three retrospective peptide–enzyme case studies: prolyl endopeptidase (PEP; primary nine-peptide electronic-energy analysis, 82 retained configurations), historical beta-secretase 1 (BACE1; 63 audited snapshots, 52 retained after cleaning), and reconstructed angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE; 131 valid QM/MM decompositions, with a distinct 73-configuration GIF/IP/LP core comparison). These data support question-specific representation diagnostics and descriptive configurational-contrast analysis; they do not establish universal applicability or external affinity-prediction performance. Version v4 adds recovered simulation input files, topology and parameter files, preparation and analysis scripts, and file-level provenance manifests. The input supplement contains 8,597 recovered source files, together with the unchanged earlier numerical archive and verification records (8,740 regular files in total). It includes GROMACS run inputs for PEP and BACE1, ACE OpenMM production configurations and Amber input files, Zn-model parameterisation/validation inputs, ORCA component inputs with their coordinate and point-charge dependencies, and separately identified sensitivity, matched-perturbation, and unsuccessful diagnostic branches. The earlier numerical archive is also retained as a separate top-level download for continuity. No scientific numerical results were changed. The computational representations differ among the case studies. Primary PEP uses mixed AMBER03/CHARMM27 production protocols and inherited embedding charges. Historical BACE1 uses dynamically selected gas-phase receptor clusters and is retained for representation auditing. Corrected ACE uses snapshot-specific electrostatic embedding with a documented receptor-QM definition. The three enzymes do not share a single fixed-fragment computational representation. The original structural-analysis program that produced the historical 4 Å contact subsets C–E was not recovered. Curated subset memberships and scripts reproducing the statistics from those memberships are provided. Additional historical provenance limitations, evidence levels, and relocated source paths are documented in the supplement README and manifests. MD trajectories and bulk simulation outputs are not included. File recovery and integrity checks do not imply that the full historical simulation workflow has been rerun in a fresh environment. Third-party force-field distribution files retain their original attribution and licensing terms.

Version v4 adds recovered simulation input files, topology and parameter files, preparation and analysis scripts, and file-level provenance manifests. The input supplement contains 8,597 recovered source files, together with the unchanged earlier numerical archive and verification records (8,740 regular files in total). It includes GROMACS run inputs for PEP and BACE1, ACE OpenMM production configurations and Amber input files, Zn-model parameterisation/validation inputs, ORCA component inputs with their coordinate and point-charge dependencies, and separately identified sensitivity, matched-perturbation, and unsuccessful diagnostic branches. The earlier numerical archive is also retained as a separate top-level download for continuity. No scientific numerical results were changed. The computational representations differ among the case studies. Primary PEP uses mixed AMBER03/CHARMM27 production protocols and inherited embedding charges. Historical BACE1 uses dynamically selected gas-phase receptor clusters and is retained for representation auditing. Corrected ACE uses snapshot-specific electrostatic embedding with a documented receptor-QM definition. The three enzymes do not share a single fixed-fragment computational representation. The original structural-analysis program that produced the historical 4 Å contact subsets C–E was not recovered. Curated subset memberships and scripts reproducing the statistics from those memberships are provided. Additional historical provenance limitations, evidence levels, and relocated source paths are documented in the supplement README and manifests. MD trajectories and bulk simulation outputs are not included. File recovery and integrity checks do not imply that the full historical simulation workflow has been rerun in a fresh environment. Third-party force-field distribution files retain their original attribution and licensing terms.

summary: Fusion Pilot Plants (FPPs) need control systems that survive diagnostic and actuator failures . We present DIII-D experiments  validating real-time, ML-enabled controllers in FPP-relevant scenarios under both imposed diagnostic dropouts and real in-shot hardware failures. Conventional equilibrium reconstruction fails when key diagnostics drop out. Our ML-based RTCAKENN recovers plasma profiles under simulated failures of Thomson Scattering (TS), Charge Exchange Recombination (CER), and Motional Stark Effect (MSE) and maintains accuracies above 90%. Coordinated ML-controlled gyrotron power adjustments (>0.5MW) avoided argon accumulation and MHD-induced confinement collapse. We also accessed Resonant Magnetic Perturbation (RMP) Edge Localized Mode (ELM)-suppressed plasmas at reduced RMP coil current where large sawteeth would otherwise break ELM suppression. The approach was to reduce sawtooth magnitude (and increase frequency) by holding ECCD inside q=1. Control held through the same TS dropouts and ECH failures, with RTCAKENN providing q=1 localization while ECHO maintained aiming. These first-of-a-kind results show integrated ML-enabled fault-tolerant control sustaining FPP-relevant operating points through imposed and unscripted failures, foundational for resilient burning-plasma control.

summary: Integrating contemporary infill architectural projects into historical urban environments presents a delicate challenge between spatial evolution and cultural heritage preservation. Traditional visual impact assessments rely heavily on qualitative, subjective expert evaluations, often leading to procedural delays, public disputes, and compromised urban aesthetics. This paper develops a quantitative, multi-criteria methodology—termed the Visual-Spatial Adaptability Index (VSAI)—to evaluate and optimize the insertion of new architectural objects within historic urban contexts. Combining 3D volumetric viewshed analysis, 2D morphological silhouette integrity, facade solid-to-void rhythm analysis, and computational material texture matching, the VSAI framework establishes an objective metric for context-sensitive design. Empirical validation conducted across 50 infill intervention scenarios in historic urban centers demonstrates that VSAI-guided design optimization yields a 34.2% increase in expert approval consensus and a 42.1% reduction in historical view corridor occlusion compared to conventional baseline proposals. The methodology provides urban planning boards, heritage authorities, and architectural practitioners with a repeatable, transparent computational tool for sustainable heritage conservation.

title: DEVELOPMENT OF A METHODOLOGY FOR ASSESSING THE VISUAL AND SPATIAL ADAPTABILITY OF NEW ARCHITECTURAL OBJECTS IN HISTORICAL URBAN ENVIRONMENTS

summary: This paper proposes the Zero Principle as a philosophical and ontological framework for understanding transformation, consciousness, experience, dissolution, and the emergence of new possibilities. The central proposition is that Zero (0) should not be understood merely as mathematical nothingness . Within this framework, Zero represents an open conceptual state in which an existing form loses its claim to finality, allowing another possibility, meaning, direction, or form to emerge. The proposed structural cycle is: Form → Dissolution → 0 → Possibility → New Form At the level of human experience, the corresponding process is: Impulse → Witness → Insight → Transformation → New Direction The paper further introduces a Zero-Level Sutra : Word ≠ Truth Word → Sign → Understanding → Beyond Word → 0 The sutra proposes that words, names, colors, forms, and concepts should not automatically be treated as ultimate reality. Different philosophical traditions may use different terms—such as Brahman, Śūnyatā, Nirvāṇa, Neti-Neti, Witness, Silence, Tao, and Fana —but Vedanta 2.0 does not claim that these concepts are identical. Instead, it explores whether they can be comparatively examined at a “zero-level,” where conceptual definitions reach their limits. The paper also examines the relationship between witnessing and transformation, proposing that conscious observation can create a space between stimulus and automatic reaction. The framework is applied metaphorically to failure, loss, death, patience, faith, mystery, natural cycles, renewal, and symbolic interpretations of Diwali. The proposed structural cycle is: Form → Dissolution → 0 → Possibility → New Form At the level of human experience, the corresponding process is: Impulse → Witness → Insight → Transformation → New Direction The paper further introduces a Zero-Level Sutra : Word ≠ Truth Word → Sign → Understanding → Beyond Word → 0 The sutra proposes that words, names, colors, forms, and concepts should not automatically be treated as ultimate reality. Different philosophical traditions may use different terms—such as Brahman, Śūnyatā, Nirvāṇa, Neti-Neti, Witness, Silence, Tao, and Fana —but Vedanta 2.0 does not claim that these concepts are identical. Instead, it explores whether they can be comparatively examined at a “zero-level,” where conceptual definitions reach their limits. The paper also examines the relationship between witnessing and transformation, proposing that conscious observation can create a space between stimulus and automatic reaction. The framework is applied metaphorically to failure, loss, death, patience, faith, mystery, natural cycles, renewal, and symbolic interpretations of Diwali. The paper does not present the Zero Principle as an established scientific law. It is presented as an evolving philosophical hypothesis and conceptual framework within the broader Vedanta 2.0 project.   हिंदी यह शोध-पत्र शून्य सिद्धांत (Zero Principle) को transformation, consciousness, experience, dissolution तथा new possibilities के emergence को समझने के लिए एक दार्शनिक और ontological framework के रूप में प्रस्तुत करता है। इसका केंद्रीय प्रस्ताव यह है कि Zero (0) को केवल mathematical nothingness के रूप में नहीं समझना चाहिए । इस framework में Zero ऐसी खुली conceptual अवस्था का प्रतीक है जहाँ कोई existing form अपनी अंतिमता का दावा खो देता है और दूसरी possibility, meaning, direction या form के emergence की संभावना खुलती है। प्रस्तावित संरचनात्मक चक्र है: रूप → विसर्जन → 0 → संभावना → नया रूप मानवीय अनुभव के स्तर पर: आवेग → दृष्टा → अंतर्दृष्टि → रूपांतरण → नई दिशा Paper में एक Zero-Level Sutra भी प्रस्तावित किया गया है: शब्द ≠ सत्य शब्द → संकेत → बोध → शब्दातीत → 0 इस सूत्र का आशय है कि शब्द, नाम, रंग, रूप और अवधारणाएँ स्वयं अंतिम सत्य को सिद्ध नहीं करतीं। विभिन्न दार्शनिक परंपराएँ ब्रह्म, शून्यता, निर्वाण, नेति-नेति, दृष्टा, मौन, ताओ और फ़ना जैसे अलग-अलग शब्दों का प्रयोग करती हैं। Vedanta 2.0 यह दावा नहीं करता कि ये सभी अवधारणाएँ समान हैं; बल्कि यह जाँचता है कि क्या इन्हें एक “zero-level” पर तुलनात्मक रूप से देखा जा सकता है, जहाँ conceptual definitions अपनी सीमा तक पहुँचती हैं। Paper witnessing और transformation के संबंध का भी अध्ययन करता है तथा यह प्रस्तावित करता है कि conscious observation stimulus और automatic reaction के बीच एक space उत्पन्न कर सकती है। यह framework failure, loss, death, patience, faith, mystery, natural cycles, renewal तथा Diwali के symbolic interpretation जैसे विषयों पर भी लागू किया गया है। यह paper Zero Principle को established scientific law के रूप में प्रस्तुत नहीं करता । इसे व्यापक Vedanta 2.0 framework के भीतर एक evolving philosophical hypothesis और conceptual framework के रूप में प्रस्तुत किया गया है।
title: The Zero Principle: Witnessing, Dissolution, Transformation, and New Possibility / Hindi- शून्य सिद्धांत: दृष्टा, विसर्जन, रूपांतरण और नई संभावना

summary: Complete data workbook, analysis programme, figure scripts and output files for the manuscript on phenylacetylglutamine and beta-adrenergic cyclic nucleotide generation in isolated rat aorta. Thirty Wistar rats (15 healthy, 15 with high-fat-diet/low-dose-streptozotocin type 2 diabetes; 7 males and 8 females per group). The archive contains the nine-sheet data workbook, the analysis programme that reproduces every table, figure and reported number from it, the figure scripts, a numeric audit script, and the complete result files. Both curves of every organ-bath ring are included, so that the fixed-curve-order limitation reported in the manuscript can be verified independently. Files are restricted and available on reasonable request. Version 2.0 (7 November 2026). One correction, affecting free-text annotation only: nineteen cells of the Notes column of sheet 04_OrganBath_Tension read "Data sampled at 40 Hz"; the acquisition rate of the PowerLab 8/35 and LabChart 8 recording was 10 Hz, and those notes now read "Data sampled at 10 Hz", in agreement with the Methods section of the manuscript. The Notes column is free text and is never read by the analysis programme, so no measured value, formula or computed result is affected; every number in the results files is unchanged and the numeric audit still passes 94 of 94.
title: Data and code: phenylacetylglutamine suppresses beta-adrenergic cyclic AMP and cyclic GMP generation in intact rat aorta, in health and in type 2 diabetes

summary: Supporting research data and analysis code for an integrative study of benzo[a]pyrene-associated candidates and an MMP3 fibroblast network in ulcerative colitis. The archive contains derived analytical tables, numerical figure data, executed analysis scripts and parameters, software-version evidence, source-provenance records, 18 main/supplementary figures in native PDF/SVG, and an author-supplied conceptual graphical abstract in TIFF. Large public input matrices and third-party dependencies are obtained from the original sources identified in the provenance and run-order documentation. The documented original path and dependency requirements remain applicable; this collection is not an independently validated one-command reproduction. The results describe computational associations and virtual network responses, without establishing measured exposure effects or experimental target engagement.

summary: This code uses machine learning to predict hydrochar properties from feedstock and operating conditions. It applies NSGA-II + TOPSIS to find optimal temperature and time for three applications: energy, soil, and adsorption. Finally, it trains an inverse model to predict the best conditions for any new feedstock.

summary: Stable information geometry Normalize finite nonnegative probability weights without overflowing their sum, including joint arrays, integer totals and subnormal scales. Retain positive support in log space across the full finite-weight range, including finite KL, tiny entropy/mutual information and recoverable rare-state likelihood contributions. Define eps consistently as normalized-probability pseudocounts followed by renormalization. eps=0 preserves exact support boundaries, including infinite KL for missing reference support. Preserve subnormal support in Jensen–Shannon mixtures and smooth joint distributions once before computing mutual information marginals. Widen integral Fisher scores before products. Ordinary batches retain the floating Gram fast path; overflow-risk normalized batches use exact accumulation so unrelated small curvature is not erased. Estimate Quadray Fisher information from transformed scores; safely symmetrize and analyze large/subnormal Fisher spectra and curvature. Keep zero-posterior likelihood terms out of expected surprise while retaining genuine infinite/undefined likelihood contributions on positive support. Promote NumPy-backed Fraction numerator/denominator fields before coordinate arithmetic, exact centroids and strict inverse elimination. Signed/unsigned fields no longer wrap these exact paths. Preserve existing half-up snapped centroid and componentwise inverse contracts. Compare exact continuous centroids with symergetics alongside the five-runtime coordinate, determinant and independently enumerated FCC checks.
