summary: Stable information geometry Normalize finite nonnegative probability weights without overflowing their sum, including joint arrays, integer totals and subnormal scales. Retain positive support in log space across the full finite-weight range, including finite KL, tiny entropy/mutual information and recoverable rare-state likelihood contributions. Define eps consistently as normalized-probability pseudocounts followed by renormalization. eps=0 preserves exact support boundaries, including infinite KL for missing reference support. Preserve subnormal support in Jensen–Shannon mixtures and smooth joint distributions once before computing mutual information marginals. Widen integral Fisher scores before products. Ordinary batches retain the floating Gram fast path; overflow-risk normalized batches use exact accumulation so unrelated small curvature is not erased. Estimate Quadray Fisher information from transformed scores; safely symmetrize and analyze large/subnormal Fisher spectra and curvature. Keep zero-posterior likelihood terms out of expected surprise while retaining genuine infinite/undefined likelihood contributions on positive support. Exact geometry and suite integration Add exported centroid_exact(points) , returning a canonical four- Fraction tuple without lattice snapping, including arbitrary-size and rational inputs. Promote NumPy-backed Fraction numerator/denominator fields before coordinate arithmetic, exact centroids and strict inverse elimination. Signed/unsigned fields no longer wrap these exact paths. Preserve existing half-up snapped centroid and componentwise inverse contracts. Compare exact continuous centroids with symergetics alongside the five-runtime coordinate, determinant and independently enumerated FCC checks. summary: Grant-free uplink access in low-Earth-orbit (LEO) non-terrestrial networks (NTNs) poses a coordination challenge when multiple UEs share a satellite channel without real-time centralized scheduling under long propagation delays and time-varying channels. Conventional random access does not exploit peer context, leading to collisions and inefficient channel use as contention increases. To address this problem, we propose IRIS, a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for decentralized grant-free direct-to-satellite (D2S) uplink access, with A2A-IRIS as its sidelink-assisted Agent-to-Agent (A2A) realization. Each UE executes a shared binary transmission policy using local traffic/channel information augmented by compact peer states exchanged over UE-to-UE sidelink, while Vanilla-IRIS serves as a local-only ablation. Evaluations in rural and suburban LEO D2S deployments use TLE-based trajectories propagated using the Simplified General Perturbations 4 (SGP4), with a Walker-Delta constellation as fallback. A2A-IRIS achieves 2.1579 and 5.4478 Mbps, corresponding to 99.9% and 96.1% of the respective scenario-specific upper bounds. Relative to Vanilla-IRIS, throughput improves by 40.8% and 325.0%, with collision rates of 0.0000 and 0.0433, while one- and two-epoch delayed centralized schedulers are outperformed by approximately 51--130%. A2A-IRIS also improves fairness, service coverage, and transmission efficiency with moderate Deep Q-Network (DQN) inference overhead. Active-UE load scalability results further show sustained performance over the evaluated load range. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of sidelink-assisted A2A coordination for decentralized LEO D2S uplink access under propagation delay and delayed channel feedback.
title: IRIS: Intelligent Random Access with Integrated Shared Learning for Decentralized LEO Direct-to-Satellite Uplinks

summary: Multi-agent LLM systems explore in parallel by spawning sub-agents with isolated context windows, whereas single-agent systems append every search and verification step into one growing trajectory. However, existing multi-agent frameworks duplicate prefix KV caches across branches, exchange findings by re-prefilling text summaries, and flatten or drop cross-branch dependencies during reinforcement learning (RL). We introduce Octopus, a single-model multi-agent RL framework in which all threads share one backbone and coordinate over a GPU-resident directed acyclic graph (DAG) of KV states through five primitives (fork, read_thread, wait_threads, rewind, commit). Octopus combines three co-designed mechanisms: (1) Zero-Copy Radix Forking, which spawns branches as $\mathcal{O}(1)$ cursor views over shared physical KV pages; (2) Attention-Only KV Mounting, which mounts a sibling thread's terminal KV blocks directly into full-attention layers while bypassing linear-recurrent states (Gated DeltaNet / Mamba-2), cutting off-task hijacking by $21\times$ ($57.9\% \to 2.7\%$) while retaining $92.2\%$ of full-text mutual information at zero extra KV allocation; and (3) a Packed DAG-GRPO Trainer, which packs all episode branches into one block-sparse attention pass and assigns counterfactual branch credit via leave-one-branch-out marginal rewards. Trained end-to-end with GRPO on Qwen3.5-4B over a sparse BM25 corpus, Octopus reaches $49.6\%$ accuracy on BrowseComp-Plus ($+17.5$ points over single-agent GRPO at 143K context and $+12.5$ points over text-summary multi-agent RL) and $51.2\%$ on OpenResearcher, outperforming dense-retrieval agents up to $250\times$ larger while increasing training throughput $3.3\times$ and cutting peak KV memory $2.8\times$.
title: Octopus: One Brain, Many Branches for Latent-KV Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

summary: Wellbore stability analysis is an essential part of well planning where mechanical characteristics of rocks and the state of in-situ stresses are determined to evaluate the likelihood of borehole failure during drilling. In this study, natural and drilling induced fractures were characterized using image logs for a fractured reservoir located in Southern Iran. Mechanical Earth Modeling (MEM) and wellbore stability analysis were also carried out by the combination of wireline log data and in-situ measurements for a vertical well drilled in this field. The obtained results indicated the presence of several major/minor fractures in the studied interval but majority of them were found to be closed fractures. According to the MEM, formations would suffer from breakout (shear failure) in several intervals which might be linked to their low strengths, huge stress anisotropy and inappropriate selection of the mud weight. Give then fact that the break-out failure obtained from the Mogi-Coulomb criterion had a match with the borehole failure captured by the caliper log, the geomechanical parameters estimated through the methodology proposed should have sufficient accuracy and can be used for the stability analysis of other wells drilled in the same field.
title: Natural fracture characterization and wellbore stability analysis of a highly fractured southwestern Iranian oilfield

F052   Diamond NV-Center Neural Magnetometry at the Limit Primary endpoint: noise-equivalent magnetic sensitivity [T/sqrt(Hz)]. Hidden perturbation: blinded fluorescence count-rate swap. Hidden perturbation: blind removal of one magnetometer channel. Rival: interpolation smoothing or favorable source depth, rather than improved resolution. F055   Quantum-Assisted Neural Magnetic Field Inversion at the Limit Primary endpoint: magnetic source localization error [mm]. Hidden perturbation: concealed head-phantom conductivity swap. Rival: regularization choice or favored source prior generates an apparent localization gain. summary: Thermal Quantum Annealing (tQuA) is a quantum architecture in which a system coupled non-adiabatically to a thermodynamic reservoir evolves toward the ground state of a target Hamiltonian . This paper provides a rigorous and honest foundation for tQuA and its extension to Quantum Intelligent Matrix Methods (QIMM). We distinguish carefully among Theorems (proved in cited literature), Propositions (proof sketches with explicitly identified gaps), and Conjectures (claims with open steps). This work delivers three principal contributions: Convergence Proof Chain: We present a five-pillar proof chain establishing that tQuA converges to the global minimum from any initial state, without adiabatic scheduling, without eigenstate knowledge, and with a strictly positive escape rate from every local minimum at any . Honest Scaling Benchmarks: We present scaling benchmarks for the Liouvillian spectral gap   on gopherhole Hamiltonians, reporting a key finding: fixed-schedule tQuA achieves a perfectly flat gap ( , independent of   up to ) when the number of local minima   is fixed and small, but experiences steep polynomial decay ( ) when   grows proportionally to . Adaptive Policy Framework: Third, we outline a rich adaptive annealing policy framework using observed function evaluations and prior probability distributions   over problem classes, framing it as a primary research direction for future empirical tuning.   The framework applies broadly to nonconvex optimization in artificial intelligence, signal processing, and imaging, with specific application to "seeing the sky" technologies described in the companion paper on intensity-correlation interferometry (Hyland & Werbos 2024).
tags: thermal quantum annealing, open quantum systems, Lindblad master equation, spectral gap, adaptive annealing policy, gopherhole landscape, quantum matrix methods, classical-quantum equivalence, Gibbs state, nonconvex optimization
title: Analytic Foundations of Thermal Quantum Annealing: Convergence Guarantees and Computational Advantage for Quantum Matrix Methods

summary: In standard multi-head attention, every head uses the same query, key, and value (QKV) projection matrices for every token. We study a simple variant in which, in every layer, a subset of the heads are token-specific: their QKV projections depend on the identity of the input token, while the remaining heads keep ordinary shared projections. Token-specific projections are parameterized as a shared matrix plus a per-token low-rank correction stored in a hashed lookup table, so the extra computation is small, although the parameter count grows. In GPT-style language models trained on FineWeb, with 2 of 4 heads per layer token-specific, every run had lower validation loss than every standard-attention run, at both of the scales we tested. At the larger of two scales (6 layers, width 512, 300M training tokens, 3 seeds per method), validation loss fell from 4.154 ± 0.005 to 4.107 ± 0.008, a 4.6% reduction in perplexity. A control that adds the same number of lookup-table parameters to the same heads as per-token vectors, rather than per-token matrix corrections, reached only 4.148 ± 0.002, indicating that the gain is not explained by the additional parameters alone. At the smaller scale, a sweep over the number of token-specific heads suggests that mixing token-specific and shared heads works at least as well as making all heads token-specific. The main cost is throughput: our unoptimized implementation trains about 30% slower than the baseline. These are small-scale results, and we discuss their limitations in detail.
title: Token-Specific Attention Heads: Mixing Per-Token and Shared Query, Key, and Value Projections in Transformer Language Models

summary: Supplementary data for an experiment that replaced the larva segmentation model of the Tenebrio molitor behavioral-phenotyping pipeline while every downstream step (Petri geometry, primary-larva selection, continuity gate, interpolation, smoothing, features, quality control) was held fixed. Five segmenters were compared: the YOLO11s-seg used for the v1.0.0 dataset, YOLOv8s-seg, YOLO26s-seg and Mask R-CNN R50-FPN v2 trained on full tray images, and a YOLO11s-seg trained on Petri crops. The crop-trained model was then applied to all 34 videos and the Results analysis repeated. On Petri crops, the input the pipeline processes, mask mAP@0.5 was 0.10 for the full-tray YOLO11s and 0.99 for the crop-trained YOLO11s and Mask R-CNN; on 79 held-out labelled video frames larva recall was 0.69, 0.99 and 0.96. The two ground-truth-accurate models agreed with each other (CCC 0.91–0.99 on distance, speed, edge fraction, entropy and area). Heat contrasts kept their direction on the 34 videos. Contents: configuration, protocol and results documents, held-out accuracy, ground-truth localization, the 12-video comparison (agreement, equivalence, per-configuration features and QC), the 34-video re-run with the crop-trained model, treatment contrasts and provenance. Model weights are not included. The values are objective behavioral proxies and do not measure welfare or any subjective state.
title: Tenebrio molitor behavioral phenotyping dataset: segmenter comparison supplementary data

summary: Abstract The Laser Cognition (LC) is a proposed multilevel theoretical framework for investigating how selective attention, conscious access, curiosity-guided inquiry, associative recruitment, and representational integration may contribute to the emergence and evaluation of novel ideas. Its central explanatory metaphor is laser illumination: a complex cognitive field contains multiple thoughts, memories, representations, and potential relationships, while a selected cognitive target receives processing priority. The framework uses this metaphor to organize a proposed mechanism linking cognitive-field activation, attentional targeting, awareness-mediated processing, focus regulation, associative recruitment, integrative recombination, candidate generation, and metacognitive evaluation. LC retains the distinction between the full theory, its default mechanism, and its canonical primary case. The primary case is the Laser-Spotlight Cognitive Genesis Case (LSCGC); the proposed default mechanism is the Laser Cognition Default Mechanism (LC-DM); and its principal operational cycle is the Laser-Guided Cognitive Integration Cycle (LGCIC). The framework is formalized using a weighted cognitive graph, a dual-route attentional-targeting model, a normalized attentional-allocation function, a focus-stability measure, an associative-recruitment equation, a cognitive-integration index, a probabilistic candidate-emergence model, and a feedback-control representation. The mathematical expressions constitute proposed model specifications, not established equations of human neural operation. Awareness, attention, curiosity, affective engagement, cognitive flexibility, and metacognitive monitoring are treated as related but conceptually distinct constructs. The architecture includes eighteen layers, a multidomain research structure, eight initial research hypotheses, explicit falsifiability requirements, a cross-system functional generalization framework, a fourteen-step research protocol, and a twenty-part manuscript structure. Human cognition is the primary explanatory domain. summary: Abstract The Laser Cognition (LC) is a proposed multilevel theoretical framework for investigating how selective attention, conscious access, curiosity-guided inquiry, associative recruitment, and representational integration may contribute to the emergence and evaluation of novel ideas. Its central explanatory metaphor is laser illumination: a complex cognitive field contains multiple thoughts, memories, representations, and potential relationships, while a selected cognitive target receives processing priority. The framework uses this metaphor to organize a proposed mechanism linking cognitive-field activation, attentional targeting, awareness-mediated processing, focus regulation, associative recruitment, integrative recombination, candidate generation, and metacognitive evaluation. LC retains the distinction between the full theory, its default mechanism, and its canonical primary case. The primary case is the Laser-Spotlight Cognitive Genesis Case (LSCGC); the proposed default mechanism is the Laser Cognition Default Mechanism (LC-DM); and its principal operational cycle is the Laser-Guided Cognitive Integration Cycle (LGCIC). The framework is formalized using a weighted cognitive graph, a dual-route attentional-targeting model, a normalized attentional-allocation function, a focus-stability measure, an associative-recruitment equation, a cognitive-integration index, a probabilistic candidate-emergence model, and a feedback-control representation. The mathematical expressions constitute proposed model specifications, not established equations of human neural operation. Awareness, attention, curiosity, affective engagement, cognitive flexibility, and metacognitive monitoring are treated as related but conceptually distinct constructs. summary: This archive contains the code, derived data, and results of the study " Reported or observed? Satellite-mapped flood exposure reveals a reporting gap that machine-learned impact models inherit."  The study compares the number of people reported as affected by floods in EM-DAT with the population living inside the inundation mapped by MODIS in the Global Flood Database, for 1,266 country-level flood records from 2000 to 2018. It measures how the ratio of reported to observed impact depends on the reporting country at equal hazard, including floods that cross borders; tests whether ridge and gradient-boosting impact models trained on reported labels inherit this dependence; evaluates transfer across continents with importance weighting, the area of applicability and (weighted, Mondrian) conformal prediction; and shows how a small fraction of satellite labels removes most of the inherited bias. Results are expressed in the relative economic value of impact-based warnings. Contents. scripts/: the complete Python pipeline, including Google Earth Engine extraction of observed labels, ex-ante exposure (GHSL, GloFAS, MERIT Hydro) and ERA5-Land forcing on administrative footprints (steps 10-15), statistical and machine-learning analyses (steps 20-25), and figure scripts (steps 30-32). jobs/: the SLURM batch script used on the national supercomputer of Côte d'Ivoire and an equivalent local runner. data/: derived tables at the level of the EM-DAT record (observed exposure and flooded area, quality fractions, exposure and landscape predictors, hydroclimatic forcing, country covariates, EM-DAT-GFD links), GFD event metadata, study regions and a Natural Earth base map. results/: all result tables of the paper (2,000 cluster-bootstrap draws). README.md explains how to reproduce every result and figure. EM-DAT data are not redistributed, in accordance with the CRED terms of use. The derived tables carry only the EM-DAT identifier, country code and year. Users can download the public EM-DAT export of 11 May 2026 from https://www.emdat.be and rebuild the analysis table with two scripts; with that export the rebuilt table is identical to the one used in the paper. Code is released under the MIT licence; derived data and results under CC BY 4.0, without prejudice to the licences of the source products (Global Flood Database, ERA5-Land, GHSL, GloFAS, MERIT Hydro, FAO GAUL, World Bank indicators, Natural Earth).

summary: Data and analysis code for a mixed-method, between-subjects user study comparing SQL-LLM, a natural-language database interface backed by GPT-4o, with Snowflake, a conventional SQL editor. Twenty SQL-literate participants each completed 12 querying tasks drawn from the BIRD Text-to-SQL benchmark across three relational schemas (Books, Mondial Geo, Legislator), with screen recordings, think-aloud protocols, and timing logs. The package contains the raw study inputs (cleaned timing/SQL spreadsheet, hand-coded behavioral proxies, 11 think-aloud transcripts, per-participant notebooks and reports), derived and graded artifacts (execution-based correctness grades, three LLM-judge grades, BIRD gold answers, model/timing CSVs, LLM inter-coder reliability files), and the full analysis pipeline (figure notebook, execution grader, gold-answer fetcher, difficulty-validation and effect-size scripts). See README.md for the layout and steps. The BIRD gold SQLite databases are not included but are regenerated from the public BIRD train split via the provided script. Code is released under the MIT License; data files under CC BY 4.0.
title: Replication Package: Natural Language Interfaces for Databases — What Changes for Users? (SQL-LLM vs. Snowflake User Study)

summary: Audio textures exhibit complex temporal dynamics that are not well represented by single-scale models. We propose a multi-scale latent trajectory approach for audio texture synthesis using latent representations extracted from a pretrained neural audio codec. By decomposing latent trajectories into slow structural and fast stochastic components, we enable direct modeling and interpretation of the longterm temporal structure and fine-grained detail of audio textures. Our experiments on environmental audio textures suggest that the proposed method significantly improves audio quality over a single-scale baseline and achieves performance competitive with a latent diffusion model. Using perceptually motivated summary statistics, we demonstrate that generated continuations preserve texture identity. Through the proposed methods, we enable continuous texture generation from a given context and expose a latent structure that may support control over long-term dynamics.
title: MULTI-SCALE LATENT TRAJECTORY MODELLING FOR AUDIO TEXTURE SYNTHESIS

summary: Аннотация. В статье представлен комплексный лингвистический и историко-дипломатический анализ письма вице-губернатора крепости Анапа Сеид-Махмуда Мусселима от 29 марта 1817 года, которое адресовано русскому адмиралу Алексею Самуиловичу Грейгу. Этот документ рассматривается как важнейшее локальное историческое открытие, который на данный момент формирует вокруг себя уникальный контекст пограничной российско-османской коммуникации и одновременно вписывается в макроконтекст реализации условий Бухарестского мирного договора 1812 г. В ходе исследования подробно изучена композиционная структура документа, выявлены системные графические, орфографические и грамматические девиации во французском тексте. Исследование позволяет реконструировать уровень османских адъютантов и специфику функционирования французского языка как инструмента дипломатии.   Abstract. The article presents a complex linguistic and historical-diplomatic analysis of the letter of the vice-governor of the fortress Anapa Seyid-Mahmud Mousselim dated 29 March 1817, which was addressed to the Russian admiral Alexey Samuilovitch Greig. This document is regarded as the most important local historical discovery, which at the moment forms around it a unique context of the Russian border -Ottoman communication and at the same time fits into the macro context of the implementation of the terms of the Treaty of Bucharest (1812). In the course of the study, the compositional structure of the document was thoroughly examined, systematic graphical, orthographic, and grammatical deviations in the French text were identified. The study allows for a reconstruction of the level of Ottoman adjutants and the specificity of the functioning of the French language as an instrument of diplomacy.
title: ЛИНГВИСТИЧЕСКИЕ ИНТЕРФЕРЕНЦИИ И ПРАГМАТИКА ДИПЛОМАТИЧЕСКОГО ДИСКУРСА В РОССИЙСКО-ОСМАНСКОЙ КОРРЕСПОНДЕНЦИИ НАЧАЛА XIX ВЕКА (НА МАТЕРИАЛЕ ПИСЬМА ИЗ АНАПЫ А.С. ГРЕЙГУ)

title: sdos: order-N spectral density of states for large sparse Hermitian problems

summary: Interpretations have been widely used in the study of provenance of queries on semiring-annotated databases. Here, we consider two different interpretation-based semantics for first-order formulas in negation normal form, namely, the canonical-interpretation semantics and the compatible-interpretation semantics. We show that the resulting query languages cannot express the monus operation on semiring-annotated relations, when the annotations come from the bag semiring or the tropical semiring or the fuzzy semiring. Consequently, the semantics of SQL cannot be captured using the interpretation-based semantics considered here.
title: Monus vs. Interpretations in Semiring Semantics

summary: Supplementary dataset for three pre-registered buyer-side experiments verifying x402 v2 payments on Base mainnet, executed as scripted protocol runs and committed regardless of outcome; every reported number traces to a committed analysis.json and raw artifacts under experiments/ . Experiment 1: echo-verify A fresh USD 0.01 mainnet happy-path settlement, verified end-to-end via payer-anchored Transfer events on two independent RPCs (paid run 1.11 s; discovery median 0.0388 s over 15 GETs; tx 0xa3143d32319392227c017ce86dceb2a8e377b7e4f32c21f2693a6925e91f201c ). Headline finding: exactly 0.01 USDC settled to payTo per Transfer events on both RPCs. Experiment 2: mock-seller Hostile-seller failure-mode detection, including a same-nonce EIP-3009 replay on an Anvil fork pinned at block 54035433. Headline finding: 4 of 4 hostile-seller failure modes were correctly detected; the replay reverted at EVM state level with FiatTokenV2: authorization is used or canceled . summary: Analysis and figure-generation code for the manuscript "[title]". The code demonstrates, on a public dataset of student teaching evaluations, why comparing a section's mean rating to a department average is statistically invalid, and shows how the power to detect a real difference collapses at small sample sizes. Scripts: turkiye_simulation_NREP5000.py (Monte Carlo power/breakpoint analysis), turkiye_leaveoneout_analysis.py (structure and leave-one-out benchmark comparisons), turkiye_make_all_figures.py (figures). See README for versions and seeds. Data: Türkiye Student Evaluation dataset (Gündüz & Fokoue), UCI ML Repository ID 262, DOI 10.24432/C5S02S, CC BY 4.0. Not redistributed here; retrieved from UCI at run time. Reproducibility: all draws seeded; results stable to <1 percentage point at NREP = 5000; fast Mann–Whitney routine validated against scipy to machine precision. Requirements: Python 3 with numpy, pandas, scipy, matplotlib, ucimlrepo. License: [MIT/BSD-3-Clause]. Please cite both this code and the dataset (DOI 10.24432/C5S02S). Code is released under the MIT License; figures and documentation are released under CC BY 4.0.

summary: Designing healthcare strategies requires anticipating their clinical and operational consequences before implementation, a task that often relies on health system simulation. Such a simulation necessitates modeling how patient states evolve and generate care demands. However, conventional approaches typically tailor compact state transitions to a single policy question and omit history-dependent dynamics, thus requiring the redefinition of states and transitions when there is a new question that entails different clinical information. We propose to learn a patient world model from longitudinal EHRs using a neural network to provide a shared clinical representation of patient trajectories that can serve simulation questions across scenarios. Taking ICU operations as an example, we train the model on MIMIC-IV, freeze it, and couple its time-queryable predictions to shared ICU calendars, resources, and queues via scenario-specific mappings, so that one model renders admission demand, care tasks, and discharge proposals across simulations evaluating ICU bed capacity, care dispatch, and post-ICU transfer capacity. Experiments show that our model matches Markov and semi-Markov comparators in aggregate occupancy and directional responses to capacity and dispatch policies. It also reproduces policy gains from replayed observed trajectories. For patients entering the same support state from different prior trajectories, the learned representation captures a 24-h recovery difference (-6.4 predicted versus -6.7 observed percentage points), a contrast missed by compact state models, which propagates into distinct simulated care demand, queue burden, and bed use. These results indicate that a learned world model of patient dynamics has the potential to replace question-specific state models, allowing new care policies to be evaluated by reconfiguring the scenario without model rebuilding.
title: Learning a patient world model for health system simulation in intensive care

summary: Self-attention carries a quadratic cost in token count, which limits how far Vision Transformers can scale with input resolution. We introduce SSoG, a separable sum-of-Gaussians spatial operator that replaces dense self-attention with a learned mixture of axis-factorized Gaussian kernels, reducing the per-layer cost from $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ to subquadratic in $N$. Unlike dot-product self-attention, whose Lipschitz constant is unbounded outside a compact input domain, SSoG with fixed kernels is globally Lipschitz continuous, which, via the Picard--Lindelöf theorem, guarantees that the continuous-depth variant has a unique solution on the whole integration interval, a global guarantee that dense-attention counterparts lack in general. On CIFAR-100 at $224\times224$, in a matched discrete-Transformer setting and in the continuous setting, SSoG improves Top-1 accuracy by 2.2--4.1 points across three model widths while using 8.8--16.6\% fewer parameters, with depth and training recipe held fixed. In a looped-Transformer setting, SSoG improves Top-1 accuracy by 5.4--8.1 points. We further probe inference-time scaling by evaluating on inputs up to $1024\times1024$ at matched batch size: in the continuous-depth (Neural ODE) architecture, SSoG reaches up to 154\% higher throughput and over 60\% lower peak memory than dense attention, with the gap widening as resolution grows, consistent with the difference in asymptotic cost. In the discrete and looped settings, SSoG also achieves over 30\% higher throughput than dense attention at this resolution. Together, these results establish SSoG as a practical, parameter-efficient, and theoretically grounded alternative to dense attention across discrete, weight-shared, and continuous-depth Transformer variants.
title: Beyond Quadratic Attention: Separable Gaussian Operators for ODE Vision Transformers

summary: Imagine an AI that makes so many paperclips it consumes resources needed for human life. Its measure of success has displaced the purpose that made it valuable. This failure shares an optimization structure with Goodhart's law, which arose from human monetary policy. The connection turns the question toward civilization itself. Markets became powerful by responding to dispersed knowledge and changing reality. Yet financial success can increasingly depend on accumulating claims over future production rather than expanding human possibilities. We examine that hypothesis through financial claims, asset revaluation, and housing access. The Declaration of Independence supplies a different account of purpose: life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness. Enterprises can preserve market discovery while organizing first to avoid harm, then to create human benefit, and finally to earn returns that sustain their work. Perhaps solving the paperclip problem for machines begins with solving it for ourselves.
title: The Human Paperclip Maximizer: Goodhart's Law, Financial Optimization, and the Preconditions for AI Alignment

summary: AI appears to be accelerating because its benchmark scores are accelerating. Yet the systems being measured are trained and selected through closed procedures, while useful intelligence is ultimately judged against an open-ended world. Object detection provides an unusually direct empirical test of this mismatch. The high-end conventional COCO record reviewed here reached approximately 66 average precision in 2023 and has changed little through 2026 despite sustained research, large models, new architectures, new supervision, synthetic data, prompting, and architecture search. This is not a comparison between obsolete vision technology and modern language AI: object detection now uses the same fundamental machinery—transformers, learned representations, gradient optimization, sequence prediction, and in some systems the same multimodal parameters. Pix2Seq explicitly formulates detection as language modeling; Florence-2 and PaliGemma perform both perceptual and linguistic tasks.   We develop a mathematical model of the closed/open mismatch. Let an open causal state space have effective dimension d while the information admitted by a closed optimizer lies on a codimension-one boundary. At resolution ε, the number of distinguishable open states scales as (R/ε)^d while the boundary scales as (R/ε)^(d−1). The corresponding metric-entropy ratio approaches (d−1)/d. Under a state-identification model, Fano's inequality converts this information ratio into the same asymptotic upper bound on exact identification. For a three-dimensional causal volume and its two-dimensional boundary, the result is 2/3.   The theorem is mathematical: it establishes what follows from the stated information geometry. Its application to AI is scientific: observation determines whether contemporary closed-ended systems serving open-ended objectives exhibit that geometry. The empirical record is strikingly consistent with the resulting two-thirds hypothesis. Closed language benchmarks can exceed two-thirds easily because the objective itself is closed. More reality-coupled end-to-end tasks remain much harder. Recursive self-improvement does not escape the information boundary merely by searching it more aggressively. Under the stated information constraint, additional optimization alone cannot remove the modeled limitation.
title: The Illusion of Accelerating Intelligence: Closed Optimization, Open-Ended Reality, and the Two-Thirds Limit

summary: Integrating contemporary infill architectural projects into historical urban environments presents a delicate challenge between spatial evolution and cultural heritage preservation. Traditional visual impact assessments rely heavily on qualitative, subjective expert evaluations, often leading to procedural delays, public disputes, and compromised urban aesthetics. This paper develops a quantitative, multi-criteria methodology—termed the Visual-Spatial Adaptability Index (VSAI)—to evaluate and optimize the insertion of new architectural objects within historic urban contexts. Combining 3D volumetric viewshed analysis, 2D morphological silhouette integrity, facade solid-to-void rhythm analysis, and computational material texture matching, the VSAI framework establishes an objective metric for context-sensitive design. Empirical validation conducted across 50 infill intervention scenarios in historic urban centers demonstrates that VSAI-guided design optimization yields a 34.2% increase in expert approval consensus and a 42.1% reduction in historical view corridor occlusion compared to conventional baseline proposals. The methodology provides urban planning boards, heritage authorities, and architectural practitioners with a repeatable, transparent computational tool for sustainable heritage conservation.
tags: Historical urban environment, Visual-spatial adaptability, Infill architecture, Viewshed analysis, Urban morphology, Heritage conservation, IMRAD
title: DEVELOPMENT OF A METHODOLOGY FOR ASSESSING THE VISUAL AND SPATIAL ADAPTABILITY OF NEW ARCHITECTURAL OBJECTS IN HISTORICAL URBAN ENVIRONMENTS

summary: Benchmark data for The UNICORNE Protein Conformation Database Enables Large-Scale Benchmarking of Dynamic Structure Prediction (NeurIPS 2026, Evaluations & Datasets Track). UNICORNE-BENCH-1, the first release of the UNICORNE benchmark, is a set of multi-conformation proteins, each a single UniProt entry with at least two experimentally resolved conformations (839 evaluated; 829 after fold-quality review). All other files are unchanged.

summary: We study an extremal problem involving three disks inside the unit disk. Two disks are initially placed so that they are tangent to each other and internally tangent to the unit circle. A third disk of maximum possible radius is then inserted, subject to tangency with both original disks. We prove that the minimum possible sum of the areas of the three disks is 11π/18, attained when their radii are 1/2, 1/2, and 1/3. Surprisingly, the minimizing configuration does not consist of three equal disks, despite the symmetry of the problem. Three different proofs are presented, based on Descartes' circle theorem, geometric inversion, and a parametrization using tangency points.
tags: Circle packing; Descartes' circle theorem; inversion; extremal geometry; geometric optimization
title: Three Circles in a Unit Disk: Three Solutions to an Extremal Problem

summary: This dataset supports the manuscript “Assessing the Interpretability of QM/MM Interaction Energies: A Representation-Aware Diagnostic Framework,” submitted to the Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling (ci-2026-038804). The numerical data describe three retrospective peptide–enzyme case studies: prolyl endopeptidase (PEP; primary nine-peptide electronic-energy analysis, 82 retained configurations), historical beta-secretase 1 (BACE1; 63 audited snapshots, 52 retained after cleaning), and reconstructed angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE; 131 valid QM/MM decompositions, with a distinct 73-configuration GIF/IP/LP core comparison). These data support question-specific representation diagnostics and descriptive configurational-contrast analysis; they do not establish universal applicability or external affinity-prediction performance. Version v4 adds recovered simulation input files, topology and parameter files, preparation and analysis scripts, and file-level provenance manifests. The input supplement contains 8,597 recovered source files, together with the unchanged earlier numerical archive and verification records (8,740 regular files in total). It includes GROMACS run inputs for PEP and BACE1, ACE OpenMM production configurations and Amber input files, Zn-model parameterisation/validation inputs, ORCA component inputs with their coordinate and point-charge dependencies, and separately identified sensitivity, matched-perturbation, and unsuccessful diagnostic branches. The earlier numerical archive is also retained as a separate top-level download for continuity. No scientific numerical results were changed. The computational representations differ among the case studies. Primary PEP uses mixed AMBER03/CHARMM27 production protocols and inherited embedding charges. Historical BACE1 uses dynamically selected gas-phase receptor clusters and is retained for representation auditing. Corrected ACE uses snapshot-specific electrostatic embedding with a documented receptor-QM definition. The three enzymes do not share a single fixed-fragment computational representation. The original structural-analysis program that produced the historical 4 Å contact subsets C–E was not recovered. Curated subset memberships and scripts reproducing the statistics from those memberships are provided. Additional historical provenance limitations, evidence levels, and relocated source paths are documented in the supplement README and manifests. MD trajectories and bulk simulation outputs are not included. File recovery and integrity checks do not imply that the full historical simulation workflow has been rerun in a fresh environment. Third-party force-field distribution files retain their original attribution and licensing terms.

summary: Simulated OCO-2 soundings and everything needed to reproduce the amortized probabilistic retrieval described in the accompanying paper. Version 3 adds the operational a priori of every reference sounding in February, March and July 2020 (oco2_apriori.tar.gz): the a priori state vector and its covariance, and the a priori XCO 2 and its pressure-weighting function. These are the prior baselines added to the paper in its second revision. Every other archive is unchanged from version 2. Version 2 adds, to the February 2020 delivery already in version 1: the reference-disjoint, within-reference, all-February and training-size split tables, each with the standardization constants estimated from its own training partition (oco2_splits.tar.gz); the trained checkpoints of all six models on each of the three splits reported in the paper (oco2_model_weights_v2.tar.gz); the two held-out months, March and July 2020, as the archives the scoring jobs consumed — spectra, ACOS profile covariances, covariates and the month split table (oco2_month_202003_full.tar.gz, oco2_month_202007_full.tar.gz); and the per-sounding predictive artifacts from which every table and figure in the paper is regenerated without a GPU (oco2_scoring_artifacts.tar.gz). Version 1's archives are included unchanged. oco2_model_weights.tar.gz is the original submission's checkpoints, kept for provenance and superseded by the _v2 archive. The paper's numbers come from the reference-disjoint split table group_split_v1_cov.csv and the _v2 weights. CONTENTS.md describes each archive and SHA256SUMS.txt covers all of them. The code that reads them is at https://github.com/acallesalda/oco2-amortized-uq, archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22667577 ; scripts/get_data.sh downloads, verifies and unpacks everything to the paths the code expects. The simulation experiment, its a priori and the operational ACOS L2FP retrievals were produced at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, California Institute of Technology.
title: Simulated OCO-2 data, split tables, trained model weights, and predictive artifacts for amortized probabilistic CO2 retrieval

These are the prior baselines added to the paper in its second revision. Every other archive is unchanged from version 2. Version 2 adds, to the February 2020 delivery already in version 1: the reference-disjoint, within-reference, all-February and training-size split tables, each with the standardization constants estimated from its own training partition (oco2_splits.tar.gz); the trained checkpoints of all six models on each of the three splits reported in the paper (oco2_model_weights_v2.tar.gz); the two held-out months, March and July 2020, as the archives the scoring jobs consumed — spectra, ACOS profile covariances, covariates and the month split table (oco2_month_202003_full.tar.gz, oco2_month_202007_full.tar.gz); and the per-sounding predictive artifacts from which every table and figure in the paper is regenerated without a GPU (oco2_scoring_artifacts.tar.gz). Version 1's archives are included unchanged. oco2_model_weights.tar.gz is the original submission's checkpoints, kept for provenance and superseded by the _v2 archive. The paper's numbers come from the reference-disjoint split table group_split_v1_cov.csv and the _v2 weights. CONTENTS.md describes each archive and SHA256SUMS.txt covers all of them. The code that reads them is at https://github.com/acallesalda/oco2-amortized-uq, archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22667577 ; scripts/get_data.sh downloads, verifies and unpacks everything to the paths the code expects. The simulation experiment, its a priori and the operational ACOS L2FP retrievals were produced at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, California Institute of Technology.
title: Simulated OCO-2 data, split tables, trained model weights, and predictive artifacts for amortized probabilistic CO2 retrieval

summary: Fusion Pilot Plants (FPPs) need control systems that survive diagnostic and actuator failures . We present DIII-D experiments  validating real-time, ML-enabled controllers in FPP-relevant scenarios under both imposed diagnostic dropouts and real in-shot hardware failures. Conventional equilibrium reconstruction fails when key diagnostics drop out. Our ML-based RTCAKENN recovers plasma profiles under simulated failures of Thomson Scattering (TS), Charge Exchange Recombination (CER), and Motional Stark Effect (MSE) and maintains accuracies above 90%. ECHO, a fault-robust ML controller, coordinates electron cyclotron heating (ECH) by reallocating gyrotron power s and steering across surviving gyrotrons when units fail mid-shot. In a Hybrid scenario with real ECH dropouts, we mitigated heavy-Z impurity accumulation (argon proxy) using core ECH power tracking a real-time ML radiated-power (Bolo-NN) model for pumpout , and Electron Cyclotron Current Drive (ECCD) steering onto the 3/2 tearing mode for MHD amplitude control. Coordinated ML-controlled gyrotron power adjustments (>0.5MW) avoided argon accumulation and MHD-induced confinement collapse. We also accessed Resonant Magnetic Perturbation (RMP) Edge Localized Mode (ELM)-suppressed plasmas at reduced RMP coil current where large sawteeth would otherwise break ELM suppression. The approach was to reduce sawtooth magnitude (and increase frequency) by holding ECCD inside q=1. Control held through the same TS dropouts and ECH failures, with RTCAKENN providing q=1 localization while ECHO maintained aiming. These first-of-a-kind results show integrated ML-enabled fault-tolerant control sustaining FPP-relevant operating points through imposed and unscripted failures, foundational for resilient burning-plasma control.
title: ML-Enabled Fault Resistant Plasma Control on DIII-D

summary: This paper proposes the Zero Principle as a philosophical and ontological framework for understanding transformation, consciousness, experience, dissolution, and the emergence of new possibilities. The central proposition is that Zero (0) should not be understood merely as mathematical nothingness . Within this framework, Zero represents an open conceptual state in which an existing form loses its claim to finality, allowing another possibility, meaning, direction, or form to emerge. The proposed structural cycle is: Form → Dissolution → 0 → Possibility → New Form At the level of human experience, the corresponding process is: Impulse → Witness → Insight → Transformation → New Direction The paper further introduces a Zero-Level Sutra : Word ≠ Truth Word → Sign → Understanding → Beyond Word → 0 The sutra proposes that words, names, colors, forms, and concepts should not automatically be treated as ultimate reality. Different philosophical traditions may use different terms—such as Brahman, Śūnyatā, Nirvāṇa, Neti-Neti, Witness, Silence, Tao, and Fana —but Vedanta 2.0 does not claim that these concepts are identical. Instead, it explores whether they can be comparatively examined at a “zero-level,” where conceptual definitions reach their limits. The paper also examines the relationship between witnessing and transformation, proposing that conscious observation can create a space between stimulus and automatic reaction. The framework is applied metaphorically to failure, loss, death, patience, faith, mystery, natural cycles, renewal, and symbolic interpretations of Diwali. The paper does not present the Zero Principle as an established scientific law. It is presented as an evolving philosophical hypothesis and conceptual framework within the broader Vedanta 2.0 project.   हिंदी यह शोध-पत्र शून्य सिद्धांत (Zero Principle) को transformation, consciousness, experience, dissolution तथा new possibilities के emergence को समझने के लिए एक दार्शनिक और ontological framework के रूप में प्रस्तुत करता है। इसका केंद्रीय प्रस्ताव यह है कि Zero (0) को केवल mathematical nothingness के रूप में नहीं समझना चाहिए । इस framework में Zero ऐसी खुली conceptual अवस्था का प्रतीक है जहाँ कोई existing form अपनी अंतिमता का दावा खो देता है और दूसरी possibility, meaning, direction या form के emergence की संभावना खुलती है। प्रस्तावित संरचनात्मक चक्र है: रूप → विसर्जन → 0 → संभावना → नया रूप मानवीय अनुभव के स्तर पर: आवेग → दृष्टा → अंतर्दृष्टि → रूपांतरण → नई दिशा Paper में एक Zero-Level Sutra भी प्रस्तावित किया गया है: शब्द ≠ सत्य शब्द → संकेत → बोध → शब्दातीत → 0 इस सूत्र का आशय है कि शब्द, नाम, रंग, रूप और अवधारणाएँ स्वयं अंतिम सत्य को सिद्ध नहीं करतीं। विभिन्न दार्शनिक परंपराएँ ब्रह्म, शून्यता, निर्वाण, नेति-नेति, दृष्टा, मौन, ताओ और फ़ना जैसे अलग-अलग शब्दों का प्रयोग करती हैं। Vedanta 2.0 यह दावा नहीं करता कि ये सभी अवधारणाएँ समान हैं; बल्कि यह जाँचता है कि क्या इन्हें एक “zero-level” पर तुलनात्मक रूप से देखा जा सकता है, जहाँ conceptual definitions अपनी सीमा तक पहुँचती हैं। Paper witnessing और transformation के संबंध का भी अध्ययन करता है तथा यह प्रस्तावित करता है कि conscious observation stimulus और automatic reaction के बीच एक space उत्पन्न कर सकती है। यह framework failure, loss, death, patience, faith, mystery, natural cycles, renewal तथा Diwali के symbolic interpretation जैसे विषयों पर भी लागू किया गया है। यह paper Zero Principle को established scientific law के रूप में प्रस्तुत नहीं करता । इसे व्यापक Vedanta 2.0 framework के भीतर एक evolving philosophical hypothesis और conceptual framework के रूप में प्रस्तुत किया गया है।
title: The Zero Principle: Witnessing, Dissolution, Transformation, and New Possibility / Hindi- शून्य सिद्धांत: दृष्टा, विसर्जन, रूपांतरण और नई संभावना

summary: Complete data workbook, analysis programme, figure scripts and output files for the manuscript on phenylacetylglutamine and beta-adrenergic cyclic nucleotide generation in isolated rat aorta. Thirty Wistar rats (15 healthy, 15 with high-fat-diet/low-dose-streptozotocin type 2 diabetes; 7 males and 8 females per group). The archive contains the nine-sheet data workbook, the analysis programme that reproduces every table, figure and reported number from it, the figure scripts, a numeric audit script, and the complete result files. Both curves of every organ-bath ring are included, so that the fixed-curve-order limitation reported in the manuscript can be verified independently. Files are restricted and available on reasonable request. Version 2.0 (7 November 2026). One correction, affecting free-text annotation only: nineteen cells of the Notes column of sheet 04_OrganBath_Tension read "Data sampled at 40 Hz"; the acquisition rate of the PowerLab 8/35 and LabChart 8 recording was 10 Hz, and those notes now read "Data sampled at 10 Hz", in agreement with the Methods section of the manuscript. The Notes column is free text and is never read by the analysis programme, so no measured value, formula or computed result is affected; every number in the results files is unchanged and the numeric audit still passes 94 of 94.
title: Data and code: phenylacetylglutamine suppresses beta-adrenergic cyclic AMP and cyclic GMP generation in intact rat aorta, in health and in type 2 diabetes

summary: Exact numbers and live geometry Add SymergeticsNumber.nth_root(value, degree, max_denominator=1000000) and reuse it for sqrt . Preserve integer Fraction exponents, perfect rational roots and powers without a binary-float conversion, including huge integers, tiny fractions and negative odd roots. Promote integral scalars and NumPy-backed Fraction fields before arithmetic, comparison, roots/powers, sign normalization and coordinate snapping. Bound only irrational approximations by max_denominator ; exact roots may exceed that cap. Decimal approximation is finite precision, not certified symbolic algebra or rounding. Add polyhedron centroid_exact() compatible with QuadMath's canonical rational centroid tuple, without integer coordinate snapping. summary: Code and saved numerical results for the calibrated takeoff race in "Prizes, Shared Hazard, and the Speed of Frontier AI" (arXiv:2611.04266). The archive contains model code, saved results, generated number macros and tables, figures, and reproduction instructions. The results are conditional model calculations, not estimates of actual catastrophe probabilities. No external data are needed. This archive is a snapshot; the full pipeline was not rerun during packaging.
title: Replication Code and Results: Prizes, Shared Hazard, and the Speed of Frontier AI

summary: Supporting research data and analysis code for an integrative study of benzo[a]pyrene-associated candidates and an MMP3 fibroblast network in ulcerative colitis. The archive contains derived analytical tables, numerical figure data, executed analysis scripts and parameters, software-version evidence, source-provenance records, 18 main/supplementary figures in native PDF/SVG, and an author-supplied conceptual graphical abstract in TIFF. Large public input matrices and third-party dependencies are obtained from the original sources identified in the provenance and run-order documentation. The documented original path and dependency requirements remain applicable; this collection is not an independently validated one-command reproduction. The results describe computational associations and virtual network responses, without establishing measured exposure effects or experimental target engagement.
title: Data and code for an integrative study of benzo[a]pyrene-associated candidates and an MMP3 fibroblast network in ulcerative colitis

summary: This code uses machine learning to predict hydrochar properties from feedstock and operating conditions. It applies NSGA-II + TOPSIS to find optimal temperature and time for three applications: energy, soil, and adsorption. Finally, it trains an inverse model to predict the best conditions for any new feedstock.

summary: Final data for using and reproducing PACo-Aptamer, a ligand-conditioned RNA inverse-folding model. The package contains the final chain splits, RNA and RNA-ligand training features, the two final PACo-Aptamer ensemble checkpoints, machine-readable results used by the figure scripts, final figure assets and an example RNA structure. A per-file SHA-256 manifest is included. Source code and usage instructions: RNA_tertiary_stru_IF (MIT). This dataset is released under CC BY 4.0. Primary data originate from the RCSB Protein Data Bank, PDB Chemical Component Dictionary, AptaDB and the UTexas Aptamer Database; see the archive README for attribution.
title: Reproduction data and final model checkpoints for PACo-Aptamer

summary: Stable information geometry Normalize finite nonnegative probability weights without overflowing their sum, including joint arrays, integer totals and subnormal scales. Retain positive support in log space across the full finite-weight range, including finite KL, tiny entropy/mutual information and recoverable rare-state likelihood contributions. Define eps consistently as normalized-probability pseudocounts followed by renormalization. eps=0 preserves exact support boundaries, including infinite KL for missing reference support. Preserve subnormal support in Jensen–Shannon mixtures and smooth joint distributions once before computing mutual information marginals. Widen integral Fisher scores before products. Ordinary batches retain the floating Gram fast path; overflow-risk normalized batches use exact accumulation so unrelated small curvature is not erased. Estimate Quadray Fisher information from transformed scores; safely symmetrize and analyze large/subnormal Fisher spectra and curvature. Keep zero-posterior likelihood terms out of expected surprise while retaining genuine infinite/undefined likelihood contributions on positive support. Promote NumPy-backed Fraction numerator/denominator fields before coordinate arithmetic, exact centroids and strict inverse elimination. Signed/unsigned fields no longer wrap these exact paths. Preserve existing half-up snapped centroid and componentwise inverse contracts. Compare exact continuous centroids with symergetics alongside the five-runtime coordinate, determinant and independently enumerated FCC checks. summary: Stable information geometry Normalize finite nonnegative probability weights without overflowing their sum, including joint arrays, integer totals and subnormal scales. Retain positive support in log space across the full finite-weight range, including finite KL, tiny entropy/mutual information and recoverable rare-state likelihood contributions. Define eps consistently as normalized-probability pseudocounts followed by renormalization. eps=0 preserves exact support boundaries, including infinite KL for missing reference support. Preserve subnormal support in Jensen–Shannon mixtures and smooth joint distributions once before computing mutual information marginals. Widen integral Fisher scores before products. Ordinary batches retain the floating Gram fast path; overflow-risk normalized batches use exact accumulation so unrelated small curvature is not erased. Estimate Quadray Fisher information from transformed scores; safely symmetrize and analyze large/subnormal Fisher spectra and curvature. Keep zero-posterior likelihood terms out of expected surprise while retaining genuine infinite/undefined likelihood contributions on positive support. summary: Supporting code and derived tables for the manuscript "Diagnosing an Operational Ground Snow-Load Ensemble over South Korea  Without Snow-Water-Equivalent Measurements: Mass Provenance, Calibration Exposure, and Member Redundancy" (Cha, Kim, Park and Lee), submitted to Earth and Space Science.   The archive contains the precipitation mass-balance model,the SNOWPACK configuration and patch used  for the two energy-balance members, the analysis and parameter-sweep scripts that generate every number  and figure in the paper, and the derived station-winter tables for 97 stations and the 30 winters 1996/97 to 2025/26. summary: Background: : Adverse drug reactions (ADRs) are an important concern in clinical practice and can lead to treatment failure, hospitalization and increased healthcare costs. Genetic variations among individuals can influence drug-metabolizing enzymes, transport proteins and drug targets, resulting in differences in drug response and susceptibility to toxicity. Pharmacogenomics (PGx) provides an approach to understanding these genetic differences and supporting personalized drug therapy. Objective: To systematically evaluate the role of pharmacogenomics in predicting and preventing adverse drug reactions, with particular emphasis on clinically relevant gene–drug interactions and pharmacogenomics-guided treatment outcomes. Methods: : A systematic literature review will be conducted using databases including PubMed, Google Scholar, and the Cochrane Library. Relevant studies will be identified using keywords such as pharmacogenomics, pharmacogenetics, adverse drug reactions, genetic polymorphism, drug toxicity and personalized medicine. Studies investigating associations between genetic variations, medication-related adverse reactions and genotype-guided prescribing will be considered. Study selection and reporting will follow PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Expected results: The review is expected to identify clinically important gene–drug associations, evaluate the evidence supporting pharmacogenomics-guided prescribing and examine its potential to reduce medication-related toxicity. It will also explore challenges associated with implementing pharmacogenomic testing in routine clinical practice. Conclusion: : Pharmacogenomics has the potential to improve medication safety by identifying individuals at increased risk of specific adverse drug reactions. Its effective implementation requires reliable genetic testing, clinical interpretation, healthcare professional education and accessible prescribing guidelines.
title: Role of Pharmacogenomics in Predicting and Preventing Adverse Drug Reactions: A Systematic Review of Gene–Drug Interactions and Clinical Outcomes

summary: Files supporting a preregistered external test of one fixed eight-gene transcript module (writer8: POMGNT2, POMK, B3GALNT2, FKTN, FKRP, RXYLT1, B4GAT1, LARGE1; the enzymes that build matriglycan on alpha-dystroglycan) in public human and rodent skeletal-muscle transcriptomes of disuse, recovery and training. The protocol (version 1.0) and Amendment A1 were registered on OSF before the search, screening and any access to expression data (https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/GDVJH); Amendments A2 and A3 were registered before data access (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23204360). The post hoc plans, Amendments A4 and A5, were added to the registration before the parts that read expression data again were run (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23851939 and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23855491). The archive holds the result tables of the registered analysis (pooled estimates, gates, multiplicity families, per-comparison effect sizes, leave-one-cohort-out, composition sensitivity, alternative arms, gene-level description, per-unit scores, descriptive comparisons), the registered analysis code with its synthetic tests, the data readers and download manifests with the SHA-256 of every input, the read-reprocessing record (nf-core/rnaseq 3.27.0, Salmon, Ensembl 116), the search, screening and extraction records with the author's confirmation and adjudication workbooks, the exposure log of every data access after registration, and the scripts that build the tables, figures and reference table of the accompanying article. Version 2.0 adds the post hoc analyses, which are not registered and not blind and change no registered result: Amendment A4 Part 1 (from the registered result files), Part 2 (programmes, an expression-matched random gene-set null, alternative scores and ranking universes) and the three checks of Amendment A5, each with its code, synthetic tests, outputs, manifest and run record; the record of a post hoc scan of public glycoproteomics data; and the scripts and outputs of the tables and figures of the second version of the article. The scoring code of version 1.0.0 (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22884854) is required to rerun the analysis. Not included: expression data (all public at GEO, ArrayExpress/ENA and MoTrPAC; fetch scripts and checksums are included), the manuscript text, and the Methods sections of source publications read during verification. MANIFEST.sha256 lists the SHA-256 of every file; README.md describes the contents and how to reproduce the article's tables and figures. Version 1.0 was prepared but never published; this is the first public version. Version v3.0 (2026-11-07) adds the record of the checks run after the second editorial decision (post-reject/analysis/round3_2026-11-07/: the reproduction gate R0 of the registered pooled estimates, the plans frozen with SHA-256 digests before each check, the post hoc checks R2 to R6 with their result tables, receipts and code, the draft of Amendment A6 with its metadata-only search record, and the data-access log of that round) and the scripts, number-provenance table, figures and supporting-information tables of the third version of the article (post-reject/manuscript-v3/). The files of the registered analysis and of v2.0 are unchanged. The checks of v3.0 are not registered and not blind; they carry no gate and change no registered result.
title: Preregistered reanalysis of a dystroglycan glycan-biosynthesis transcript score in disuse, recovery and training: result tables, analysis code and screening records

summary: A sixth-generation (6G) mobile network must share the radio resources of each base station among services with different requirements for delay, throughput, and energy use. Radio access network (RAN) slicing addresses this problem by allocating radio resources among logically separated services, and increasingly autonomous controllers are proposed to manage these allocations. Two proposed enhancements are a learned meta-agent that adjusts the controller’s configuration and a quantum optimizer for difficult discrete allocation decisions. Here we examine when these enhancements add value beyond strong classical controls using SHARP, a safety-preserving multi-cell RAN slicing controller whose per-slot capacity constraint is enforced independently of the added optimization layers. The meta-agent is evaluated against the best static parameter setting and the controller’s built-in adaptation. Its learned policy selects the same value in every observed state, so in deployment it coincides with a fixed setting (V = 3) and does not outperform the best static setting; its role is to locate that setting without a manual sweep. Relative to the default setting inherited from the host study, the located setting improves slot-level power-budget compliance by five to ten percentage points during constrained regimes at a one to two percent goodput cost, while the controller’s Lyapunov virtual queue already provides long-run adaptation of the power constraint. For the discrete allocation problem, plain QAOA does not outperform the classical baselines. Warm-started QAOA with a rotated mixer shows improvement only in the rugged regime evaluated here: it incurs no observed losses to the greedy seed in 48 comparisons and strictly improves six of 16 instances under the IBM-Heron-calibrated noise model, increasing normalized frame utility from 0.927 to 0.941. This gain is measured in frame utility rather than delivered goodput, and its attribution to quantum sampling remains unresolved because a matched classical seeded-perturbation control is not included. The greedy solution remains the fallback when the quantum device does not return within the planning deadline. We therefore formulate a controllerspecific break-even condition relating the expected utility gain, device availability, and quantum-dispatch cost, and derive the corresponding hardware requirements. All results are simulation outputs; no quantum hardware is executed and no quantum advantage is claimed.
title: Bounding the benefit of agentic meta-adaptation and quantum-assisted optimization for safe multi-cell 6G radio access network slicing

summary: Higgs-pair production through gluon fusion is sensitive both to the Higgs self-coupling and to additional scalars exchanged in the s channel. We compute gg → hh at leading order in QCD in the CP-conserving two-Higgs-doublet model with Yukawa alignment (A2HDM), keeping the full top-quark mass dependence and every interference term among the box, the light-Higgs triangle and the heavy-scalar triangle. Previous A2HDM studies of heavy scalars decaying to Higgs pairs used the narrow-width approximation. We contrast two benchmark points. When the heavy scalar H decouples from the top-quark loop, the modified couplings of h weaken the destructive box–triangle interference, and the 13 TeV cross section rises to 1.27 times the Standard Model value without any resonance. For m_H = 300 GeV, below the ttbar threshold, the cross section reaches 3.69 times the Standard Model value; interference with the continuum changes the integrated resonant contribution by only about 4%, but turns the parton-level m_hh distribution into a peak–dip structure. The two mechanisms are therefore separated by the shapes of the m_hh and p_T spectra rather than by the rate. Both benchmarks are illustrative and satisfy a simplified set of theoretical and experimental constraints. Code: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24029211

title: Interference and resonance effects in gluon-fusion Higgs-pair production in the Yukawa-aligned two-Higgs-doublet model

summary: First release of Main Street Highways: an open, segment-level dataset of fatal crashes (FARS 2015-2024) on state and U.S. highways in and near 15,195 U.S. towns under 10,000 people (lower 48 states). Each highway is split into town center, rest of town, and outside town (0-5 miles), with 2024 HPMS traffic. 72,301 segments and 39,300 matched fatal crashes. Code, provenance log, quality report, codebook, limitations, and verification records are included. Data and documents: CC BY 4.0. Code: MIT.

summary: This replication package accompanies the paper "Design Principles for Engineering Multi-Agent Systems for Automated Procedure Cleansing: An Action Design Research Study at ASML" The study applied Action Design Research over three Build–Intervention–Evaluation (BIE) cycles (Alpha, Beta, and Final) to design and evaluate an LLM-based multi-agent system that cleanses industrial procedures against ASML's internal Standard of Procedures (SoP) and ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English. ASML procedure documents are proprietary and are not included.

summary: Full autosomal meta-analysis summary statistics (5,372,439 variants) from the two-cohort inverse-variance meta-GWAS of coded infantile haemangioma (Million Veteran Program European-ancestry and FinnGen R13 ICD-10 D18.0; 13,417 cases total). Columns (17): key, rsid, beta_fg, se_fg, p_fg, beta_mvp, se_mvp, se_route, p_mvp, beta_meta, se_meta, z, p_meta, Q_heterogeneity, same_dir, af_fg, af_mvp. Allele orientation follows the source MVP and FinnGen published dictionaries (no explicit EA/OA column). Data supporting the manuscript 'Transfer, not discovery: cross-cohort meta-analysis of coded haemangioma confirms CASP8...' (IH-A). Source cohorts: MVP and FinnGen R13, each under their own ethics approvals and data access policies; this deposit contains only de-identified aggregate summary statistics

summary: The analytical dataset, extraction provenance and analysis code for a study of how the cross-validation splitting rule affects machine-learning performance reported on literature-compiled membrane data. 452 canonical CO2/N2 measurements from 75 open-access studies published 2020-2026. Every value carries the page it was read from, a content hash and the DOI of its source. A panel of models was evaluated under cross-validation grouped by source study, and one random forest was also evaluated under a random row split. Version 1.0.2 replaces the dataset of version 1.0.1 with the one the manuscript analyses: rows found ineligible in review were removed, four studies outside the stated membrane scope were excluded, and measurements printed twice under different sample names were merged (sample_aliases.json). It adds the fold assignments and out-of-fold predictions for both splitting rules, the review decisions and analyses, and the analysis code with its notebook. Contents: adjudication.json : contradictions and how each was resolved analysis_code.zip : analysis code, the notebook, and the exact library versions audit_draw.json : the random audit: the sample, recorded before any row was seen audit_log.jsonl : the random audit: one verdict per row, with the time it was given audit_result.json : the random audit: agreement and the error-rate bound citation_table.csv : every value attributed to its source DOI dataset.csv : the analytical dataset exclusion_decisions.json : the post-review decision on each flagged row, who made it, and the page quotation it rests on expansion_protocol.json : the preregistered expansion protocol extraction_model.json : the extraction model's architecture, read from its files fulltext_decisions.csv : the screening ledger human_decisions.csv : the researcher's corrections leakage_diagnostic.json : the grouped-versus-random comparison over five seeds model_summary.csv : every model's grouped cross-validation result, all cohorts observations.csv : pre-canonicalisation observations oof_predictions_primary.csv : outer-fold assignments and every model's out-of-fold prediction reconciliation.json : counts and losses at every stage from search hit to analytical row reviewer_checks.json : sensitivity analyses added in review rights_decisions.csv : the release decision recorded for each source study rights_ledger.csv : the rights ledger rights_manifest.json : what was released and withheld, with the dataset checksum sample_aliases.json : measurements a study printed twice under different sample names, merged into one row, with the source quotation for each secondary_permeability.json : CO2 permeability as a secondary target, added in review source_repairs.json : the sentence justifying each repair split_comparison_predictions.csv : fold assignments and predictions under the grouped and the random split study_reconciliation.csv : the outcome of every study screened at full text validation_report.json : the extraction quality-control report, page by page No source PDF, rendered page image or figure reproduced from a source is included. Each study is identified by DOI so that it can be retrieved from its publisher under that publisher's terms. 14 studies released their extracted values but not the short sentences quoted as evidence, because their licence could not be established or is not a Creative Commons licence; those sentences are marked as withheld in the files and listed in rights_manifest.json. Every analysed row is present, so the deposit reproduces the analysis reported in the manuscript.

summary: This code-only release supports an exploratory comparison of regional genetic signal sharing between the INTERVAL CD55 protein assay and sepsis phenotypes from UK Biobank and the Million Veteran Program. It includes frozen numerical functions, a portable replay interface, synthetic tests, and documentation of source-specific access terms. No original GWAS summary-statistic files, per-variant real-data inputs, or participant-level records are included. Replaying the manuscript's numerical results requires the frozen intermediate inputs described in the README and input manifest. This release is not a complete end-to-end source-data reconstruction pipeline. The software uses Python and base R 4.6.0 and is distributed under the MIT License.

summary: Flagship 55/60 Can randomized or justified quasi-experimental intervention isolate the manufacturing effect from cell-lot, material and culture confounding? CAUSAL VERIFICATION AND COUNTERFACTUAL CONTROL IN NANOROBOT-ASSISTED REGENERATIVE MANUFACTURING AT THE LIMIT This 777-page Research Design Working Edition in the STARLI Nano Regenerative Biomanufacturing series investigates intervention-defined causal treatment contrast rather than observational association. Its scientific coupling is causal inference x microscale interventions x biological functional validation. The evidence perimeter is prospective and nonclinical, using closed in-vitro systems, organ-on-chip platforms or authorized ex-vivo material; neither clinical efficacy nor autonomous human intervention is claimed. The falsifiable question is: Can randomized or justified quasi-experimental intervention isolate the manufacturing effect from cell-lot, material and culture confounding? The proposed minimum demonstration is: Randomize tool action within balanced chip batches, retain sham and medium-only controls, and repeat on a second platform. Strong comparators include correlational predictor, nonrandomized matched cohort and randomized sham manipulation. The central competing explanation is shared medium, selection, interference or time-dependent confounding. The noncompensatory stop rule is: negative controls exhibit the claimed effect or modest unmeasured confounding reverses it. Every eligible, stopped, refused and unsuccessful experiment belongs to the full denominator. Thirty conditional mathematical plates specify different analytic roles, measurements, units and blind failure tests. Eighty-two chapters contain 410 individual research investigations. Two hundred Research Gates organize twenty causal challenge families across ten primary physical observables, each with an independently read companion, concealed intervention, matched comparator, explicit rival and refusal gate. Thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos propose future experimental and evidence instruments. All are experimental plans rather than executed observations. The source Atlas and methodology ancestors provide reference architecture but do not establish the new integrated candidate. Source-supplied ancestry includes 10.5281/zenodo.23046134 and 10.5281/zenodo.23486020; source-associated external DOI candidates must be bibliographically checked before citation. Research Gate lexical differentiation is not proof of scientific originality. The PDF is English-only and a separate QA record states outstanding independent physics, biology and DOI verification. summary: Research companion for the manuscript "Does Better Feature Coverage Improve SAR Ship Classification? A Controlled Study under Limited Labels". This archive contains materials that support inspection and numerical verification of the reported results: source-code snapshots, training and development image-identifier lists, frozen training-subset lists, protocol and provenance records, archived development logs, existing aggregate score tables, the statistical implementation, and figure materials. Not included: original SAR imagery, original provider metadata, third-party pretrained weights, trained checkpoint payloads, per-image held-out labels and predictions, held-out partition identifiers, and unpublished exact weighting diagnostics. NASTaR and FUSAR-Ship remain subject to their own provider terms; this archive does not redistribute them and grants no rights over them.
