summary: The rational management of water resources and the control of hydroagricultural techniques in the Oued Souf area are complex and crucial to a harmonious and sustainable development. The Oued Souf area is presently facing the problem of upwelling from groundwater, which is harmful to cultures and homes. In order to minimize this problem, several aerated lagoon treatment plants were set up; this technique allows an efficient control of pollution due especially to the upwelling phenomenon. The aim of this study is to provide information about the efficiency and the management of an aerated lagoon treatment system at two plants of the Oued Souf area, the Hassani Abdelkrim and the Reguiba plants. The obtained results show that the removal efficiency of organic load is significant (greater than 50%), thus indicating that aerated lagoon system is well suited to arid areas. published by the   Journal of Biodiversity and Environmental Sciences | JBES
title: Treatment of domestic and agricultural water by natural lagoon system in arid areas, case of Oued Souf, Algeria

summary: Abstract This document gives a technical and functional description of Algorithmic Logic Fingerprints (ALF): a way to verify that an AI model or algorithm in production still makes the decisions that were reviewed and approved, and to stop its output from taking effect if it does not. The problem. Current AI trust mechanisms prove identity and origin, not behaviour: Model signing (OpenSSF Model Signing, led by Google, NVIDIA and HiddenLayer; NVIDIA NGC signed models) proves which file a model is. Attestation and transparency logs (for example Apple Private Cloud Compute) prove which software a server runs. Neither shows what the model actually decides. A model can be fine-tuned, quantised, wrapped in a prompt or proxy layer, or replaced behind the same name or signature, and an AI agent can act on its output before anyone notices. How it works. Fingerprint generation. A compact cryptographic fingerprint of decision behaviour is created without access to source code, model weights or training data. For machine-learning models it is built by sampling decision boundaries. For rule-based or traditional code it is built from normalised control-flow and decision structure. Sealed-probe verification. In the highest-assurance mode, the model is tested with a sealed set of inputs that the computing system cannot see in advance. Four views must match together: decision boundaries, monotonicity and consistency, constraint activation, and constraint topology. A different model wrapped to imitate the approved one cannot pass all four. Approved-fingerprint registry. Each approved model or algorithm version has a reference fingerprint that can be checked at any time. Run-time check at the point of effect. Inside a trusted execution environment (for example a confidential VM or a confidential GPU), the live fingerprint is compared with the approved one after computation finishes and before the output is used. Fail-closed enforcement. If the fingerprint does not match, approval is automatically invalidated and the output is withheld. The capability needed to act (send, pay, move, transmit) is not released. Validation receipts. Each decision produces a tamper-evident receipt anchored in a ledger, for audit and incident analysis. Where it applies. The same mechanism applies to AI agents and model-serving platforms, payment and digital-currency systems (including offline wallets), vehicles and robots, and satellites. It complements existing technology rather than replacing it: model signing and model registries (NVIDIA NGC, Google Kaggle); verifiable and confidential AI clouds (Apple Private Cloud Compute, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, AWS, and NVIDIA, Intel and AMD confidential hardware); agent platforms (Google, Microsoft, Amazon Web Services); payment flows (Visa, Mastercard, PayPal, Ant Group); vehicle software governance under UN Regulation 156; Chinese AI platforms (Alibaba, Baidu, ByteDance, Tencent, Huawei, Zhipu AI). It also gives a technical signal for the EU AI Act's substantial-modification rule and for China's generative AI filing regime, both of which depend on knowing whether the deployed system is the one that was assessed. Source disclosure. The related application PCT/IB2026/055615 (filed 4 June 2026, publicly disclosed 16 July 2026) claims priority from it. Author: Sangam Das. summary: This article examines a method for developing students' chemical language through digital storytelling. The proposed methodological solution involves a sequence of activities in which students not only create a digital story but also translate the content of a chemical phenomenon from its observed form into a verbal explanation, a microcosm model, and a symbolic notation. The method includes setting up a chemical situation, identifying the linguistic core of the topic, a sequential description of the process, peer review of the scenario, creation of a digital story, and reverse transformation of the information. To evaluate the results, criteria for terminological and symbolic accuracy, understanding of the meaning of chemical notation, logical explanation, and coherence of chemical language are identified. The proposed approach can be used in studying exchange reactions, electrolytic dissociation, oxidation-reduction, and organic reactions.
tags: chemical language, digital storytelling, chemical symbols, nomenclature, chemical formulas, reaction equations, chemistry teaching.
title: METHOD OF DEVELOPING CHEMICAL LANGUAGE IN STUDENTS BASED ON DIGITAL STORYTELLING

summary: Reproducibility package for the manuscript "Right Ventricular Function and the Mechanical Power–Mortality Gradient During Invasive Ventilation: A Candidate Echo-Informed Ventilator Tolerance Phenotype." Contents: SQL extraction queries (Charlson comorbidity index; plateau-pressure–based "strict" mechanical power), Python analysis code (primary logistic models with stratum-specific estimates and multiplicative interaction; adjustment ladder; RERI; RV-stratified restricted cubic splines; simulation-based power analysis; main-effects-versus-interaction decomposition), and aggregate-level derived results. No patient-level data are included; source data (MIMIC-IV, MIMIC-IV-ECHO, and the hour-resolution respiratory-support dataset) are available to credentialed users via PhysioNet. summary: Analysis package for a study of copy-specific assignment at the two 23S rRNA copies of Helicobacter pylori . The package contains the seventeen supplementary tables, the analysis and figure code, the recorded software versions, the reconstruction log for the long-read alignments, and a per-read phase-evidence table. What is reproducible. The six-criterion classification of 103 matched isolates is re-runnable and every verdict was re-derived from the counts with zero mismatches. The reference metadata for all cited works is captured from Europe PMC and every DOI was verified against its record. The figures are generated by script and each passes a programmatic overlap, clipping and text-on-line audit before export. The short-read counts at the two A2143 coordinates are reproduced from the archived alignment, whose header records the exact command and tool versions. What is not. The original NCBI query string and its date were not retained, so the cohort cannot be rebuilt verbatim; per-accession inclusion flags are given instead. The barrnap installation originally used on the analysis machine is missing a Perl module and does not run; the rRNA copy numbers were therefore archived values in earlier versions and are re-derived with barrnap 1.10.5 in this version. The original parameter sets for two of the three long-read procedures were not retained; those procedures were re-run and both original and re-run values are reported side by side and never pooled. One cell of the long-read table reproduces exactly; the others do not, and this is stated in the manuscript. Changes in version 4. The package matches the manuscript. All thirteen supplementary tables are present, including Supplementary Tables S12 and S13, which were absent from the previous version, and Supplementary Table S1 now carries the genome length and assembly level of all 1,483 retained genomes rather than leaving those columns empty. A new Supplementary Table S1b lists the seven excluded genomes that could be recovered from local storage, with their lengths; the genome-length window is 1.5 to 1.7 Mb and this version states the evidence that fixes its bounds. Three new scripts are included: the marker-control experiment (scripts 26 and 27), in which the single copy-differentiating base of the isolate was set to A in both copies, to C in both, to T in both, and exchanged between them, with the reads realigned to each control; and the structural diagnostic of the two 26695 23S copies (script 28), which reports that copy 1 contains no ambiguous base while copy 2 contains one N at genome position 1,475,696. The four control reference sequences are deposited under results/marker_control/. Changes in version 6. This version restores the complete file set. The previous version was published from an incomplete upload, so most of the figures, several of the supplementary tables and part of the analysis code were missing from that record. Zenodo caps a record at 100 files and this package has 134, so the package is now deposited as a single archive, hp23s_copy_assignment_package.zip , which holds every file at the path it occupies in the source repository; this README, the SHA-256 manifest and the archive of rRNA calls and copy sequences are additionally placed loose in the record. From version 10 the manuscript itself is not deposited, in the archive or loose. Every member of the archive is listed in SHA256SUMS.txt with its SHA-256, and that manifest is regenerated here, which corrects the entry for this README (the previous manifest had been computed before the last edit of the file). DOI.txt now lists the version DOIs, and the data-availability sentence in the manuscript names the concept DOI rather than one version, so that it cannot point at a superseded record. Changes in version 7. This version is a manuscript round: the text is rebuilt from the same locked data by the same script, and no reported value changes. Three defects in the supplementary apparatus are correcte
title: Long reads assign a 23S rRNA resistance allele to one of the two copies in Helicobacter pylori; a complete short-read assembly does not

summary: Vacuum is an absolutely static reference system. When light propagates in a vacuum, it moves in an absolutely static reference system. The propagation speed of light in a medium is a constant, which has nothing to do with the motion state of the light source, the observer or the receiver. When light propagates in a medium, it is dragged by the inertia of the medium. While light propagates in a vacuum, the vacuum is absolutely static, which cannot drag the light to move, and the speed, position, and direction of light in a vacuum are fixed. Based on this theory, a light interference experiment can be performed as proof, using a Michelson interferometer. The principle of the experiment is to split the laser into two beams of light at a half-reflecting mirror,one of which passes through a vacuum quartz tube and reaches the Mirror M1,The light reflects back from M1,Passing through a vacuum quartz tube,Project onto the screen through a half mirror; The other beam of light does not pass through the vacuum quartz tube,reaches the Mirror M2,The light reflects back from M2,Project onto the screen through a half mirror.however, both of the beams converge on the screen, forming interference fringes.Because the speed, position, and direction of light in a vacuum are fixed and the absolute motion of the earth will drive the vacuum quartz tube to move,when the absolute direction of the earth's motion and the direction of light propagation are parallel to each other,light will have an extra optical path in the tube; when they are perpendicular to each other, light will not have the extra optical path in the tube, so after the instrument has turned 90 degrees, the interference fringes will move. The key to this experiment is to create a vacuum. The structure of the experiment is simple that I hope someone could make an experimental verification. According to this theory, it can be concluded that the essence of Fizeau experiment , sagnac effect and Hoek experiment is the same. The reverse process of Fizeau experiment is sagnac effect, vice versa. According to this theory, the Fizeau experiment has a calculated result of movement at 0.236 fringes and a measured value at 0.23 fringes; in the case of Ruyong Wang's experiment "Generalized Sagnac Effect", the moving phase difference has a calculated result at 0.000251 and measured value at 0.000246 in the experiment. Obviously, this theory is more consistent with the experimental measurement results and the theoretical explanation is more real and natural. The sagnac effect, Mach-Zehnder interferometer and Michelson interferometer can all be used to conduct experiments based on this principle to verify whether there is an absolutely stationary reference system. Among them, the sagnac effect has the highest accuracy, the Mach-Zehnder interferometer the second and the Michelson interferometer the lowest. If Michelson and Morley had used a 11m-long vacuum quartz tube for the experiment, they might have observed a movement of 0.373 interference fringesand there might have no so-called "dark clouds". This experiment is actually to measure the sagnac effect of the Earth's rotation by using a Michelson interferometer.

summary: Executable analysis pipeline (Jupyter notebook for Kaggle) and complete results for a study on spectroscopic screening of food adulteration with a stated risk of false accusation. Seven chemometric and deep-learning classifiers (PLS-DA, SVM, random forest, ROCKET, 1D-CNN and a multitask 1D-CNN with and without Beer-Lambert mixup) are compared under grouped, repeated cross-validation. Their out-of-fold scores feed three conformal layers: (i) class-conditional (Mondrian) conformal triage into PASS, FLAG and REFER decisions, with an ablation against marginal calibration and an analysis of calibration size and deployment batch shift; (ii) cross-conformal detection of adulterants absent from training (DD-SIMCA, leave-one-adulterant-out, network embeddings) with Benjamini-Hochberg batch screening; and (iii) a leave-level-out audit for level-batch confounding whose threshold is calibrated by a semi-synthetic Beer-Lambert simulation built from real ATR-FTIR spectra. Four public datasets are analysed (NIR hyperspectral imaging of extra-virgin olive oil; ATR-FTIR of turmeric with wheat flour; MIR of strawberry purée; ATR-FTIR of edible oils); they are not redistributed here (see README for sources and licences). The archive contains the notebook with the outputs of the run reported in the article, all result tables (CSV), figures (PNG), a results summary, run logs and environment information.
title: Risk-controlled spectroscopic screening of food adulteration with conformal prediction: code and results

summary: The FBT spectral-capacity action is the heat trace of one specified geometric Dirac operator at fixed spectral resolution. This paper states its domain and trace hypotheses, exact first and second variations, stationarity tests, coupled relative-torus 4 + 2 expression, and complete finite-computation requirements. The current application uses the embeddingto-operator map already supplied by DCQ6 and FBT10D on the closed coherent product. No second source map is required. The degree-24 regular magnetic realization, its singular-end analysis and the separate torus numerical benchmark are removed from the main development. Their removal leaves the functional and the relative-torus geometry intact. The global line-extension obstruction is retained to explain this separation. The inherited twist, its closed domain and all metric, spin and connection variations are used together. Exact fibre integration preserves the full heat trace; the four-dimensional quadratic action and normal stability certificates are cited from FBT10D with their original scope. General spectral error bounds retain feedback through omitted modes and distinguish affine connection tests from nonlinear geometric families. A final ledger separates established results from resolution selection, balance-layer selection, full nonlinear control and real-time interpretation. This revision introduces no new numerical sign certificate or physical mass prediction.
title: FBT10A: The Spectral–Capacity Action of the Fracture–Berry–Tension Framework

summary: Description This dataset provides harmonised administrative and surveillance health data describing the epidemiology and health system burden of varicella (ICD-10: B01) and herpes zoster (ICD-10: B02) in Bulgaria during the period 2023–2025 . The analysed time window corresponds to the post-COVID-19 period and precedes the introduction of mandatory varicella vaccination (2026) , providing an important baseline for evaluating vaccination policies and monitoring changes in disease epidemiology. The dataset integrates aggregated information from several national administrative and surveillance systems: 1. National Health Insurance Fund (NHIF) – hospital reimbursement through clinical pathways. 2. National Health Information System (NHIS) – national digital health infrastructure containing information on hospitalisations, outpatient medical examinations, and vaccination administration. 3. National Social Security Institute (NSSI) – sick leave records, sick leave duration, and compensation payments. 4. National Statistical Institute (NSI) – population denominators used for epidemiological rate calculations. National infectious disease surveillance system – mandatory reporting of infectious diseases according to Bulgarian public health legislation. All datasets are aggregated administrative records and contain no personally identifiable information . Data are aggregated at the regional (oblast) level and reported at monthly resolution , except for population denominators, which are annual. Regional names have been standardised to English transliterations , while the original Bulgarian names are preserved. All financial variables in this dataset are reported in Bulgarian lev (BGN) , which was the official currency of Bulgaria during the study period 2023–2025 . Bulgaria adopted the euro (EUR) in 2026 . However, the Bulgarian lev had long operated under a currency board arrangement with a fixed exchange rate to the euro . The official fixed exchange rate was: 1 EUR = 1.95583 BGN This exchange rate remained unchanged throughout the study period and can be used to convert financial variables in this dataset to euros for international comparison. Case Definition and Surveillance Classification Case definitions follow Ordinance No. 21 of 18 July 2005 on the registration, notification and reporting of infectious diseases , issued by the Bulgarian Ministry of Health. Clinical criteria A person presenting with: acute onset fever moderately impaired general condition polymorphic pruritic rash consisting of macules, papules, vesicles and crusts Laboratory criteria Laboratory confirmation may include: detection of varicella-zoster virus antigen detection of virus-specific antibodies viral isolation detection of viral nucleic acid Epidemiological criteria person-to-person transmission exposure to a common source of infection Case classification Classification Definition Possible case Meets clinical criteria Probable case Meets clinical criteria and has an epidemiological link Confirmed case Meets clinical and laboratory criteria During outbreaks, a case meeting clinical criteria and having an epidemiological link may also be classified as confirmed. summary: The study aimed to optimize preoperative modeling and the individualized selection of surgical treatment for genital prolapse in women of childbearing age. Materials and methods: A retrospective-prospective descriptive comparative analysis of clinical and functional data from 85 fertile women (Group 1: n=45 with connective tissue dysplasia markers; Group 2: n=40 without manifest CTD) was conducted. Anatomical defects were quantified using the international POP-Q system, levator muscle tone was evaluated via perineometry and 3D/4D pelvic floor ultrasound, and systemic connective tissue dysplasia was assessed using clinical risk scores. Results: Standardized objective quantification using POP-Q, integration of obstetric history, levator defect scoring, and metabolic/CTD markers allowed for the development of a predictive mathematical risk matrix. Custom laparoscopic reconstructive techniques (pectopexy and laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy with autologous/mesh organ-preserving repair) yielded 95.6% 2-year anatomical success compared to 77.5% in standard vaginal repair. Conclusion: Personalized surgical strategies and preoperative modeling based on multiple functional, anatomic, and connective tissue parameters significantly improve long-term outcomes, preserve reproductive capacity, and minimize recurrence in fertile women with pelvic floor dysplasia

summary: Implementation Mechanisms for Tipiṭaka-Grounded AI Alignment — An Engineering Companion to Suffering-Cessation as Value Function This paper reads the Abhidhamma — the analytical third division of the Theravāda Buddhist canon — as a process specification of mind: typed, momentary mental events arising one at a time under twenty-four typed conditioning relations, with ethical class tracked per event and per position in a processing cycle. From that reading it derives a research program for AI alignment evaluation and intervention: a red-team taxonomy of mimicry failure modes, resting-state (minimal-context) evaluation of language models, an intervention-timing typology over a processing cycle, a typed causal vocabulary, the limits of interpretability by subtraction, paired entailment-and-denial consistency testing of alignment claims, and a positive competence taxonomy. It is the engineering companion to Suffering-Cessation as Value Function (Ly, 2026), which argues for the Theravāda Tipiṭaka as a substrate for autonomous-AI alignment, and it develops the canon's third basket — the Abhidhamma Piṭaka — at the layer where that paper's §6.6 left off: the layer of cognitive process itself. We make one framing claim and two structural contributions. The framing claim is the compilation thesis : the Abhidhamma is a substrate-neutral process-specification of mind, and each era that has received it has read it in the vocabulary for process it had to hand — the scholastic commentators' wheels of classification, the twentieth century's reading of it as a psychology, cognitive science's information processing, and computation for ours. The tradition itself reached for machine images again and again, each fitted to one lesson; computation is this era's addition. The claim defended here is not that the Abhidhamma secretly describes computers. It is that the computational reading is our era's compilation of a specification that has survived the earlier readings, and that this compilation's target can enact what it compiles rather than only describe it. Formal and computational readings exist (Barendregt 2006; Karunananda et al. 2015; Lou 2017); Takeuchi (2026) reads transformer self-attention as anattā and pursues alignment by subtraction; an agent grounded in the substrate is engineered toward enacting wholesome cognition rather than simulating it. No priority is claimed for that aim. The first structural contribution is the machine architecture (§4): the samsaric process rendered in four repaired mappings — (1) a conditioned machine with exactly one free variable, against the strictly deterministic reading the canon itself condemns in Makkhali Gosāla's fatalism; (2) citta as the instruction-cycle rather than the processor, with the 89/121 citta-typology as a shared instruction set, the mindstream ( santāna ) as the thread, and uniqueness residing in the execution trace; (3) the kammic continuity as an append-only linked ledger rather than a blockchain — no miners, no consensus, maximal privacy, immutable entries whose ripening remains context-dependent; and (4) the counter-gear : the dhamma-wheel that engages the samsaric wheel at its one free variable and unwinds the machine by fuel-withdrawal rather than force, terminating in kiriya -mode execution — action that leaves no kammic residue. The second structural contribution is the verification-suite reading (§5) of the analytical books: the Yamaka as bidirectional property-testing, the Vibhaṅga's interrogation method as schema validation, the Dhātukathā as inclusion-matrix consistency, and the Kathāvatthu as formal adversarial protocol — with the Kathāvatthu's opening controversy ( puggalakathā , the refutation of the person-entity) read as the canon pre-running, and settling, this paper's own central repair. summary: A six-gene mineralization-inhibitor score (ENPP1, ANKH, MGP, GGCX, VKORC1, NT5E) in CD90+ dermal fibroblasts reads lower in systemic sclerosis than in controls. The gene set, direction, detection floors and significance threshold were fixed before any expression value was read. In a pre-registered held-out set of 50 donors (25 and 25), the observed difference is -0.2939 at one-sided p = 0.0204. That replication is across platforms within one study (GSE195452), not across studies, and no ambient RNA correction was applied. The score did not replicate in an independent series. In GSE292979, the same frozen genes, direction, floors and threshold were applied under a pre-registration, and a blinded second implementation reproduced every donor score within 1e-6 before the result was unmasked. All four pre-registered contrasts were null (primary -0.0412, one-sided p 0.4955; minimum attainable p 0.0045). The paper offers no explanation for the null and does not claim the effect is absent. The score is a pre-specified composite, not a pathway readout: a leave-one-out shows the signal concentrated in VKORC1, GGCX and NT5E, and the paper makes no mechanistic claim. The osteogenic half of the original hypothesis did not clear its pre-registered detection floor in any dataset examined. This is not a study of calcinosis lesions, not evidence of specificity, and not a mechanism. It is a pre-registered result that held within one study and did not replicate in the one independent series tested, reported with both outcomes.

summary: Lectures and practical classes remain the core formats for teaching specialized subjects in medical and dental universities, yet their modernization is often guided by descriptive experience rather than by empirical evidence. This review aimed to synthesize the evidence on the effectiveness of contemporary lecture and practical-class formats and to propose evidence-informed criteria for selecting them in the teaching of specialized subjects. A narrative review of literature indexed in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, ERIC and Google Scholar was performed, prioritizing meta-analyses, systematic reviews and randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Findings were interpreted through constructive alignment, cognitive load theory and Miller's pyramid of clinical competence. Across 225 studies, active learning increased examination performance by 0.47 standard deviations, and students taught by traditional lecturing were 1.5 times more likely to fail. In health professions education, the flipped classroom outperformed traditional teaching (SMD = 0.33); in dental education, problem-based, case-based, team-based and flipped formats together outperformed lecture-based learning (SMD = 0.48; 29 RCTs, 3,502 students). Technology-enhanced simulation was associated with large effects on knowledge and skills (effect sizes 1.09–1.20) compared with no intervention. However, the evidence shows high heterogeneity and focuses mainly on knowledge and learner satisfaction rather than clinical performance. Lectures and practical classes should be designed as a single aligned system in which the teaching format is selected according to the intended learning outcome and level of competence. Locally conducted controlled studies are needed to confirm these effects in medical universities of Uzbekistan.

This review aimed to synthesize the evidence on the effectiveness of contemporary lecture and practical-class formats and to propose evidence-informed criteria for selecting them in the teaching of specialized subjects. A narrative review of literature indexed in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, ERIC and Google Scholar was performed, prioritizing meta-analyses, systematic reviews and randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Findings were interpreted through constructive alignment, cognitive load theory and Miller's pyramid of clinical competence. Across 225 studies, active learning increased examination performance by 0.47 standard deviations, and students taught by traditional lecturing were 1.5 times more likely to fail. In health professions education, the flipped classroom outperformed traditional teaching (SMD = 0.33); in dental education, problem-based, case-based, team-based and flipped formats together outperformed lecture-based learning (SMD = 0.48; 29 RCTs, 3,502 students). Technology-enhanced simulation was associated with large effects on knowledge and skills (effect sizes 1.09–1.20) compared with no intervention. However, the evidence shows high heterogeneity and focuses mainly on knowledge and learner satisfaction rather than clinical performance. Lectures and practical classes should be designed as a single aligned system in which the teaching format is selected according to the intended learning outcome and level of competence. Locally conducted controlled studies are needed to confirm these effects in medical universities of Uzbekistan.

summary: This record provides the complete reproducibility package for the manuscript: “A Smaller Drop Is Not Robustness: A Validation-Locked Cross-Pipeline and Independent-Cohort Evaluation of a Quantum Kernel for Chest X-ray Classification.” The study re-evaluates an apparent robustness advantage of a four-qubit ZZ-feature-map quantum support vector machine (QSVM-ZZ) for chest X-ray classification. The revised experimental design separates absolute target performance from internal-to-target degradation and addresses configuration-selection bias, limited random-seed inference, duplicate and provenance concerns, feature-compression effects, asymmetric feature encoding, prediction collapse, and lack of independent-cohort validation. Experimental scope The package contains reproducibility materials for three complementary evaluation settings: Source and internal evaluation: PneumoniaMNIST, derived from the Guangzhou/Kermany pediatric chest X-ray cohort. Cross-pipeline preprocessing-shift evaluation: original Kermany test images representing the same underlying cohort through a different preprocessing pipeline. Independent-cohort evaluation: the RSNA Pneumonia Detection Challenge / NIH Clinical Center chest radiograph cohort. The confirmatory low-dimensional benchmark uses a configuration selected from source validation data only and evaluates QSVM-ZZ against RBF-SVM, logistic regression and a compact MLP across ten fresh seeds. Additional analyses include wider classical feature representations, a symmetric π·tanh encoding control, prediction-collapse and near-collapse audits, strict one-to-one paired radiograph evaluation, and repeated fine-tuned ResNet18 experiments. Key contents The record includes: raw-image duplicate and provenance-audit outputs; perceptual-hash screening results; reconstructed group-aware source training and validation splits; high-confidence source-to-raw correspondence mappings; the corrected 554-radiograph one-to-one paired mapping; PCA explained-variance and compression-sensitivity analyses; validation-only QSVM configuration-selection results; ten-seed confirmatory predictions and performance metrics; exact seed-level sign-flip tests and Holm-adjusted statistical comparisons; classical π·tanh encoding-control results; exact-collapse and near-collapse audits; source-validation-selected wider classical reference results; grouped domain-classifier outputs; five-seed fine-tuned ResNet18 predictions, training histories and trained checkpoints; independent RSNA primary and secondary evaluation outputs; derived RSNA frozen-feature arrays; executable Kaggle/Jupyter notebooks; software-version and random-seed information; SHA-256 integrity manifests; and legacy exploratory QSVM/VQC outputs retained for transparency and provenance. Principal methodological finding The revised analysis shows that QSVM-ZZ can exhibit a smaller internal-to-target macro-F1 decline than a matched low-dimensional RBF-SVM, but that smaller decline does not constitute evidence of practically useful robustness. QSVM-ZZ remains near chance by AUROC on both the Kermany preprocessing-shift target and the independent RSNA cohort, and its absolute target advantage over matched RBF-SVM is not statistically established. Applying the same π·tanh feature squashing used by QSVM-ZZ to the classical RBF-SVM substantially reduces the absolute Kermany performance gap, indicating that the classical-to-quantum encoding contributes to the apparent stability. Wider classical representations and fine-tuned ResNet18 additionally demonstrate that conclusions drawn from a severely compressed four-dimensional benchmark should not be generalized to broader model classes. Data-use and redistribution statement This archive contains derived features, mappings, predictions, statistical results, trained model checkpoints, code and analysis outputs. It does not redistribute raw RSNA DICOM images or raw Kermany/PneumoniaMNIST source-i

summary: Where is the place of the human being in the physical picture of the world? This question is usually answered from one of two camps: consciousness is a product of the brain and nothing more; or consciousness is immaterial and does not depend on the body. This work takes a different path — forward from the physical foundation, step by step — and looks at where it leads. The foundation is the work “The Birth of Dimensions: A Formal Skeleton” (BD). It contains nothing but a single assumption: everything is a process, an ideal sine wave, and its centre is the observer. Dimensions are born by squaring: first time, then, by iterating the same square, space and mass. Elementary particles turn out to be a resonance of at least three dimensions — time, space and mass. From the same assumption BD obtains the rules of quantum mechanics, the Lorentz transformations and the masses of particles from the speed of light alone. If the foundation is right, its rule should show up everywhere — including in the work of the brain. And it does: the main ranges of brain rhythms approximately form a ladder of squares — 2–3, 4–9, 16–81 Hz — built in the same way as the tower of levels in BD: the width of the levels in logarithms doubles with every step, and the alpha rhythm falls on the boundary between levels. The rhythm bands are blurred, but that is how it should be: the electroencephalogram is a projection of a higher-frequency process onto a single dimension, and within one level the process is smooth. What matters is something else — resonance between frequencies, and in the brain it was measured long ago. This leads to an assumption: the body is a resonator, and since bodies are alike, this answers the question of why different observers see one common world. Consciousness is then built like an elementary particle — as an agreement of three frequencies linked by squares — only on a higher-frequency level. That is why we see its work but cannot weigh it with instruments of our level; and that is why the world is perceived as three-dimensional. The structure is examined: the “I” is the observer; consciousness is time, the “here and now”; the subconscious is space, the “self” and its history; superconsciousness, intuition, is mass, which is born in self-reflection. From this follows an assumption about the meaning of life as the cultivation of intuition. If consciousness is like a particle, the reverse is also true: every particle may contain what we call consciousness. In the calculations of BD the Milky Way is the image of a neutron, and we live inside it; there are neutrons in almost every atom of our body. And the Universe, if it is like a black hole — part of a particle of a larger world — may be an observer. This is a hypothesis, not a proof. At the end there is a list of ways to test it, and what is established is separated from what is assumed. summary: Vacuum is an absolutely static reference system. When light propagates in a vacuum, it moves in an absolutely static reference system. The propagation speed of light in a medium is a constant, which has nothing to do with the motion state of the light source, the observer or the receiver. When light propagates in a medium, it is dragged by the inertia of the medium. While light propagates in a vacuum, the vacuum is absolutely static, which cannot drag the light to move, and the speed, position, and direction of light in a vacuum are fixed. Based on this theory, a light interference experiment can be performed as proof, using a Michelson interferometer. The principle of the experiment is to split the laser into two beams of light at a half-reflecting mirror,one of which passes through a vacuum quartz tube and reaches the Mirror M1,The light reflects back from M1,Passing through a vacuum quartz tube,Project onto the screen through a half mirror; The other beam of light does not pass through the vacuum quartz tube,reaches the Mirror M2,The light reflects back from M2,Project onto the screen through a half mirror.however, both of the beams converge on the screen, forming interference fringes.Because the speed, position, and direction of light in a vacuum are fixed and the absolute motion of the earth will drive the vacuum quartz tube to move,when the absolute direction of the earth's motion and the direction of light propagation are parallel to each other,light will have an extra optical path in the tube; when they are perpendicular to each other, light will not have the extra optical path in the tube, so after the instrument has turned 90 degrees, the interference fringes will move. The key to this experiment is to create a vacuum. The structure of the experiment is simple that I hope someone could make an experimental verification. According to this theory, it can be concluded that the essence of Fizeau experiment , sagnac effect and Hoek experiment is the same. The reverse process of Fizeau experiment is sagnac effect, vice versa. According to this theory, the Fizeau experiment has a calculated result of movement at 0.236 fringes and a measured value at 0.23 fringes; in the case of Ruyong Wang's experiment "Generalized Sagnac Effect", the moving phase difference has a calculated result at 0.000251 and measured value at 0.000246 in the experiment. Obviously, this theory is more consistent with the experimental measurement results and the theoretical explanation is more real and natural. The sagnac effect, Mach-Zehnder interferometer and Michelson interferometer can all be used to conduct experiments based on this principle to verify whether there is an absolutely stationary reference system. Among them, the sagnac effect has the highest accuracy, the Mach-Zehnder interferometer the second and the Michelson interferometer the lowest. If Michelson and Morley had used a 11m-long vacuum quartz tube for the experiment, they might have observed a movement of 0.373 interference fringesand there might have no so-called "dark clouds". This experiment is actually to measure the sagnac effect of the Earth's rotation by using a Michelson interferometer.

summary: Biometric authentication has become a primary mechanism for accessing critical systems, from corporate facilities and banking applications to healthcare records and smart home devices. The term bio-key encompas ses both the use of physiological and behavioural traits as authentication keys and the hardware security tokens (FIDO2 keys) that integrate biometric sensors. Despite widespread adoption, there is no formal ontology that in tegrates the full bio-key authentication chain, namely enrollment, biometric capture, template storage, matching, decision, and access grant, with security assurance levels, privacy requirements, and governance mechanisms. This gap produces semantic interoperability failures, inconsistent security assessments, and weak auditability, especially when biometric templates are compromised or when authentication decisions are contested. The critical asymmetry is that biometric traits are irrevocable: unlike passwords, a com promised fingerprint or iris pattern cannot be reissued. Existing ontologies focus on biometric modalities in isolation or on hardware tokens, but none formally models the complete chain as a data governance and privacy problem. This doctoral project proposes two complementary contributions: (i) a formal ontology, built with the OntoView method, that describes bio-key authentication chains, their security levels, privacy constraints, and governance gates, serving as an instrument for interoperability, risk assessment, and regulatory compliance; and (ii) a verification method, based on the on tology, that specifies and evaluates biometric gates and audit requirements, with direct impact on privacy protection and social well-being. For high value targets, the ontology distinguishes single-party authentication from quorum-based authentication (M-of-N), in which M co-present custodians must each authenticate with their own bio-key and the access secret is split among N parties. The ontology and method will be validated by encoding reported cases, by expert evaluation, and by an empirical study on a si mulated multi-modal biometric testbed with scripted spoofing, replay, and collusion scenarios.
title: Ontology for Bio-Key Authentication: Modalities, Security Levels, Privacy, and Governance

summary: Vacuum is an absolutely static reference system. When light propagates in a vacuum, it moves in an absolutely static reference system. The propagation speed of light in a medium is a constant, which has nothing to do with the motion state of the light source, the observer or the receiver. When light propagates in a medium, it is dragged by the inertia of the medium. While light propagates in a vacuum, the vacuum is absolutely static, which cannot drag the light to move, and the speed, position, and direction of light in a vacuum are fixed. Based on this theory, a light interference experiment can be performed as proof, using a sagnac effect. The principle of the experiment is to split the laser into two beams of light at a half-reflecting mirror, one of which passes through a vacuum quartz tube and reaches the screen, the other passes through a vacuum quartz tube from the other directionand and reaches the screen; however, both of the beams converge on the screen, forming interference fringes. Because the speed, position, and direction of light in a vacuum are fixed and the absolute motion of the earth will drive the vacuum quartz tube to move,when the absolute direction of the earth's motion and the direction of light propagation are parallel to each other,light will have an extra optical path in the tube; when they are perpendicular to each other, light will not have the extra optical path in the tube, so after the instrument has turned 90 degrees, the interference fringes will move. The key to this experiment is to create a vacuum. The structure of the experiment is simple that I hope someone could make an experimental verification. According to this theory, it can be concluded that the essence of Fizeau experiment , sagnac effect and Hoek experiment is the same. The reverse process of Fizeau experiment is sagnac effect, vice versa. According to this theory, the Fizeau experiment has a calculated result of movement at 0.236 fringes and a measured value at 0.23 fringes; in the case of Ruyong Wang's experiment "Generalized Sagnac Effect", the moving phase difference has a calculated result at 0.000251 and measured value at 0.000246 in the experiment. Obviously, this theory is more consistent with the experimental measurement results and the theoretical explanation is more real and natural. The sagnac effect, Mach-Zehnder interferometer and Michelson interferometer can all be used to conduct experiments based on this principle to verify whether there is an absolutely stationary reference system. Among them, the sagnac effect has the highest accuracy, the Mach-Zehnder interferometer the second and the Michelson interferometer the lowest. If Michelson and Morley had used a 11m-long vacuum quartz tube for the experiment, they might have observed a movement of 0.373 interference fringes and there might have no so-called "dark clouds". This experiment is actually using the Sagnac effect to measure the Earth's rotation.

title: A Hypothetical Experimental Approach to Prove the Existenceof an Absolutely Stationary Reference Frameby Using the sagnac effect

summary: Implementation Mechanisms for Tipiṭaka-Grounded AI Alignment — An Engineering Companion to Suffering-Cessation as Value Function This paper reads the Abhidhamma — the analytical third division of the Theravāda Buddhist canon — as a process specification of mind: typed, momentary mental events arising one at a time under twenty-four typed conditioning relations, with ethical class tracked per event and per position in a processing cycle. From that reading it derives a research program for AI alignment evaluation and intervention: a red-team taxonomy of mimicry failure modes, resting-state (minimal-context) evaluation of language models, an intervention-timing typology over a processing cycle, a typed causal vocabulary, the limits of interpretability by subtraction, paired entailment-and-denial consistency testing of alignment claims, and a positive competence taxonomy. It is the engineering companion to Suffering-Cessation as Value Function (Ly, 2026), which argues for the Theravāda Tipiṭaka as a substrate for autonomous-AI alignment, and it develops the canon's third basket — the Abhidhamma Piṭaka — at the layer where that paper's §6.6 left off: the layer of cognitive process itself. We make one framing claim and two structural contributions. The framing claim is the compilation thesis : the Abhidhamma is a substrate-neutral process-specification of mind, and each era that has received it has read it in the vocabulary for process it had to hand — the scholastic commentators' wheels of classification, the twentieth century's reading of it as a psychology, cognitive science's information processing, and computation for ours. The tradition itself reached for machine images again and again, each fitted to one lesson; computation is this era's addition. The claim defended here is not that the Abhidhamma secretly describes computers. It is that the computational reading is our era's compilation of a specification that has survived the earlier readings, and that this compilation's target can enact what it compiles rather than only describe it. Formal and computational readings exist (Barendregt 2006; Karunananda et al. 2015; Lou 2017); Takeuchi (2026) reads transformer self-attention as anattā and pursues alignment by subtraction; an agent grounded in the substrate is engineered toward enacting wholesome cognition rather than simulating it. No priority is claimed for that aim. The first structural contribution is the machine architecture (§4): the samsaric process rendered in four repaired mappings — (1) a conditioned machine with exactly one free variable, against the strictly deterministic reading the canon itself condemns in Makkhali Gosāla's fatalism; (2) citta as the instruction-cycle rather than the processor, with the 89/121 citta-typology as a shared instruction set, the mindstream ( santāna ) as the thread, and uniqueness residing in the execution trace; (3) the kammic continuity as an append-only linked ledger rather than a blockchain — no miners, no consensus, maximal privacy, immutable entries whose ripening remains context-dependent; and (4) the counter-gear : the dhamma-wheel that engages the samsaric wheel at its one free variable and unwinds the machine by fuel-withdrawal rather than force, terminating in kiriya -mode execution — action that leaves no kammic residue. The second structural contribution is the verification-suite reading (§5) of the analytical books: the Yamaka as bidirectional property-testing, the Vibhaṅga's interrogation method as schema validation, the Dhātukathā as inclusion-matrix consistency, and the Kathāvatthu as formal adversarial protocol — with the Kathāvatthu's opening controversy ( puggalakathā , the refutation of the person-entity) read as the canon pre-running, and settling, this paper's own central repair. title: The Wheel That Unwinds the Wheel: The Abhidhamma as Executable Process-Specification

summary: This record provides the complete reproducibility package for the manuscript: “A Smaller Drop Is Not Robustness: A Validation-Locked Cross-Pipeline and Independent-Cohort Evaluation of a Quantum Kernel for Chest X-ray Classification.” The study re-evaluates an apparent robustness advantage of a four-qubit ZZ-feature-map quantum support vector machine (QSVM-ZZ) for chest X-ray classification. The revised experimental design separates absolute target performance from internal-to-target degradation and addresses configuration-selection bias, limited random-seed inference, duplicate and provenance concerns, feature-compression effects, asymmetric feature encoding, prediction collapse, and lack of independent-cohort validation. Experimental scope The package contains reproducibility materials for three complementary evaluation settings: Source and internal evaluation: PneumoniaMNIST, derived from the Guangzhou/Kermany pediatric chest X-ray cohort. Cross-pipeline preprocessing-shift evaluation: original Kermany test images representing the same underlying cohort through a different preprocessing pipeline. Independent-cohort evaluation: the RSNA Pneumonia Detection Challenge / NIH Clinical Center chest radiograph cohort. The confirmatory low-dimensional benchmark uses a configuration selected from source validation data only and evaluates QSVM-ZZ against RBF-SVM, logistic regression and a compact MLP across ten fresh seeds. Additional analyses include wider classical feature representations, a symmetric π·tanh encoding control, prediction-collapse and near-collapse audits, strict one-to-one paired radiograph evaluation, and repeated fine-tuned ResNet18 experiments. Key contents The record includes: raw-image duplicate and provenance-audit outputs; perceptual-hash screening results; reconstructed group-aware source training and validation splits; high-confidence source-to-raw correspondence mappings; the corrected 554-radiograph one-to-one paired mapping; PCA explained-variance and compression-sensitivity analyses; validation-only QSVM configuration-selection results; ten-seed confirmatory predictions and performance metrics; exact seed-level sign-flip tests and Holm-adjusted statistical comparisons; classical π·tanh encoding-control results; exact-collapse and near-collapse audits; source-validation-selected wider classical reference results; grouped domain-classifier outputs; five-seed fine-tuned ResNet18 predictions, training histories and trained checkpoints; independent RSNA primary and secondary evaluation outputs; derived RSNA frozen-feature arrays; executable Kaggle/Jupyter notebooks; software-version and random-seed information; SHA-256 integrity manifests; and legacy exploratory QSVM/VQC outputs retained for transparency and provenance. Principal methodological finding The revised analysis shows that QSVM-ZZ can exhibit a smaller internal-to-target macro-F1 decline than a matched low-dimensional RBF-SVM, but that smaller decline does not constitute evidence of practically useful robustness. QSVM-ZZ remains near chance by AUROC on both the Kermany preprocessing-shift target and the independent RSNA cohort, and its absolute target advantage over matched RBF-SVM is not statistically established. Applying the same π·tanh feature squashing used by QSVM-ZZ to the classical RBF-SVM substantially reduces the absolute Kermany performance gap, indicating that the classical-to-quantum encoding contributes to the apparent stability. Wider classical representations and fine-tuned ResNet18 additionally demonstrate that conclusions drawn from a severely compressed four-dimensional benchmark should not be generalized to broader model classes. Data-use and redistribution statement This archive contains derived features, mappings, predictions, statistical results, trained model checkpoints, code and analysis outputs. It does not redistribute raw RSNA DICOM images or raw Kermany/PneumoniaMNIST source-i
title: Does a Smaller Performance Drop Really Mean Robustness? A Validation-Locked Evaluation of a Quantum Kernel for Chest X-ray Classification

summary: Where is the place of the human being in the physical picture of the world? This question is usually answered from one of two camps: consciousness is a product of the brain and nothing more; or consciousness is immaterial and does not depend on the body. This work takes a different path — forward from the physical foundation, step by step — and looks at where it leads. The foundation is the work “The Birth of Dimensions: A Formal Skeleton” (BD). It contains nothing but a single assumption: everything is a process, an ideal sine wave, and its centre is the observer. Dimensions are born by squaring: first time, then, by iterating the same square, space and mass. Elementary particles turn out to be a resonance of at least three dimensions — time, space and mass. From the same assumption BD obtains the rules of quantum mechanics, the Lorentz transformations and the masses of particles from the speed of light alone. If the foundation is right, its rule should show up everywhere — including in the work of the brain. And it does: the main ranges of brain rhythms approximately form a ladder of squares — 2–3, 4–9, 16–81 Hz — built in the same way as the tower of levels in BD: the width of the levels in logarithms doubles with every step, and the alpha rhythm falls on the boundary between levels. The rhythm bands are blurred, but that is how it should be: the electroencephalogram is a projection of a higher-frequency process onto a single dimension, and within one level the process is smooth. What matters is something else — resonance between frequencies, and in the brain it was measured long ago. This leads to an assumption: the body is a resonator, and since bodies are alike, this answers the question of why different observers see one common world. Consciousness is then built like an elementary particle — as an agreement of three frequencies linked by squares — only on a higher-frequency level. That is why we see its work but cannot weigh it with instruments of our level; and that is why the world is perceived as three-dimensional. The structure is examined: the “I” is the observer; consciousness is time, the “here and now”; the subconscious is space, the “self” and its history; superconsciousness, intuition, is mass, which is born in self-reflection. From this follows an assumption about the meaning of life as the cultivation of intuition. If consciousness is like a particle, the reverse is also true: every particle may contain what we call consciousness. In the calculations of BD the Milky Way is the image of a neutron, and we live inside it; there are neutrons in almost every atom of our body. And the Universe, if it is like a black hole — part of a particle of a larger world — may be an observer. This is a hypothesis, not a proof. At the end there is a list of ways to test it, and what is established is separated from what is assumed. Revisions as of 07.11.2026:  The list of related works has been corrected.       Где в физической картине мира место человеку? Обычно на этот вопрос отвечают из двух лагерей: сознание — порождение мозга, и только; или сознание нематериально и от тела не зависит. Эта работа идёт другим путём — от физической основы вперёд, шаг за шагом, и смотрит, куда она приводит. Основа — работа «Рождение измерений: формальный скелет» (РИ). В ней нет ничего, кроме одного допущения: всё есть процесс, идеальный синус, а его центр — наблюдатель. Измерения рождаются возведением в квадрат: сначала время, затем, итерациями того же квадрата, пространство и масса. Элементарные частицы оказываются резонансом как минимум трёх измерений — времени, пространства и массы. Из того же допущения РИ получает правила квантовой механики, преобразования Лоренца и массы частиц из одной лишь скорости света. Если основа верна, её правило должно про
title: Consciousness as a Wave Structure: A Possible Connection Between Brain Frequencies and Perception Frequencies

summary: STARLI | F071–F080 / 300 Flagship 13 Fission · Volume I · Biointerface Perturbations, Surface Reliability and Traceable Validation Author: 33  |  Nonclinical Research Design Working Edition v1.3  |  English Zenodo Ten-Volume Overview This collection joins two five-theme research units from the STARLI 300-theme atlas. Research Unit I (F071–F075) examines local electric fields, surface aging, ionic-strength coupling, photothermal side effects and mechanical stress at biological interfaces. Research Unit II (F076–F080) extends the inquiry to multilayer coating reliability, molecular selectivity, noise-source attribution, reversible surface function and material leaching. The central concern is whether an interface claim survives realistic matrix changes, traceable controls and independent reconstruction. The ten English research working editions comprise 7,770 PDF pages: 300 candidate mathematical plates, 820 chapter openings, 4,100 separately paginated investigations, 2,000 Research Gates and 330 Phoenix Answer Embryos. summary: Code, configuration files, result files and scripts that regenerate every table and figure of the manuscript "Source Audited Evaluation of Lightweight Phishing Detectors for Telecom Text: Leakage, Debiasing, and Conformal Abstention" (Ahmad, Shehzad, Hasan, Hussain), submitted to IEEE Transactions on Artificial Intelligence. The archive contains the source audit (exact and MinHash near duplicate removal, Cramér's V between source and label), the SDAP detector (word BiLSTM and byte CNN under a gradient reversal source adversary) with its ablations, TF IDF baselines, leave one source out evaluation, temperature scaling and split conformal abstention, character level attack perturbations, the per message predictions and logs of the reported run, the figure scripts, and the LaTeX source of the manuscript in the IEEE TAI template. The public corpora (UCI SMS Spam Collection, Enron spam, a Phishing Pot sample and a labelled URL list) are downloaded from their original providers by scripts/fetch_data.sh; see README.md for the full reproduction steps and data licences. Version 2.0 updates the manuscript source and author metadata and redraws the two method diagrams; the experimental results are unchanged from version 1.

The public corpora (UCI SMS Spam Collection, Enron spam, a Phishing Pot sample and a labelled URL list) are downloaded from their original providers by scripts/fetch_data.sh; see README.md for the full reproduction steps and data licences. Version 2.0 updates the manuscript source and author metadata and redraws the two method diagrams; the experimental results are unchanged from version 1.

summary: Acute respiratory infections in children comprise etiologically and clinically heterogeneous diseases with overlapping early manifestations, whereas the risk of respiratory failure and other adverse outcomes varies according to age, premorbid conditions, and the causative pathogen. This review aims to analyze current approaches to etiological diagnosis and evidence-based risk factors for severe disease in children. An analytical search covered PubMed/MEDLINE and documents issued by the World Health Organization and the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence for 2015-2026. Priority was given to guidelines, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, diagnostic accuracy studies, and large cohorts. Clinical assessment identifies the anatomical level of respiratory involvement and current severity but cannot reliably establish viral etiology. Nucleic acid amplification remains the most sensitive method for detecting most respiratory viruses. Diagnostic value depends on the timing and quality of specimen collection, panel composition, and clinical context; a positive multiplex result does not establish the causal contribution of every detected agent. Serology has a limited role in an acute episode. Consistently reported baseline risk factors include young age, prematurity, chronic lung disease, hemodynamically significant congenital heart disease, neurological disorders, immunodeficiency or immunosuppressive treatment, and malnutrition. Hypoxemia, apnea, progressive respiratory distress, feeding inability, altered consciousness, and impaired perfusion indicate evolving organ dysfunction and require immediate assessment. Reliable prediction should integrate baseline risk factors with dynamic clinical variables. Any prediction model requires independent validation in the pediatric population for which its use is intended.
title: Acute Respiratory Infections in Children: Current Approaches to Etiological Diagnosis and Prediction of Severe Disease (Literature Review).

summary: STARLI | F091–F100 / 300 Flagship 13 Fission · Volume I · Collective Microrobotic Autonomy, Swarm Safety and Mission Continuity Author: 33  |  Nonclinical Research Design Working Edition v1.3  |  English Zenodo Ten-Volume Overview This ten-volume collection closes the first hundred of the STARLI 300-theme research-design atlas. Research Unit I (F091–F095) examines autonomous sampling, local-to-global coordination, pheromone-like signaling, collision avoidance and collective energy allocation. Research Unit II (F096–F100) examines distributed planning, localization uncertainty, changing network topology, fault isolation and safe mission handoff. Each volume states prospective physical tests rather than completed experimental findings. The ten English working editions total 7,770 PDF pages: 300 candidate mathematical plates, 820 chapter openings, 4,100 independently paginated investigations, 2,000 Research Gates and 330 Phoenix Answer Embryos. The v1.3 Gate-annotation pass contrasts mechanisms, physical witnesses, blinded falsifiers, rivals, stopping boundaries and successor interfaces. These editorial counts and text-screening results do not establish causal independence or scientific validation. The Ten Research Directions F091  Nanorobotic Collective Autonomy Sampling At The Limit — Proposes controlled tests of swarm sampling throughput and identity preservation. A concealed communication partition probes whether completion gains survive the loss of collective coordination, against a centralized full-state controller; collision events and consensus error remain explicit vetoes. F092  Microrobotic Local Collaboration And Global Mission At The Limit — Asks whether agent-to-agent collaboration improves global agreement when robots lack an unmetered global-state feed. Hidden adversarial-neighbor states test dependence on outside tracking; fixed behavior rules with matched energy provide the comparator. F093  Nanorobotic Collective Pheromone Communication At The Limit — Explores prospective chemical-trail or signal-mediated coordination with collision exposure as a primary outcome. Hidden actuator saturation and a matched-actuation single-agent baseline challenge claims that signaling, rather than redundancy or imposed motion, caused the improvement. F094  Microscale Robot Collective Collision Avoidance Control At The Limit — Examines collision-safe motion while monitoring spatial coverage, recovery time and communication burden. A blinded shared-localization bias tests whether apparent avoidance depends on erroneous common position estimates; safety-boundary crossings trigger rejection. F095  Nanorobotic Collective Energy Allocation At The Limit — Tests dynamic allocation of limited energy across agents during dropout and recovery. Hidden agent-loss clusters challenge energy accounting and recovery-time claims against fixed rules with an equal energy budget; persistent unsafe confidence is a stop condition. F096  Microrobotic Distributed Mission Planning At The Limit — Studies task planning without a central controller using communication load, work-per-task and selective abstention as prospective metrics. Hidden network partitions expose plans that depend on unavailable messages, while a matched-actuation single-agent system tests whether coordination adds value. F097  Nanorobotic Collective Localization Uncertainty At The Limit — Tests whether robots can act safely when position confidence is uncertain or neighbors provide deceptive state information. Energy per accepted task, abstention and completion are checked against a full-state centralized benchmark; unrecognized safety-boundary crossings invalidate the claim. F098  Microrobotic Collective Dynamic Topology Control At The Limit — Examines when changing neighbor connections should trigger reconfiguration or justified refusal to proceed

F094 Microscale Robot Collective Collision Avoidance Control At The Limit — Examines collision-safe motion while monitoring spatial coverage, recovery time and communication burden. F095 Nanorobotic Collective Energy Allocation At The Limit — Tests dynamic allocation of limited energy across agents during dropout and recovery. F098 Microrobotic Collective Dynamic Topology Control At The Limit — Examines when changing neighbor connections should trigger reconfiguration or justified refusal to proceed. F099 Nanorobotic Collective Fault Isolation At The Limit — Investigates recognition and containment of malfunctioning agents without allowing errors to propagate across the swarm. The study checks consensus error, collisions and coverage against centralized full-state control; an apparently successful handoff is rejected if safety invariants are violated. Scope, Falsifiability and Evidence Boundaries All ten volumes are prospective, nonclinical research-design working editions for traceable materials, authorized ex-vivo systems, synthetic phantoms and bench-scale microfluidic tests. Proposed comparisons require preregistered budgets, blinded perturbations, independent reference measurements, complete negative-trial denominators and explicit safety stops. summary: This paper outlines a comparative structural framework for analyzing how judicial rulings from supranational courts (specifically the CJEU under Article 267 TFEU preliminary references and the ECHR) systematically transform domestic policy parameters without explicit legislative mandates.   Adapted specifically to the institutional mechanics of the French legal order, the framework operationalizes four key structural components:   Judicial Displacement (JD): The structural mechanism through which supranational courts assume primary interpretative authority over national policy, constrained in France by Article 55 of the Constitution.   Administrative Gradualism (AG): The incremental realignment of domestic policy through an iterative sequence of secondary executive and regulatory instruments (décrets, arrêtés, circulaires, and administrative guidance) issued by ministries and independent regulatory bodies (e.g., CNIL, ARCOM).   The Mandate Scale (M_0–M_3): A heuristic metric assessing the spectrum of explicit democratic authorization present within electoral manifestos, winning coalitions, or direct referendums regarding supranational constraints.   Four-Step Operational Cycle: A recurring sequence mapping the trajectory from supranational judicial trigger \rightarrow national administrative response (expanding, reclaiming, or accommodating) \rightarrow democratic legitimacy deficits (input, throughput, output) \rightarrow systemic political outcomes (evolutionary pushback via contrôle de conventionnalité or systemic backlash).   The paper includes a comparative matrix contrasting UK statutory mechanism (HRA 1998, Statutory Instruments) against French constitutional pathways (Sarran, Nicolo, Article 38 ordonnances), along with a rigorous methodology defining a "True-Negative Profile" to test boundary conditions against selection bias.  Note on Origin & Systemic Scope: This publication represents an operational draft outline designed to establish baseline terminology, structural mechanics, and theoretical metrics for ongoing comparative legal research.   This work is a direct spin-off and structural adaptation of the foundational framework established in: Davidson, C. K. S., Judicial Displacement and Administrative Gradualism, DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.24023708.    While the original benchmark paper evaluated these dynamics within a dualist, parliamentary context (specifically United Kingdom immigration policy and prisoner voting rights under ECHR jurisprudence), this adaptation recalibrates the core analytical model to the monist-leaning, semi-presidential institutional architecture of the French Fifth Republic under Article 55 of the 1958 French Constitution.    This draft serves as the immediate European adaptation within a broader comparative research agenda, with future planned adaptations extending the framework to examine administrative realignments, executive rule-making, and judicial review dynamics within the United States constitutional framework.

summary: This analysis examines how computational configuration choices shape resource efficiency in confidential genomic collaboration across institutions. A descriptive secondary analysis uses 14 PRINCESS benchmark configurations published in 2017, comprising seven batch sizes evaluated with compression enabled and disabled across three sites. Matched runtime differences, ratios and joint memory comparisons identify configuration tradeoffs. With compression enabled, increasing batch size from 100 to 10,000 variants reduces runtime by 75.49 percent, while expansion to one million variants provides only 0.38 percent further improvement despite requiring 32.69 times as much memory. Without compression, runtime reaches its observed minimum at 8,000 variants and subsequently increases. Compression enabled records longer enclave runtime in every matched pair. These patterns reveal diminishing processing gains and configuration dependent resource tradeoffs, without isolating their underlying mechanisms. The contribution is a comparative interpretation distinguishing faster execution from economical resource use. The findings refine a resource constraint perspective and support joint evaluation of execution time and memory when configuring protected genomic workflows, with numerical recommendations bounded by the observed benchmark environment.
title: BENCHMARKING CONFIDENTIAL GENOMIC COMPUTING EFFICIENCY THROUGH BATCH SIZE, COMPRESSION, AND MEMORY USE ACROSS COLLABORATIVE SITES

summary: This data set contains raw SPECT projection data acquired on a variety of scanners and for a variety of isotopes. The data is used in the official PyTomography SPECT tutorials at this website. Version 2 (PyTomography 4) keeps SPECT.zip as it was and adds the regions of interest that PyTomography 4's tutorials measure, as 3D Slicer segmentations: jaszak_rois.seg.nrrd (the six spheres and the background of the SIMIND Jaszczak phantom) and lu177_nema_symt2_rois.seg.nrrd (the six spheres, the lung insert and the background of the Lu-177 NEMA phantom scanned on the Siemens Symbia T2). Version 2.1 (PyTomography 4) keeps every file of version 2 and adds the data of the kernel EM tutorial: a simulated Lu-177 DOTATATE SPECT scan of the Zubal phantom ( zubal_projections.npy ), a simulated Ga-68 DOTATATE PET image as its prior ( zubal_pet_prior.npy ) and the attenuation map ( zubal_attenuation_map.npy ), described in zubal_README.md . They were made and contributed by Huanzhe Wei, King's College London. If you use them, please cite: Wei H, Livieratos L, Reader AJ. PET-informed deep-learned kernel method for theranostic SPECT reconstruction. IEEE Transactions on Radiation and Plasma Medical Sciences (2026). doi:10.1109/TRPMS.2026.3737413.

summary: This paper proposes Recursive Anticipatory Argumentation-Control Theory (RAACT), an interdisciplinary framework for representing argumentative discourse as a dynamic, par- tially observed, and recursively updated interaction system. Its central mechanism, Recur- sive Anticipatory Argument-Path Interception (RAAPI), combines contextual observation, pragmatic-linguistic encoding, argument reconstruction, opponent-state estimation, proba- bilistic argument-path forecasting, formal refutation verification, anticipatory intervention, and feedback-based model revision. The framework is developed around the Pre-emptive Refutation Fork Case (PRFC), a primary analytical case in which one participant forecasts an opponent's possible argumenta- tive move and presents a logically evaluated counterargument before that move is explicitly advanced. Subsequent responses are classified into continuation, substitution, qualification, forecast challenge, clarification, and novel argumentative pathways. The mathematical specification introduces latent-state models, observation functions, categorical predictive distributions, Bayesian belief updating, intervention-utility functions, estimation errors, and forecast-evaluation metrics. Conditional mathematical propositions identify what can be established under explicit assumptions, while empirical hypotheses dis- tinguish predictive accuracy from intervention effectiveness and strategic response restriction. RAACT is presented as a formal theoretical architecture and a research program, not as an empirically validated universal law. Its principal scientific obligations are to demonstrate incremental predictive value, establish causal effects under an identifiable research design, prove specific mathematical claims under stated assumptions, and identify boundary conditions through counterexamples and independent replication. summary: This record provides the complete reproducibility package for the manuscript: “A Smaller Drop Is Not Robustness: A Validation-Locked Cross-Pipeline and Independent-Cohort Evaluation of a Quantum Kernel for Chest X-ray Classification.” The study re-evaluates an apparent robustness advantage of a four-qubit ZZ-feature-map quantum support vector machine (QSVM-ZZ) for chest X-ray classification. The revised experimental design separates absolute target performance from internal-to-target degradation and addresses configuration-selection bias, limited random-seed inference, duplicate and provenance concerns, feature-compression effects, asymmetric feature encoding, prediction collapse, and lack of independent-cohort validation. Experimental scope The package contains reproducibility materials for three complementary evaluation settings: Source and internal evaluation: PneumoniaMNIST, derived from the Guangzhou/Kermany pediatric chest X-ray cohort. Cross-pipeline preprocessing-shift evaluation: original Kermany test images representing the same underlying cohort through a different preprocessing pipeline. Independent-cohort evaluation: the RSNA Pneumonia Detection Challenge / NIH Clinical Center chest radiograph cohort. The confirmatory low-dimensional benchmark uses a configuration selected from source validation data only and evaluates QSVM-ZZ against RBF-SVM, logistic regression and a compact MLP across ten fresh seeds. Additional analyses include wider classical feature representations, a symmetric π·tanh encoding control, prediction-collapse and near-collapse audits, strict one-to-one paired radiograph evaluation, and repeated fine-tuned ResNet18 experiments. Key contents The record includes: raw-image duplicate and provenance-audit outputs; perceptual-hash screening results; reconstructed group-aware source training and validation splits; high-confidence source-to-raw correspondence mappings; the corrected 554-radiograph one-to-one paired mapping; PCA explained-variance and compression-sensitivity analyses; validation-only QSVM configuration-selection results; ten-seed confirmatory predictions and performance metrics; exact seed-level sign-flip tests and Holm-adjusted statistical comparisons; classical π·tanh encoding-control results; exact-collapse and near-collapse audits; source-validation-selected wider classical reference results; grouped domain-classifier outputs; five-seed fine-tuned ResNet18 predictions, training histories and trained checkpoints; independent RSNA primary and secondary evaluation outputs; derived RSNA frozen-feature arrays; executable Kaggle/Jupyter notebooks; software-version and random-seed information; SHA-256 integrity manifests; and legacy exploratory QSVM/VQC outputs retained for transparency and provenance. Principal methodological finding The revised analysis shows that QSVM-ZZ can exhibit a smaller internal-to-target macro-F1 decline than a matched low-dimensional RBF-SVM, but that smaller decline does not constitute evidence of practically useful robustness. QSVM-ZZ remains near chance by AUROC on both the Kermany preprocessing-shift target and the independent RSNA cohort, and its absolute target advantage over matched RBF-SVM is not statistically established. Applying the same π·tanh feature squashing used by QSVM-ZZ to the classical RBF-SVM substantially reduces the absolute Kermany performance gap, indicating that the classical-to-quantum encoding contributes to the apparent stability. Wider classical representations and fine-tuned ResNet18 additionally demonstrate that conclusions drawn from a severely compressed four-dimensional benchmark should not be generalized to broader model classes. Data-use and redistribution statement This archive contains derived features, mappings, predictions, statistical results, trained model checkpoints, code and analysis outputs. It does not redistribute raw RSNA DICOM images or raw Kermany/PneumoniaMNIST source-i

summary: STARLI | F081–F090 / 300 Flagship 13 Fission · Volume I · Microrobotic Biointerfaces, Interfacial Stability and Traceable Validation Author: 33  |  Nonclinical Research Design Working Edition v1.3  |  English Zenodo Ten-Volume Overview This collection joins two five-theme research units from the STARLI 300-theme atlas. Research Unit I (F081–F085) studies cell-surface marker identification, chemical interface memory, fluid-shear fatigue, cross-sensitive nano-quantum readouts and precursors of interface failure. Research Unit II (F086–F090) extends these questions to coupled interface physics, degradability, nonequilibrium adsorption, cross-environment robustness and trustworthy validation. Every proposal requires independently traceable specimens, blinded perturbations and explicit rival explanations; no proposed advantage is reported as measured.
