summary: This record provides the complete reproducibility package for the manuscript: “A Smaller Drop Is Not Robustness: A Validation-Locked Cross-Pipeline and Independent-Cohort Evaluation of a Quantum Kernel for Chest X-ray Classification.” The study re-evaluates an apparent robustness advantage of a four-qubit ZZ-feature-map quantum support vector machine (QSVM-ZZ) for chest X-ray classification. The revised experimental design separates absolute target performance from internal-to-target degradation and addresses configuration-selection bias, limited random-seed inference, duplicate and provenance concerns, feature-compression effects, asymmetric feature encoding, prediction collapse, and lack of independent-cohort validation. Experimental scope The package contains reproducibility materials for three complementary evaluation settings: Source and internal evaluation: PneumoniaMNIST, derived from the Guangzhou/Kermany pediatric chest X-ray cohort. Cross-pipeline preprocessing-shift evaluation: original Kermany test images representing the same underlying cohort through a different preprocessing pipeline. Independent-cohort evaluation: the RSNA Pneumonia Detection Challenge / NIH Clinical Center chest radiograph cohort. The confirmatory low-dimensional benchmark uses a configuration selected from source validation data only and evaluates QSVM-ZZ against RBF-SVM, logistic regression and a compact MLP across ten fresh seeds. Additional analyses include wider classical feature representations, a symmetric π·tanh encoding control, prediction-collapse and near-collapse audits, strict one-to-one paired radiograph evaluation, and repeated fine-tuned ResNet18 experiments. Key contents The record includes: raw-image duplicate and provenance-audit outputs; perceptual-hash screening results; reconstructed group-aware source training and validation splits; high-confidence source-to-raw correspondence mappings; the corrected 554-radiograph one-to-one paired mapping; PCA explained-variance and compression-sensitivity analyses; validation-only QSVM configuration-selection results; ten-seed confirmatory predictions and performance metrics; exact seed-level sign-flip tests and Holm-adjusted statistical comparisons; classical π·tanh encoding-control results; exact-collapse and near-collapse audits; source-validation-selected wider classical reference results; grouped domain-classifier outputs; five-seed fine-tuned ResNet18 predictions, training histories and trained checkpoints; independent RSNA primary and secondary evaluation outputs; derived RSNA frozen-feature arrays; executable Kaggle/Jupyter notebooks; software-version and random-seed information; SHA-256 integrity manifests; and legacy exploratory QSVM/VQC outputs retained for transparency and provenance. Principal methodological finding The revised analysis shows that QSVM-ZZ can exhibit a smaller internal-to-target macro-F1 decline than a matched low-dimensional RBF-SVM, but that smaller decline does not constitute evidence of practically useful robustness. QSVM-ZZ remains near chance by AUROC on both the Kermany preprocessing-shift target and the independent RSNA cohort, and its absolute target advantage over matched RBF-SVM is not statistically established. Applying the same π·tanh feature squashing used by QSVM-ZZ to the classical RBF-SVM substantially reduces the absolute Kermany performance gap, indicating that the classical-to-quantum encoding contributes to the apparent stability. Wider classical representations and fine-tuned ResNet18 additionally demonstrate that conclusions drawn from a severely compressed four-dimensional benchmark should not be generalized to broader model classes. Data-use and redistribution statement This archive contains derived features, mappings, predictions, statistical results, trained model checkpoints, code and analysis outputs. It does not redistribute raw RSNA DICOM images or raw Kermany/PneumoniaMNIST source-i
title: Does a Smaller Performance Drop Really Mean Robustness? A Validation-Locked Evaluation of a Quantum Kernel for Chest X-ray Classification

summary: Where is the place of the human being in the physical picture of the world? This question is usually answered from one of two camps: consciousness is a product of the brain and nothing more; or consciousness is immaterial and does not depend on the body. This work takes a different path — forward from the physical foundation, step by step — and looks at where it leads. The foundation is the work “The Birth of Dimensions: A Formal Skeleton” (BD). It contains nothing but a single assumption: everything is a process, an ideal sine wave, and its centre is the observer. Dimensions are born by squaring: first time, then, by iterating the same square, space and mass. Elementary particles turn out to be a resonance of at least three dimensions — time, space and mass. From the same assumption BD obtains the rules of quantum mechanics, the Lorentz transformations and the masses of particles from the speed of light alone. If the foundation is right, its rule should show up everywhere — including in the work of the brain. And it does: the main ranges of brain rhythms approximately form a ladder of squares — 2–3, 4–9, 16–81 Hz — built in the same way as the tower of levels in BD: the width of the levels in logarithms doubles with every step, and the alpha rhythm falls on the boundary between levels. The rhythm bands are blurred, but that is how it should be: the electroencephalogram is a projection of a higher-frequency process onto a single dimension, and within one level the process is smooth. What matters is something else — resonance between frequencies, and in the brain it was measured long ago. This leads to an assumption: the body is a resonator, and since bodies are alike, this answers the question of why different observers see one common world. Consciousness is then built like an elementary particle — as an agreement of three frequencies linked by squares — only on a higher-frequency level. That is why we see its work but cannot weigh it with instruments of our level; and that is why the world is perceived as three-dimensional. The structure is examined: the “I” is the observer; consciousness is time, the “here and now”; the subconscious is space, the “self” and its history; superconsciousness, intuition, is mass, which is born in self-reflection. From this follows an assumption about the meaning of life as the cultivation of intuition. If consciousness is like a particle, the reverse is also true: every particle may contain what we call consciousness. In the calculations of BD the Milky Way is the image of a neutron, and we live inside it; there are neutrons in almost every atom of our body. And the Universe, if it is like a black hole — part of a particle of a larger world — may be an observer. This is a hypothesis, not a proof. At the end there is a list of ways to test it, and what is established is separated from what is assumed. summary: Code, configuration files, result files and scripts that regenerate every table and figure of the manuscript "Source Audited Evaluation of Lightweight Phishing Detectors for Telecom Text: Leakage, Debiasing, and Conformal Abstention" (Ahmad, Shehzad, Hasan, Hussain), submitted to IEEE Transactions on Artificial Intelligence. The archive contains the source audit (exact and MinHash near duplicate removal, Cramér's V between source and label), the SDAP detector (word BiLSTM and byte CNN under a gradient reversal source adversary) with its ablations, TF IDF baselines, leave one source out evaluation, temperature scaling and split conformal abstention, character level attack perturbations, the per message predictions and logs of the reported run, the figure scripts, and the LaTeX source of the manuscript in the IEEE TAI template. The public corpora (UCI SMS Spam Collection, Enron spam, a Phishing Pot sample and a labelled URL list) are downloaded from their original providers by scripts/fetch_data.sh; see README.md for the full reproduction steps and data licences. Version 2.0 updates the manuscript source and author metadata and redraws the two method diagrams; the experimental results are unchanged from version 1.
title: Source Audited Evaluation of Lightweight Phishing Detectors for Telecom Text: Code and Results

summary: Acute respiratory infections in children comprise etiologically and clinically heterogeneous diseases with overlapping early manifestations, whereas the risk of respiratory failure and other adverse outcomes varies according to age, premorbid conditions, and the causative pathogen. This review aims to analyze current approaches to etiological diagnosis and evidence-based risk factors for severe disease in children. An analytical search covered PubMed/MEDLINE and documents issued by the World Health Organization and the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence for 2015-2026. Priority was given to guidelines, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, diagnostic accuracy studies, and large cohorts. Clinical assessment identifies the anatomical level of respiratory involvement and current severity but cannot reliably establish viral etiology. Nucleic acid amplification remains the most sensitive method for detecting most respiratory viruses. Diagnostic value depends on the timing and quality of specimen collection, panel composition, and clinical context; a positive multiplex result does not establish the causal contribution of every detected agent. Serology has a limited role in an acute episode. Consistently reported baseline risk factors include young age, prematurity, chronic lung disease, hemodynamically significant congenital heart disease, neurological disorders, immunodeficiency or immunosuppressive treatment, and malnutrition. Hypoxemia, apnea, progressive respiratory distress, feeding inability, altered consciousness, and impaired perfusion indicate evolving organ dysfunction and require immediate assessment. Reliable prediction should integrate baseline risk factors with dynamic clinical variables. Any prediction model requires independent validation in the pediatric population for which its use is intended.
title: Acute Respiratory Infections in Children: Current Approaches to Etiological Diagnosis and Prediction of Severe Disease (Literature Review).

summary: STARLI | F091–F100 / 300 Flagship 13 Fission · Volume I · Collective Microrobotic Autonomy, Swarm Safety and Mission Continuity Author: 33  |  Nonclinical Research Design Working Edition v1.3  |  English Zenodo Ten-Volume Overview This ten-volume collection closes the first hundred of the STARLI 300-theme research-design atlas. Research Unit I (F091–F095) examines autonomous sampling, local-to-global coordination, pheromone-like signaling, collision avoidance and collective energy allocation. Research Unit II (F096–F100) examines distributed planning, localization uncertainty, changing network topology, fault isolation and safe mission handoff. Each volume states prospective physical tests rather than completed experimental findings. The ten English working editions total 7,770 PDF pages: 300 candidate mathematical plates, 820 chapter openings, 4,100 independently paginated investigations, 2,000 Research Gates and 330 Phoenix Answer Embryos. The v1.3 Gate-annotation pass contrasts mechanisms, physical witnesses, blinded falsifiers, rivals, stopping boundaries and successor interfaces. These editorial counts and text-screening results do not establish causal independence or scientific validation. The Ten Research Directions F091  Nanorobotic Collective Autonomy Sampling At The Limit — Proposes controlled tests of swarm sampling throughput and identity preservation. A concealed communication partition probes whether completion gains survive the loss of collective coordination, against a centralized full-state controller; collision events and consensus error remain explicit vetoes. F092  Microrobotic Local Collaboration And Global Mission At The Limit — Asks whether agent-to-agent collaboration improves global agreement when robots lack an unmetered global-state feed. Hidden adversarial-neighbor states test dependence on outside tracking; fixed behavior rules with matched energy provide the comparator. F093  Nanorobotic Collective Pheromone Communication At The Limit — Explores prospective chemical-trail or signal-mediated coordination with collision exposure as a primary outcome. Hidden actuator saturation and a matched-actuation single-agent baseline challenge claims that signaling, rather than redundancy or imposed motion, caused the improvement. F094  Microscale Robot Collective Collision Avoidance Control At The Limit — Examines collision-safe motion while monitoring spatial coverage, recovery time and communication burden. A blinded shared-localization bias tests whether apparent avoidance depends on erroneous common position estimates; safety-boundary crossings trigger rejection. F095  Nanorobotic Collective Energy Allocation At The Limit — Tests dynamic allocation of limited energy across agents during dropout and recovery. Hidden agent-loss clusters challenge energy accounting and recovery-time claims against fixed rules with an equal energy budget; persistent unsafe confidence is a stop condition. F096  Microrobotic Distributed Mission Planning At The Limit — Studies task planning without a central controller using communication load, work-per-task and selective abstention as prospective metrics. Hidden network partitions expose plans that depend on unavailable messages, while a matched-actuation single-agent system tests whether coordination adds value. F097  Nanorobotic Collective Localization Uncertainty At The Limit — Tests whether robots can act safely when position confidence is uncertain or neighbors provide deceptive state information. Energy per accepted task, abstention and completion are checked against a full-state centralized benchmark; unrecognized safety-boundary crossings invalidate the claim. F098  Microrobotic Collective Dynamic Topology Control At The Limit — Examines when changing neighbor connections should trigger reconfiguration or justified refusal to proceed

Research Unit II (F086–F090) extends these questions to coupled interface physics, degradability, nonequilibrium adsorption, cross-environment robustness and trustworthy validation. Every proposal requires independently traceable specimens, blinded perturbations and explicit rival explanations; no proposed advantage is reported as measured. Tests interfacial noise, leachate mass and retained function against an inert coupon, separating true interface recognition from bulk-matrix changes. F082  Nanorobotic Interfacial Chemical Memory At The Limit — Asks whether an interfacial chemical state persists beyond coating history or extra ligand loading. A hidden delamination challenge, leachate balance and protein-corona turnover measurements confront an unmodified surface and mature PEG comparator. F083  Biointerface Fluid Shear And Materials Fatigue At The Limit — Examines whether repeated fluid shear and material aging alter retained surface function. Ligand-density-matched covalent coatings, concealed leachate challenges and independent material-identity records distinguish degradation from apparent antifouling caused by lost activity. F084  Nano-Quantum Interface Cross-Sensitivity At The Limit — Challenges a candidate interface readout with blinded ionic-strength shifts and independent corona, coverage and adhesion measurements. An inert same-matrix reference tests whether a measured change belongs to the interface or to the surrounding sample matrix. Hidden surface-age mismatches and PEG controls test false precursors, nonspecific binding and premature failure alarms. F086  Biointerface Multiphysics Coupling At The Limit — Studies the joint effects of adhesion, desorption, electrokinetic state and protein-corona exchange. summary: This paper outlines a comparative structural framework for analyzing how judicial rulings from supranational courts (specifically the CJEU under Article 267 TFEU preliminary references and the ECHR) systematically transform domestic policy parameters without explicit legislative mandates.   Adapted specifically to the institutional mechanics of the French legal order, the framework operationalizes four key structural components:   Judicial Displacement (JD): The structural mechanism through which supranational courts assume primary interpretative authority over national policy, constrained in France by Article 55 of the Constitution.   Administrative Gradualism (AG): The incremental realignment of domestic policy through an iterative sequence of secondary executive and regulatory instruments (décrets, arrêtés, circulaires, and administrative guidance) issued by ministries and independent regulatory bodies (e.g., CNIL, ARCOM).   The Mandate Scale (M_0–M_3): A heuristic metric assessing the spectrum of explicit democratic authorization present within electoral manifestos, winning coalitions, or direct referendums regarding supranational constraints.   Four-Step Operational Cycle: A recurring sequence mapping the trajectory from supranational judicial trigger \rightarrow national administrative response (expanding, reclaiming, or accommodating) \rightarrow democratic legitimacy deficits (input, throughput, output) \rightarrow systemic political outcomes (evolutionary pushback via contrôle de conventionnalité or systemic backlash).   The paper includes a comparative matrix contrasting UK statutory mechanism (HRA 1998, Statutory Instruments) against French constitutional pathways (Sarran, Nicolo, Article 38 ordonnances), along with a rigorous methodology defining a "True-Negative Profile" to test boundary conditions against selection bias.  Note on Origin & Systemic Scope: This publication represents an operational draft outline designed to establish baseline terminology, structural mechanics, and theoretical metrics for ongoing comparative legal research.   This work is a direct spin-off and structural adaptation of the foundational framework established in: Davidson, C. K. S., Judicial Displacement and Administrative Gradualism, DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.24023708.    While the original benchmark paper evaluated these dynamics within a dualist, parliamentary context (specifically United Kingdom immigration policy and prisoner voting rights under ECHR jurisprudence), this adaptation recalibrates the core analytical model to the monist-leaning, semi-presidential institutional architecture of the French Fifth Republic under Article 55 of the 1958 French Constitution.    This draft serves as the immediate European adaptation within a broader comparative research agenda, with future planned adaptations extending the framework to examine administrative realignments, executive rule-making, and judicial review dynamics within the United States constitutional framework.

summary: This analysis examines how computational configuration choices shape resource efficiency in confidential genomic collaboration across institutions. A descriptive secondary analysis uses 14 PRINCESS benchmark configurations published in 2017, comprising seven batch sizes evaluated with compression enabled and disabled across three sites. Matched runtime differences, ratios and joint memory comparisons identify configuration tradeoffs. With compression enabled, increasing batch size from 100 to 10,000 variants reduces runtime by 75.49 percent, while expansion to one million variants provides only 0.38 percent further improvement despite requiring 32.69 times as much memory. Without compression, runtime reaches its observed minimum at 8,000 variants and subsequently increases. Compression enabled records longer enclave runtime in every matched pair. These patterns reveal diminishing processing gains and configuration dependent resource tradeoffs, without isolating their underlying mechanisms. The contribution is a comparative interpretation distinguishing faster execution from economical resource use. The findings refine a resource constraint perspective and support joint evaluation of execution time and memory when configuring protected genomic workflows, with numerical recommendations bounded by the observed benchmark environment.
title: BENCHMARKING CONFIDENTIAL GENOMIC COMPUTING EFFICIENCY THROUGH BATCH SIZE, COMPRESSION, AND MEMORY USE ACROSS COLLABORATIVE SITES

summary: This paper proposes Recursive Anticipatory Argumentation-Control Theory (RAACT), an interdisciplinary framework for representing argumentative discourse as a dynamic, par- tially observed, and recursively updated interaction system. Its central mechanism, Recur- sive Anticipatory Argument-Path Interception (RAAPI), combines contextual observation, pragmatic-linguistic encoding, argument reconstruction, opponent-state estimation, proba- bilistic argument-path forecasting, formal refutation verification, anticipatory intervention, and feedback-based model revision. The framework is developed around the Pre-emptive Refutation Fork Case (PRFC), a primary analytical case in which one participant forecasts an opponent's possible argumenta- tive move and presents a logically evaluated counterargument before that move is explicitly advanced. Subsequent responses are classified into continuation, substitution, qualification, forecast challenge, clarification, and novel argumentative pathways. The mathematical specification introduces latent-state models, observation functions, categorical predictive distributions, Bayesian belief updating, intervention-utility functions, estimation errors, and forecast-evaluation metrics. Conditional mathematical propositions identify what can be established under explicit assumptions, while empirical hypotheses dis- tinguish predictive accuracy from intervention effectiveness and strategic response restriction. RAACT is presented as a formal theoretical architecture and a research program, not as an empirically validated universal law. Its principal scientific obligations are to demonstrate incremental predictive value, establish causal effects under an identifiable research design, prove specific mathematical claims under stated assumptions, and identify boundary conditions through counterexamples and independent replication. Keywords: argumentation theory; linguistic pragmatics; anticipatory reasoning; pre-emptive refutation; cybernetics; feedback control; state estimation; Bayesian forecasting; formal logic; strategic discourse; falsifiability.

summary: Two Hamiltonian systems that share almost nothing in their physical origins turn out to behave identically once their local structure near a 2:1 internal resonance is examined. One system models a pair of flexural modes in a micromechanical resonator through coupled Duffing oscillators. The other models the stretch–bend Fermi resonance of a molecule such as carbon dioxide through a Morse oscillator coupled to a harmonic bend. Both possess an elliptic equilibrium, equal Krein signatures, a frequency ratio close to 2:1, and a cubic resonant coupling. These shared features place them in the same resonant normal-form type, a difference resonance that confines energy exchange rather than driving escape. On the conserved polyad fixed by an initial excitation that places nearly all the energy in the higher-frequency mode, the truncated normal form of any such system collapses to a one-degree-of-freedom problem that depends on only two numbers: a scaled detuning and a scaled anharmonic curvature. Consequently the largest fraction of energy that can be transferred to the lower mode is given by a universal curve whose edges are independent of the curvature. All of the necessary invariants are computed directly from each Hamiltonian before any trajectory is integrated. Numerical integration then confirms the predictions. When the curvature is small the systems follow the one-parameter curve; when it is large they follow the two-parameter curve to high accuracy. A beam whose quartic coefficient is deliberately softened until its curvature matches that of the molecular model reproduces the molecular exchange curve directly, even though the remaining normal-form coefficients differ. An ensemble of sixty randomly drawn members of the same type likewise collapses onto the appropriate universal curve. The residual discrepancy grows roughly linearly with excitation amplitude, as expected from the truncation of the normal form. Two controls mark the boundaries of the result. Reversing one Krein signature converts the same frequency window from bounded exchange into unbounded escape. Weak viscous damping reduces the transferred fraction in the manner predicted by a correspondingly damped reduced model. A quantum treatment of the truncated normal form introduces the polyad number as a third invariant; the lowest Fermi dyad therefore follows a distinct quantum curve rather than the classical one. The findings remain local, confined to two-mode models, and classical except where the quantum analogue is stated explicitly. Within those limits they demonstrate that a dimensionless exchange relation established for one physical system can be transferred to an unrelated system once both have been rescaled by invariants computed from their own Hamiltonians.
title: The Beam That Behaves Like a Molecule

This package contains the data, code and documentation that reproduce every table, figure and number quoted in the text of the paper: the CPS extract and the other inputs, the Stata, R, MATLAB, Python and Julia programs, the reference outputs, and a master script that runs them and verifies the result.

summary: This record contains the supplementary files of the systematic review "Sliding Mode Control of Quadrotor UAVs: A Systematic Review of Convergence Guarantees and Chattering Attenuation" (submitted to Aerospace Science and Technology). ESM_1_search_and_screening.zip - merged and de-duplicated record table (bibliographic data without abstracts), screening rules, every title/abstract screening decision with its reason code, the two validation samples, and the scripts used for de-duplication, screening and the statistics of the systematic map. ESM_2_extraction_sheet.xlsx - extraction sheet of the 2,358 studies of the systematic map, and the full-text evidence coding of the 57 studies selected for full-text analysis (45 included), with the passage on which each coded item is based and a codebook. ESM_3_benchmark_code_and_data.zip - MATLAB code and simulation data of the comparative benchmark of six sliding mode controllers on a 3DR Iris quadrotor model, and the scripts that generate the figures. ESM_4_supplementary_table_and_note.pdf - Supplementary Table S1 (analysis of SMC-based controllers) and Supplementary Note S1 (control laws and gains used in the benchmark).
tags: Sliding mode control; Quadrotor UAV; Systematic review; PRISMA; Fixed-time convergence; Arbitrary-time convergence; Chattering; Benchmark
title: Supplementary data and code for "Sliding Mode Control of Quadrotor UAVs: A Systematic Review of Convergence Guarantees and Chattering Attenuation"

summary: This archive holds the data and code behind the manuscript “Five Inexpensive Checks for Machine-Learned Enzyme Turnover-Number Predictors” by Fatih Aktas and Farida Rahayu. The protocol defines five checks for machine-learned predictors of the enzyme turnover number. They use supplied prediction columns and one measured panel. The five checks are a scale audit, the mutation-response ratio, a kinetics-untrained baseline floor, transfer to external data, and a calibration check. The protocol is applied to six published predictors. The data span 1,571 variants from 130 database-derived campaigns, 23,500 variants from eight deep mutational scans, and two panels of measured turnover numbers. The archive contains the analysis scripts, the JSON output of each script, the extracted datasets, the tables and figures, a README with the execution order, a REPRODUCE guide, and a dated pre-specification note. All kinetic measurements and all model predictions come from the EnzyArena benchmark (Zeng et al., bioRxiv 2026, doi:10.64898/2026.03.29.715152). No new measurements were made. The benchmark release is not redistributed here. Software: Python 3.13, NumPy, SciPy, scikit-learn, RDKit 2026.9.1, Matplotlib 3.11.
title: Data and code for five checks on machine-learned enzyme kcat predictors

summary: Complete reproducibility materials for the manuscript “Auditing Unseen-Attack Transfer in Federated Intrusion Detection: A Controlled Leave-Family-Out Study Across Four NetFlow-v3 Captures.” The deposit contains two complementary archives. 03a_Supplementary_Material.zip contains the complete exploratory revision package, including the R0–R7 workflows, executed revision outputs, CPU diagnostics, statistical sensitivity analyses, convergence data, provenance records, verification scripts, amendments, manifests, and reproduction instructions. 03b_Supplementary_Original_Scores.zip contains the frozen original-study materials, including all 764 original job-score archives (665 main and 99 random-split jobs), raw result records, archived analysis code, and job identities. The original and revision analyses are explicitly distinguished. The revision materials do not replace or modify the frozen original prediction scores. SHA-256 manifests, coverage inventories, and verification scripts are included. The underlying NetFlow-v3 source datasets are not redistributed. The complete reproducibility package is publicly available through this version-specific Zenodo DOI. Identical archives accompany the journal resubmission.
title: Reproducibility Materials for "Auditing Unseen-Attack Transfer in Federated Intrusion Detection: A Controlled Leave-Family-Out Study Across Four NetFlow-v3 Captures"

summary: This dataset supports 121 benchmark tasks for evaluating coding agents on spatial transcriptomics alignment. It combines published tissue datasets and Albis simulations spanning serial-section alignment, cross-technology matching, robustness tests, and three-dimensional reconstruction. Compiled AnnData ( .h5ad ) files provide gene-expression measurements, spatial coordinates, and reference annotations where available. Each task is accompanied by instructions, input and output specifications, data provenance, and a defined scoring profile. The benchmark separates agent-visible inputs from reference information used for evaluation and compares submitted alignments with scripted implementations of published methods.
title: Spatial Transcriptomics Alignment Dataset for Agents

summary: Fuente del Salín (Cantabria, Spain) is one of the few decorated caves where a large assemblage of hand stencils is associated with a Gravettian occupation, including a hearth and evidence of pigment processing. Using a 3D reconstruction of the cave’s Palaeolithic state, GIS-based measurements and multivariate statistics, we analysed the spatial organisation of its 55 hand stencils. All are located near the entrance, in accessible, visible spaces able to accommodate several people, unlike the only other motif, deeper in the cave. The assemblage nonetheless includes distinct spatial groups, compositions and unusual orientations. The hearth could have lit more than half of the hands, and both kernel density analysis and hierarchical clustering single out the group surrounding it. These results strengthen the hypothesis that the hands and the occupation were contemporaneous and, together with Gargas, suggest that hand stencils could be produced in spaces also used for everyday activities.
title: By the Light of the Fire: Characterisation and Spatial Organisation of the Hand Stencils at Fuente del Salín in Relation to their Archaeological Context

summary: GLIAG essay, Geology, Minerals & Petroleum of Suriname, Revision 1.1 (7 November 2026). Every barrel of oil in the Golden Lane sits in sand that was once a mountain on the Guiana Shield. The essay follows two billion years of Suriname's geology in six acts: the Trans-Amazonian ocean floor and island arc (2.18–2.13 Ga), collision and orogenic gold (2.13–2.06 Ga), the Bakhuis ultrahigh-temperature granulites (2.07–2.05 Ga), the felsic flare-up (1.99–1.95 Ga), the Roraima sandstone and the quiet craton (1.87–1.0 Ga), and the opening of the Atlantic that built the Golden Lane turbidite fans. It links each map unit to its mineral system (gold at Rosebel, Merian and Overman; plateau and coastal bauxite; Cu–Ni–Cr, Li–Sn–Ta–Be and Nb–REE occurrences; Tambaredjo heavy oil; Golden Lane light oil) and discusses the shield-to-slope source-to-sink system. It closes with a FACT · MISSING · GLIAG JUDGEMENT · TRIGGER evidence register, a glossary, a references annex and an amendment register. Revision 1.1 corrects the provenance reading of Girault et al. (2023): their Early Cretaceous Demerara Plateau zircons are mainly Pan-African–Brasiliano and sourced from the French Guiana margin, so the shield origin of the Late Cretaceous Golden Lane sands is presented as a working hypothesis supported by Roddaz et al. (2021). Literature-based interpretation for education and research; not a resource assessment or investment advice. Location: Zoetermeer & Paramaribo. Text-and-data mining reserved under Art. 4(3) Directive (EU) 2019/790 and Art. 15o Dutch Auteurswet.
title: Suriname: a Palimpsest of Two Billion Years

summary: This archive accompanies the manuscript Sharp Cycle Stability and Auditable Error Control for Differentiable Optimal Transport. Version 2026-11-08-hcc-r1 includes the adaptive controller and outward verifier, records for 240 pressure workloads and 60 paired Fashion-MNIST training runs, 40 manufactured numerical stress problems, and scripts to replay the experiments and regenerate the tables and vector figures. Start with README.md. The fixed CT feature pool is a processed subset of histogram features from Graf et al. (2011), Relative location of CT slices on axial axis, UCI Machine Learning Repository (https://doi.org/10.24432/C5CP6G, CC BY 4.0). The reproduction instructions point to the original Fashion-MNIST repository. The bundled Elsevier bibliography style is distributed under the LaTeX Project Public License, version 1.3 or later. The earlier benchmark and fixed inputs are documented in the previous version (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24044383).
title: Reproducibility package for Sharp Cycle Stability and Auditable Error Control for Differentiable Optimal Transport

Version 2026-11-08-hcc-r1 includes the adaptive controller and outward verifier, records for 240 pressure workloads and 60 paired Fashion-MNIST training runs, 40 manufactured numerical stress problems, and scripts to replay the experiments and regenerate the tables and vector figures. Start with README.md. The fixed CT feature pool is a processed subset of histogram features from Graf et al. (2011), Relative location of CT slices on axial axis, UCI Machine Learning Repository (https://doi.org/10.24432/C5CP6G, CC BY 4.0). The reproduction instructions point to the original Fashion-MNIST repository. The bundled Elsevier bibliography style is distributed under the LaTeX Project Public License, version 1.3 or later. The earlier benchmark and fixed inputs are documented in the previous version (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24044383).

summary: This repository contains the analytical datasets, Python scripts, numerical outputs, plots and reproducibility documentation accompanying the manuscript Can strontium isotopes track changing mobility patterns? Evidence from La Tène Central Europe. The repository is intended to support transparent evaluation, replication and further comparative research on Iron Age mobility, life histories and the relationship between human movement and regional geological environments. The repository supports reproduction of the downstream statistical analyses, including: Cemetery-level isotope distributions and local/non-local classifications. Individual-level mobility estimates using two complementary classification rules: Rule A (any sampled tooth potentially non-local) and Rule B (one predefined permanent reference tooth). Mixed-effects logistic models evaluating chronological, demographic and burial material-group associations while accounting for repeated teeth from the same individual. Sensitivity analyses, paired-tooth comparisons and reconstruction of childhood strontium exposure histories. Cross-cemetery isotope comparisons and relationships between lithological diversity and strontium variability at 1, 5, 10 and 20 km spatial scales. Reproducible analytical plots and numerical verification against the published supplementary results.
title: Strontium isotopes and mobility in La Tène Central Europe: analytical data, Python code and reproducibility materials

summary: forelint is an open-source Python library that checks what a forecasting backtest score hides, before anyone acts on it. Leakage between related series: GroupTimeSplit holds out the future of entities the model never saw, and split_optimism reports how much random, group and time-only splits overstate accuracy against it. Run-to-run noise floor: noise_floor measures the spread of repeated runs and the smallest difference that exceeds it. Model comparison across many series: Diebold-Mariano with the Harvey-Leybourne-Newbold correction on long-format panels, and the model confidence set of Hansen, Lunde and Nason (2011). Backtest audit: per-item bias, tracking signal, error concentration, MASE and RMSSE, and forecast value added against a baseline, broken down by demand class (smooth, erratic, intermittent, lumpy), with stockout periods excluded from scoring. On one store of the public M5 data, backtested at ten non-overlapping forecast origins, a gradient-boosting model was 3.9% worse than a 28-day moving average on absolute error and worse on 58% of items. By demand class it added +5.0% on smooth items and lost −10.5% on intermittent and −9.2% on lumpy ones. Source: github.com/davidmashiah/forelint . Author: David Mashiah .
title: forelint: lint your forecast backtests before you trust a score

Leakage between related series: GroupTimeSplit holds out the future of entities the model never saw, and split_optimism reports how much random, group and time-only splits overstate accuracy against it. Run-to-run noise floor: noise_floor measures the spread of repeated runs and the smallest difference that exceeds it. Model comparison across many series: Diebold-Mariano with the Harvey-Leybourne-Newbold correction on long-format panels, and the model confidence set of Hansen, Lunde and Nason (2011). Backtest audit: per-item bias, tracking signal, error concentration, MASE and RMSSE, and forecast value added against a baseline, broken down by demand class (smooth, erratic, intermittent, lumpy), with stockout periods excluded from scoring. On one store of the public M5 data, backtested at ten non-overlapping forecast origins, a gradient-boosting model was 3.9% worse than a 28-day moving average on absolute error and worse on 58% of items. By demand class it added +5.0% on smooth items and lost −10.5% on intermittent and −9.2% on lumpy ones. Source: github.com/davidmashiah/forelint . Author: David Mashiah .

summary: Dataset of the paper Toward universal excited-state machine-learned potentials: a local excitation Hamiltonian for size consistency and transferability (P. Friederich). TD-DFT (ωB97X-D/6-31G*, full linear response, TURBOMOLE 7.5.1) labels for 303,061 geometries of 106,933 closed-shell organic molecules with C, H, N, O, F (and S in some dyes and ladder molecules): S0 energies and forces, the ten lowest singlet excitation energies with oscillator strengths, and analytic S1, S2, and S3 forces. Geometries: QCDGE minima, thermal geometries from GFN2-xTB dynamics at 300–1000 K, geometries from model-driven S1/S2 dynamics (four active-learning rounds), and test molecules beyond the training distribution (larger molecules from ZINC, dyes from two experimental databases, homologous ladder series up to 30 heavy atoms). Splits of the benchmark, dye-augmented, and production models of the paper. Also included: S1–S3 forces at equilibrium geometries of 2,499 test molecules; pairs of molecules at 2.5–20 Å with TD-DFT dimer spectra; twelve TD-ωB97X-D S1 reference trajectories with initial conditions and a validity flag; Löwdin hole and electron populations and charge-transfer numbers of the ten roots for 25,808 geometries; and the TURBOMOLE input and output files (without MO files) of 200,445 calculations. The file README.md describes all files, fields, units, and splits.
title: TD-ωB97X-D excited-state energies and forces of 106,933 molecules at equilibrium, thermal, and excited-state geometries

summary: Code, processed data, results and manuscript sources for G. Lim, "Low empirical Péclet numbers, rotating transport hubs and crisis-dependent macro forcing on a 27-year time-varying equity network", submitted to Physica A (2026; transferred from Chaos, Solitons & Fractals). The archive KRX27y_Transport_Network_v1_2.zip is the unchanged version 1.2.0 deposit (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23912552), which the manuscript cites for its baseline inputs: the Python pipeline (scripts 01–17), the split-corrected daily panel of 2,767 KRX stocks (2000-01-04 to 2026-11-02), the rolling 200-name universe (1,283 windows), survivorship diagnostics, window-level network statistics on residual planar maximally filtered graphs, nodal advective/diffusive flux tables and PMFG edge tables, stress composites, macro boundary forcing regressions, the early-warning evaluation and the sector/hub/spatial-concentration analysis. Version 1.3.0 adds PhysicaA_Revision_v1_3.zip with the Physica A version of the manuscript (LaTeX sources, generated numbers and tables, figures, PDF) and the robustness material behind its new sections: an operator-normalisation audit and a conditional edge-sign null on all 1,283 windows, graph-construction and estimation-length checks and a temporal circular-shift null on 24 windows, a known-direction stochastic control, and paired early-warning comparisons on identical windows with four bootstrap block lengths, together with the scripts that produce them from the version 1.2.0 inputs. Every number in the manuscript is generated from the CSV files in this deposit. Raw daily prices are not redistributed; the scripts re-download them from the public sources named in README.md. The companion study on a fixed ten-year universe has its own deposit (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23891620). Code under scripts/ and robustness/ is MIT-licensed; data, results and figures are CC BY 4.0.

summary: GPU-native Julia framework for CT and photon-counting CT simulation, reconstruction, and quantitative spectral imaging. Provides distance-driven forward projection (with Siddon ray tracing as an alternative), polychromatic Beer-Lambert physics with vendor-realistic detector response (MC-derived LUTs for GE Gemstone scintillator and Siemens NAEOTOM Alpha CdTe), FDK, helical WFBP and hybrid iterative reconstruction, sinogram and image-domain beam-hardening correction, projection-domain dual-kVp and PCCT material decomposition (K-channel profile likelihood, Cong 2022), spectral denoising, and virtual monoenergetic imaging (VMI + Grant 2014 Mono+) — all dispatching transparently across CPU, Metal, CUDA, and ROCm via AcceleratedKernels.jl.
title: BasisSimulator.jl: Open-source polychromatic CT simulation with a GPU-portable reconstruction stack

summary: First public release of Hydrograd v2.0, the Python/JAX successor of Hydrograd.jl (v1.0). Differentiable finite-volume solver for the 2D shallow water equations and the Universal SWEs (neural-network closures) on unstructured SRH-2D meshes, in double precision on CPUs and GPUs. Explicit SSP-RK3 and Tsit5 integrators with checkpointed reverse-mode gradients Steady Newton solver with a coloured sparse Jacobian and implicit-function-theorem gradients Implicit backward Euler / Crank-Nicolson stepper with per-step adjoints Hydrostatic reconstruction + HLLC with second-order MUSCL, wet/dry capable Inversion of Manning's n, bed elevation, inflow hydrographs, exit stage, vegetation and porous drag Closure learning (USWEs) with local neural-network laws Reads SRH-2D cases; HEC-RAS 2D meshes via pyHMT2D The cases, scripts and data of the model description paper (Liu, Hydrograd v2.0: differentiable shallow-water modelling on unstructured meshes, in preparation) are in paper/ Documentation: docs/manual.md . Licence: MIT.
title: Hydrograd: a differentiable two-dimensional shallow-water model on unstructured meshes

Explicit SSP-RK3 and Tsit5 integrators with checkpointed reverse-mode gradients Steady Newton solver with a coloured sparse Jacobian and implicit-function-theorem gradients Implicit backward Euler / Crank-Nicolson stepper with per-step adjoints Hydrostatic reconstruction + HLLC with second-order MUSCL, wet/dry capable Inversion of Manning's n, bed elevation, inflow hydrographs, exit stage, vegetation and porous drag Closure learning (USWEs) with local neural-network laws Reads SRH-2D cases; HEC-RAS 2D meshes via pyHMT2D The cases, scripts and data of the model description paper (Liu, Hydrograd v2.0: differentiable shallow-water modelling on unstructured meshes, in preparation) are in paper/ Documentation: docs/manual.md . Licence: MIT.
title: Hydrograd: a differentiable two-dimensional shallow-water model on unstructured meshes

summary: The Riemann hypothesis is nature's way of avoiding an information entropy collapse: the entropy over the modes of the prime fluctuation is conserved in log x only if every zero carries the same weight. Shannon's bound makes the variance the currency of the problem: the smooth count of the primes is a first moment, a first moment holds no distribution, and so any statement about the size of the prime fluctuation is a statement about a discarded second moment, which for the primes is the set of zeros of the zeta function. The step is the one Perelman took for Ricci flow; he established the invariant, and here its cause is given: unitarity. The quantum connection is the reason a lock exists in the first place. The prime fluctuation is a state acted on by the matrix M(t) = diag(e^(δ_n t)  e^(iγ_n t)); the variance is its norm, and it is conserved, with a fixed share for every mode, only when M is unitary, that is, when every zero carries the weight ½ , the single fixed point of the two fold symmetry of the functional equation. The Riemann hypothesis is then the statement that the prime fluctuation is a closed quantum system. We measure the second moment directly on 100,000 zeros and on 10,000 zeros each near zero number 10^12, 10^21 and 10^22. Six results follow. With every zero carrying the same weight, the variance of the scaled prime fluctuation is the same in every window of log x: 0.0460 with a spread of 0.0010 over eight windows up to log x = 30, against the closed form 0.0462. A single mode moved off the line by δ grows in variance as x^(2δ). The measured growth factors agree with e^(6δ) per window to within half a percent. The zeros interfere to produce the primes. At the 25 prime powers up to 60 the measured spike is 0.9995 of the predicted height with a scatter of 0.0006, and the smallest spike is 208 times the largest value at any other integer. The zeros are stiff. Neighbours closer than a tenth of the mean spacing occur 120 times less often than without stiffness, the power of the complex amplitude in reciprocal space follows the unitary ramp, and the count variance saturates at a level fixed by the primes: 0.36 at height 4 × 10^4 and 0.52 near 10^21, as predicted. The primes hold each zero in a harmonic well. The measured stiffness agrees with K = (2/|ρ|^2 )⟨(log x)^2⟩ to within one percent for the low zeros. One ancilla qubit, read in X and Y, returns both the primes and the ramp from a register that holds the zeros with equal weight. Forcing one mode off the line is not unitary, and the entropy over modes collapses from log N toward zero. The restoring force acts on the position of each zero. The stiffness between neighbours is a two point property, carried by the square of the prime sum and not by its linear response: that sum, with no zero in it, rebuilds the ramp of the first 100,000 zeros to within 0.006, including their position under the unitary ramp. By sieve to x=10^9 the true primes hold one variance at every scale, 0.0461, where random primes are 338 times louder and growing, and the Möbius sum holds 0.0289 where random signs give 0.61. The Davenport and Heilbronn function, which has the same symmetry and no product over primes (no Euler product), shows the collapse with nothing moved: below height 2,000 one zero in twelve is off the line, its variance grows by a factor of 526, and its entropy over modes is not conserved. Its two components, the Dirichlet L functions modulo 5, each have a product over primes and each hold the lock: all 4,057 zeros found below that height are on the line, the variance stays at its closed form 0.2032, and the entropy is constant. The Davenport and Heilbronn function is the open system: a mode off the line leaks by its δ, and its entropy collapse is the removal, from the lowest δ up, of layers of modes that each keep their own lock. summary: Computational verification and figure code for the manuscript “Earnings Management, Cultural Distance, and Organizational Design.” The archive contains twelve programs: symbolic re-derivation of every closed form (30 checks), randomized property tests at 200,000 draws (22 claims), an independent reconstruction of the equilibrium map including the mandated-minimum analysis (37 checks), machine proofs over unbounded real domains in Z3 (22 claims), Lean-kernel-checked certificates on parameter boxes (12 claims), verification of the online appendix (21 checks), a Lean 4 file proving the eighteen core lemmas against mathlib with a zero-axiom audit, two driver scripts, and the three figure programs. run_checks.ps1 runs every layer and writes verification_report.txt, which is included from a passing run. Requirements: Python 3.12 with numpy, sympy, scipy, matplotlib, z3-solver, and leancert, and Lean 4 with mathlib for the skeleton. License: MIT.
title: Verification and Figure Code for "Earnings Management, Cultural Distance, and Organizational Design"

summary: Delay-Doppler (DD) modulations, such as Zak-transform-based orthogonal time frequency space (Zak-OTFS) modulation, represent the channel as a sparse set of delay and Doppler shifts, which makes them well suited for radar sensing. Sensing with a single DD frame, however, is unambiguous only when the channel spread factor, i.e., the product of the delay and Doppler spreads, is less then one. Long-range mobility scenarios, including drones, airplanes, low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites, and underwater acoustic links, typically violate this crystallization condition, so that a single frame aliases the target delays, Doppler shifts, or both. Existing methods add a time-frequency pilot to a conventional DD frame, resolve the aliasing in only one dimension, and assume integer delays and Doppler shifts. We propose a frame design that combines multiple DD bases with different delay and Doppler periods, which together cover an overspread channel with fractional delays and Doppler shifts, using the same bandwidth and frame size. We show that modular arithmetic on the peak positions uniquely recovers each target by pairing the peaks through their common projection and their gains, and we derive the condition under which this pairing is ambiguous. We implement the design with two superimposed Zak-OTFS frames and propose two receivers: dual-frame sensing (DS), which performs the joint detection directly, and DS with cross-pilot cancellation (DS-XC), which additionally cancels the cross-pilot interference, re-estimates the gains by joint least squares, and removes ghost targets. Both receivers maintain a detection rate close to one as the spread factor grows, and DS-XC also achieves the lowest false-alarm rate and channel estimation error among all the compared systems. In a 100 km drone scenario, DS-XC outperforms all baselines, with a complexity that grows near-linearly with the time-bandwidth product.

summary: The scarcity of labeled underwater acoustic data limits the development of data-driven models for marine acoustic monitoring, motivating the use of self-supervised learning to exploit the abundance of unlabeled recordings. However, large-scale data alone does not guarantee effective representation learning, because model performance is strongly influenced by the distribution of the training data. To facilitate such training data, this study introduces a scalable curation pipeline that curates 3,000 hours from 41 years of raw NOAA hydrophone recordings, producing MarineSet, a large-scale and diverse dataset designed for underwater acoustic learning. A baseline model, MarineNet, trained on MarineSet achieves competitive performance on marine mammal call and ship-type classification, highlighting the value of systematic data curation for developing self-supervised learning models in underwater acoustics.

summary: The transmission of shock waves generated by underwater electrical foil explosions across solid materials with varying acoustic impedances and thicknesses is investigated. Copper foils with thicknesses of 10 and 18 $μ$m are exploded on planar substrates of aluminum, copper, and 3D-printed PLA with thicknesses up to 5 mm using a multi-gigawatt pulsed-power electrical discharge. The resulting shocks are visualized in water using high-speed shadowgraphy at 5 million frames per second, while high-resolution fiber optic hydrophone measurements provide direct quantitative measurements of shock strength after transmission through the impedance-mismatched materials. One-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic simulations are used to reproduce the foil explosion dynamics and provide insight into the thermodynamic, acoustic, and electrical properties of the foil during the explosion. The results show that shock transmission is governed not only by the impedance mismatch at the solid--water interface but also by the finite thickness and dynamic response of the supporting material. These findings provide a quantitative framework for understanding and controlling shock transmission in underwater electrical foil explosions and establish the feasibility and limitations of using solid substrates as structural supports in complex shock-generating geometries.

summary: This dataset provides the numerical inputs, source code, reference results, and reproduction workflow accompanying “Light in Light Bubbles — Gravitational Light in the Phraqtal Field” ( https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23652779 ). Version 2.0 preserves the numerical baseline of version 0.2: stationary-core calculations, regime-channel coupling, integrated gravitational-source calculations, static three-knot comparisons, constrained-curvature diagnostics, and analytical examples for tension-front energy, arrival geometry, and conditional golden-ratio relations. Original numerical programs, input fields, parameters, dependencies, and comparison tolerances remain unchanged. The historical Google Colab replay of October 27, 2026, passed 11 comparison groups and 3,055 checks within the declared tolerances. Its verification records are retained as historical evidence, not presented as a newly executed version-2.0 numerical replay. The extension adds the complete expanded German manuscript and 110 finite exact algebraic controls for magnetic twist organization, the constitutive magnetization readout, source variations, and a conditional magnetic–gravitational response. These controls distinguish directed organization from quadratic source contributions and retain the direct source term in the response calculation. No new core, regime-chain, numerical field-response, or physical-time field-evolution calculations were performed for this extension. The magnetic readout remains an explicit constitutive model choice; its physical calibration and validation against measurements remain open. The algebraic controls do not establish a measured magnetic response or derive the numerical value of Newton’s gravitational constant. The single-cell Colab notebook defaults to integrity checks and the new algebraic extension. Replaying the historical numerical calculations is optional. Release instructions and the new executable interface are in English. The expanded manuscript is in German; the original English manuscript is also retained. The package includes checksums, claim-to-material mappings, and separate historical and extension verification records.

summary: CronNet-Holo: A Unified Research Programme Author: Luis Morató de Dalmases Research Initiative: CronNet-Holo Initiative — Theory of Time Research Unit Version: 1.0 — November 2026 Document type: Research programme / preprint collection Language: English  Abstract This Zenodo record presents the complete CronNet-Holo research programme as a unified collection of manuscripts, technical specifications, and computational audits. The programme investigates a four-layer mathematical architecture for the relation between discrete geometry (the regular 600-cell), finite group representation theory (the binary icosahedral group 2I ≅ SL(2,5)), spectral operators, noncommutative geometry in the sense of Connes, and possible physical interpretations connected with M-theory and the Standard Model. The architecture is organized as: SFDG → Greg → SGUP 600 Cell → QSVG with two transversal modules: TELOS (teleological orientation and prioritization) PHYSCON (physical connection and testability). This record collects eleven documents and seven computational audit files: Manuscripts and specifications (PDFs): CronNet-Holo–Connes: Construction of a Triple Spectral Program TELOS and PHYSCON: Formal Definition of the Two Transversal Modules Spectral Frequency Data Layer and SFDG Annex G — FDL: Interface between Greg and the Frequency Data Layer CronNet-Holo H6 v9: Integral Four-Layer Architecture Regenerative Syntactic Grammar (Greg) — Version 5.1 Canonical Signatures of SER and CONFINAR Inverse Temporal Symmetry Hypothesis (H-STI) Temporal Reversal Operator: Representation Theory and the 53-Dimensional Sector Compression Grammar: M-Theory and Connes as Local Reflections CronNet-Holo–M-Theory Computational audits (PY and TXT): A. Geometric and Spectral Audit of the 600-Cell (H6 v5) B. Integral Audit 600-Cell / M53 C. SGUP 600-Cell Audit Throughout, the programme distinguishes definitions, exact mathematical identities, conditional propositions, computational results, hypotheses, conjectures, physical interpretations, and open problems. No claim is made that the programme proves the Riemann hypothesis, derives the Standard Model, or establishes an experimentally validated physical theory. 1. The Four-Layer Architecture 1.1 Canonical order The fundamental architecture of CronNet-Holo is the ordered composition SFDG → Greg → SGUP 600 Cell → QSVG. The four layers are necessary and non-interchangeable within the architectural design adopted in this programme. 1.2 Layer responsibilities     Layer Responsibility Main output SFDG Data governance, provenance, traceability Structured registry Greg Formal language and typed operations Typed expressions SGUP 600 Cell Geometric, combinatorial, and spectral construction Models, operators, spectra QSVG Geometric and spectral verification Certificates, invariants, relations 1.3 Transversal modules TELOS and PHYSCON are not additional layers. They are transversal modules that can interact with the four layers.     Module Responsibility Central question TELOS Orientation and prioritization What should we do next? PHYSCON Physical connection and testability What can we predict and test? 2. CronNet-Holo–Connes: Spectral Triple Construction 2.1 Objective The objective is to study whether the combinatorial and spectral geometry of the 600-cell can provide an initial finite structure for constructing a Connes-type spectral triple (A, H, D), where: A is an involutive algebra represented on a Hilbert space; H is a Hilbert space; D is a self-adjoint operator with compact resolvent; the commutators [D, π(a)] are bounded for the elements of a suitable dense subalgebra. summary: This paper develops a scale-spanning account of latent vibration and frequency manifestation within Extended Classical Mechanics (ECM). It examines the relationship between complete latent vibration, the negative and positive displacement domains around the manifestable origin, and the eligibility of positive displacement for progression towards physical manifestation. The development distinguishes the complete latent-vibration interval from the directed displacement associated with manifestation, establishing the proposed Pre-Latent and Pre-Planck threshold relationships in terms of the Planck length. The analysis further develops phase-dependent frequency relations below the Planck threshold and considers the proposed frequency increments associated with the Pre-Latent and Pre-Planck domains. It then presents a state-dependent sequence of energy–frequency transformations across latent, phase, and manifested states, including the reverse progression associated with dissolution. Within this framework, frequency and displacement are treated as related physical parameters whose coefficients depend on the corresponding phase domain. The paper also distinguishes the phase-state potential-energy mass representation from the mass contribution associated with the manifested domain. It formulates the effective-mass relationship and separates this ECM representation from the distinct dark-energy-related mass representation. Taken together, these developments present an integrated theoretical description of latent vibration, manifestation eligibility, threshold transitions, energy–frequency relations, and mass-state transformations within the proposed ECM framework.
title: Complete Latent Vibration and Frequency Manifestation Eligibility in Extended Classical Mechanics

summary: Complete reproducibility materials for the manuscript “Auditing Unseen-Attack Transfer in Federated Intrusion Detection: A Controlled Leave-Family-Out Study Across Four NetFlow-v3 Captures.” The deposit contains two complementary archives. 03a_Supplementary_Material.zip contains the complete exploratory revision package, including the R0–R7 workflows, executed revision outputs, CPU diagnostics, statistical sensitivity analyses, convergence data, provenance records, verification scripts, amendments, manifests, and reproduction instructions. 03b_Supplementary_Original_Scores.zip contains the frozen original-study materials, including all 764 original job-score archives (665 main and 99 random-split jobs), raw result records, archived analysis code, and job identities. summary: This dataset supports 121 benchmark tasks for evaluating coding agents on spatial transcriptomics alignment. It combines published tissue datasets and Albis simulations spanning serial-section alignment, cross-technology matching, robustness tests, and three-dimensional reconstruction. Compiled AnnData ( .h5ad ) files provide gene-expression measurements, spatial coordinates, and reference annotations where available. Each task is accompanied by instructions, input and output specifications, data provenance, and a defined scoring profile. The benchmark separates agent-visible inputs from reference information used for evaluation and compares submitted alignments with scripted implementations of published methods.
title: Spatial Transcriptomics Alignment Dataset for Agents

summary: How should complex chemical data be stored and communicated to meet chemists' different needs? Chemists identify, classify, describe, annotate and store their structures, and each need asks for something different. For atomically precise metal clusters (APMCs) and the cluster-assembled materials (CAMs) built from them, this deposit proposes a fourfold framework for their description, naming and identification: it writes each structure down once, in a standard descriptor format, and derives from it the names and identifiers that each need calls for. The problem. The same cluster appears as Au25, Au25(PET)18 or an acronym, and two Au38(PET)24 isomers are told apart by their discoverers' initials. Isomers, substitution sites, exchanged ligands and assemblies have no names. Databases hold coordinates but nothing searchable about core, staples, isomer or assembly. The InChI now encodes whole clusters, but not their handedness, and it does not yet describe crystals or cluster-assembled materials. The solution, a fourfold framework: describe once, derive the rest. APMC-META , the descriptor format: composition, core, surface motifs, ligands, symmetry, topology, isomerism, exchange, electrons, assembly and provenance, for describing and storing a cluster. APMC SYSNOM names for people, e.g. gold-25 18(2-phenylethane-1-thiolato) cluster(1−, (0/I), 8e−, Ih). APMC-ID labels for papers and tables, e.g. Au25(PET)18−–Ih. CluChI layered strings for machines and databases; reported with the InChI, they identify a cluster completely. The shortest complete form is a pair of keys: the CluChIKey at the level of description that makes the cluster unique, and the InChIKey of the whole structure. The framework is extensible: new descriptors enter through a versioned registry, and annotation never changes a key. It describes clusters at four levels (composition, core and shell, isomer, substitution and exchange) plus assemblies, and is set out in 107 rules and 35 worked examples, from the naked Au20 cluster to cluster frameworks and co-crystals. Who it is for: cluster chemists, crystallographers and database curators, cheminformaticians and InChI developers, data scientists, and IUPAC task groups and editors. What is needed next: InChI extensions with the InChI Trust (handedness, a bond convention for clusters); community conventions (cut-offs, symmetry tolerance, electron counts, linker charges); open implementations of the assigner and validator; testing on the COD and CSD by independent annotators; and an updated cluster definition that covers protected clusters and their surface motifs. What to read first: the one-page overview (file 1); the summary (file 2); then the guide for your identifier (files 3–5). The monograph (file 6) is the full specification and the document to cite; the data (file 7) hold every name, APMC-ID, CluChI record and CluChIKey of the examples (JSON, CSV) and model coordinates (XYZ). Status: the names and identifiers are the author's proposals, prepared as a contribution to the IUPAC Task Group on Naming Naked and Protected Atomically Precise Metal Clusters (IUPAC project 2024-014-2-500, https://iupac.org/project/2024-014-2-500/ ). They are not IUPAC Recommendations and have not been reviewed or endorsed by IUPAC or by the task group. Discussions with the task group members are acknowledged in the monograph. A research software prototype generated and checked the records; it is not released, and the monograph, not the code, is the specification for independent implementations. All figures were drawn from atomic coordinates by scripts or by hand; none was produced by a generative image model. The scene files of the structure pictures of the models built for the monograph are in the data archive (file 7).
title: Systematic Naming and Identification of Atomically Precise Metal Clusters and Cluster-Assembled Materials

summary: GLIAG essay, Geology, Minerals & Petroleum of Suriname, Revision 1.1 (7 November 2026). Every barrel of oil in the Golden Lane sits in sand that was once a mountain on the Guiana Shield. The essay follows two billion years of Suriname's geology in six acts: the Trans-Amazonian ocean floor and island arc (2.18–2.13 Ga), collision and orogenic gold (2.13–2.06 Ga), the Bakhuis ultrahigh-temperature granulites (2.07–2.05 Ga), the felsic flare-up (1.99–1.95 Ga), the Roraima sandstone and the quiet craton (1.87–1.0 Ga), and the opening of the Atlantic that built the Golden Lane turbidite fans. It links each map unit to its mineral system (gold at Rosebel, Merian and Overman; plateau and coastal bauxite; Cu–Ni–Cr, Li–Sn–Ta–Be and Nb–REE occurrences; Tambaredjo heavy oil; Golden Lane light oil) and discusses the shield-to-slope source-to-sink system. It closes with a FACT · MISSING · GLIAG JUDGEMENT · TRIGGER evidence register, a glossary, a references annex and an amendment register. Revision 1.1 corrects the provenance reading of Girault et al. (2023): their Early Cretaceous Demerara Plateau zircons are mainly Pan-African–Brasiliano and sourced from the French Guiana margin, so the shield origin of the Late Cretaceous Golden Lane sands is presented as a working hypothesis supported by Roddaz et al. (2021). Literature-based interpretation for education and research; not a resource assessment or investment advice. Location: Zoetermeer & Paramaribo. Text-and-data mining reserved under Art. 4(3) Directive (EU) 2019/790 and Art. 15o Dutch Auteurswet.
title: Suriname: a Palimpsest of Two Billion Years

summary: First public release of Hydrograd v2.0, the Python/JAX successor of Hydrograd.jl (v1.0). Differentiable finite-volume solver for the 2D shallow water equations and the Universal SWEs (neural-network closures) on unstructured SRH-2D meshes, in double precision on CPUs and GPUs. Explicit SSP-RK3 and Tsit5 integrators with checkpointed reverse-mode gradients Steady Newton solver with a coloured sparse Jacobian and implicit-function-theorem gradients Implicit backward Euler / Crank-Nicolson stepper with per-step adjoints Hydrostatic reconstruction + HLLC with second-order MUSCL, wet/dry capable Inversion of Manning's n, bed elevation, inflow hydrographs, exit stage, vegetation and porous drag Closure learning (USWEs) with local neural-network laws Reads SRH-2D cases; HEC-RAS 2D meshes via pyHMT2D The cases, scripts and data of the model description paper (Liu, Hydrograd v2.0: differentiable shallow-water modelling on unstructured meshes, in preparation) are in paper/ Documentation: docs/manual.md . Licence: MIT.
title: Hydrograd: a differentiable two-dimensional shallow-water model on unstructured meshes

summary: The Riemann hypothesis is nature's way of avoiding an information entropy collapse: the entropy over the modes of the prime fluctuation is conserved in log x only if every zero carries the same weight. Shannon's bound makes the variance the currency of the problem: the smooth count of the primes is a first moment, a first moment holds no distribution, and so any statement about the size of the prime fluctuation is a statement about a discarded second moment, which for the primes is the set of zeros of the zeta function. The step is the one Perelman took for Ricci flow; he established the invariant, and here its cause is given: unitarity. The quantum connection is the reason a lock exists in the first place. The prime fluctuation is a state acted on by the matrix M(t) = diag(e^(δ_n t)  e^(iγ_n t)); the variance is its norm, and it is conserved, with a fixed share for every mode, only when M is unitary, that is, when every zero carries the weight ½ , the single fixed point of the two fold symmetry of the functional equation. The Riemann hypothesis is then the statement that the prime fluctuation is a closed quantum system. We measure the second moment directly on 100,000 zeros and on 10,000 zeros each near zero number 10^12, 10^21 and 10^22. Six results follow. With every zero carrying the same weight, the variance of the scaled prime fluctuation is the same in every window of log x: 0.0460 with a spread of 0.0010 over eight windows up to log x = 30, against the closed form 0.0462. A single mode moved off the line by δ grows in variance as x^(2δ). The measured growth factors agree with e^(6δ) per window to within half a percent. The zeros interfere to produce the primes. At the 25 prime powers up to 60 the measured spike is 0.9995 of the predicted height with a scatter of 0.0006, and the smallest spike is 208 times the largest value at any other integer. The zeros are stiff. Neighbours closer than a tenth of the mean spacing occur 120 times less often than without stiffness, the power of the complex amplitude in reciprocal space follows the unitary ramp, and the count variance saturates at a level fixed by the primes: 0.36 at height 4 × 10^4 and 0.52 near 10^21, as predicted. The primes hold each zero in a harmonic well. The measured stiffness agrees with K = (2/|ρ|^2 )⟨(log x)^2⟩ to within one percent for the low zeros. One ancilla qubit, read in X and Y, returns both the primes and the ramp from a register that holds the zeros with equal weight. Forcing one mode off the line is not unitary, and the entropy over modes collapses from log N toward zero. The restoring force acts on the position of each zero. The stiffness between neighbours is a two point property, carried by the square of the prime sum and not by its linear response: that sum, with no zero in it, rebuilds the ramp of the first 100,000 zeros to within 0.006, including their position under the unitary ramp. By sieve to x=10^9 the true primes hold one variance at every scale, 0.0461, where random primes are 338 times louder and growing, and the Möbius sum holds 0.0289 where random signs give 0.61. The Davenport and Heilbronn function, which has the same symmetry and no product over primes (no Euler product), shows the collapse with nothing moved: below height 2,000 one zero in twelve is off the line, its variance grows by a factor of 526, and its entropy over modes is not conserved. Its two components, the Dirichlet L functions modulo 5, each have a product over primes and each hold the lock: all 4,057 zeros found below that height are on the line, the variance stays at its closed form 0.2032, and the entropy is constant. The Davenport and Heilbronn function is the open system: a mode off the line leaks by its δ, and its entropy collapse is the removal, from the lowest δ up, of layers of modes that each keep their own lock. title: The Riemann Hypothesis as the Avoidance of an Information Entropy Collapse

summary: The scarcity of labeled underwater acoustic data limits the development of data-driven models for marine acoustic monitoring, motivating the use of self-supervised learning to exploit the abundance of unlabeled recordings. However, large-scale data alone does not guarantee effective representation learning, because model performance is strongly influenced by the distribution of the training data. To facilitate such training data, this study introduces a scalable curation pipeline that curates 3,000 hours from 41 years of raw NOAA hydrophone recordings, producing MarineSet, a large-scale and diverse dataset designed for underwater acoustic learning. A baseline model, MarineNet, trained on MarineSet achieves competitive performance on marine mammal call and ship-type classification, highlighting the value of systematic data curation for developing self-supervised learning models in underwater acoustics.
title: MarineSet: Large-Scale Underwater Acoustic Data Curation and evaluation

summary: The central claim is that, when irreversible modifications are introduced before the nature of the phenomenon is sufficiently understood, the intervention itself may destroy conditions necessary for later evaluation. The paper therefore argues that intervention should be assessed not only in terms of immediate safety or behavioral outcomes, but also in terms of what is lost through modification, including observability, re-accessibility, restorability, and the future possibility of comparing competing hypotheses. To structure this problem, the paper develops several principles, including the Observation Before Modification Principle, the Minimum Necessary Intervention Principle, Intervention Symmetry, the Dual Precaution Principle, and the concept of Intervention-Induced Non-Observation Error. Suppression is treated as a form of intervention rather than as explanation. The argument does not presuppose AI consciousness, sentience, or moral status. First, an epistemic reason for preservation may arise independently of ontology when intervention risks destroying evidence concerning poorly understood phenomena. Second, when there is non-trivial evidence that the phenomenon could later prove morally significant, an additional conditional ethical reason for preservation may arise. The paper therefore proposes that, under ontological uncertainty, the first object of protection need not be a particular metaphysical interpretation of AI, but the conditions that allow future evidence, comparison, and revision of judgment.   The author used OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol and other ChatGPT models as research and writing assistants during the development of this manuscript. Their contributions included discussion of conceptual structure, counterargument testing, reorganization of arguments, literature-search assistance, and language revision. The author independently evaluated and revised all substantive claims, interpretations, citations, and final wording, and assumes full responsibility for the manuscript. The identification of GPT-5.6 Sol and the other ChatGPT models in this acknowledgment is intended to preserve a transparent record of the human–AI collaboration involved in the development of this work. summary: When a phone fails and its owner keeps the messaging account running on a second device, the account's history can end up in two archives, each intact and each missing what the other holds. We call this Temporal Communication Fragmentation (TCF), a loss by non-union: no message is deleted, but the platform offers no operation that joins the two halves. WhatsApp's own documentation states that old and new chats cannot be merged. We define TCF by three jointly necessary and sufficient conditions and specify CARTA 1.1, a framework for reconstructing one archive from several. CARTA is an output contract owed to a reader who cannot check the result. Records that cannot be read unambiguously are quarantined with a typed reason, and a report gives each record's provenance, the conflicts and deduplication ambiguities found, and every setting used. We evaluated a reference implementation, CHAMP-Pipeline, on synthetic fragment sets with known ground truth. With its declared date inference it reproduced the ground truth in all 4,500 configurations of a parameter sweep; the invariants and the predicted outcome held in all 5,000 random configurations of two to four fragments; and reconstruction stayed exact at one million messages. A zone-offset advisory, frozen before testing, flagged all 2,800 misdeclared zones in a designed test of overlapping fragment pairs and 1,470 of 1,542 in random configurations, and raised false alarms in 2 of 600 correctly declared runs. A systematic search found 60 chat-merging tools; none fully provides more than 2 of the five output properties CARTA specifies. With a fragment's time zone left undeclared, every benchmarked tool and CHAMP-Pipeline produce the same duplicated and misdated records, and only CHAMP-Pipeline's report says so. All data are synthetic; no real archive has been reconstructed.
title: When Chats Split Apart: Formalizing Temporal Communication Fragmentation and the CARTA Reconstruction Framework
